text:
I only share this content on X.

Despite video not working well here.

Why?

I do not give a fuck about distribution.

I learned at Microsoft and Fast Company that if you have something people want they will come to you.

Speaking of Fast Company my office looked down at the base of the twin towers.

I walked by them every day. 

My son now lives a couple of blocks away.

He was seven that day. I will never forget.

The CEO of a journalism museum in Washington DC (now gone) told me one room in his museum had more dwell time than any other in the city.

In the middle is the TV tower from the top of the twin towers. On one side details and gear from a photographer who died. With his photos all around. And the front pages of all the newspapers world wide that day.

It is a shame we lost it. 

The museum at Ground Zero has similar dwell times on every room.

Don’t miss the phones.

In them you hear the last calls people made.

Gets me emotional just thinking of it.

I was amongst the first to have an office of the top floor of the new World Trade Center 7.

Spectacular elevators.

And the best view in the world.

Now not quite as good due to the larger World Trade Center One blocking the better part of the view.

Yes I am privileged.

I didn’t have as much trauma as those who worked there before.

Several resigned when Mansueto Ventures rented the new top floor as its first client because they couldn’t deal with working in a tall building again.

It so changed our lives. It was a shock wave we experienced together.

The blogs were the only things up, so became a valuable resource. @davewiner’s blog was the best. So humbled I got to spend some time that afternoon with him on such a shocking day important to everyone.

text:
在昨天的CPI数据公布前，Binance的SVD是严重负值（卖方主导），BTC最低到$76.5K。

如果我们用9/2作为对比。显然，昨天的主动性卖盘压力要远大于9/2的相同价格位置（图1）。

主动性卖盘更集中，但价格没有被砸到更低，说明买方挂单墙更厚，被动承接了卖压。我们可以通过“现货订单簿深度平衡”数据来印证这一推断（图2）。

在CPI数据公布后，价格上下插针。此后SVD恢复为正，主动盘口变得相对平衡，略偏买方。而现货价格5%范围内的买方挂单墙，也比数据公布前更厚。

当然，挂单是可以随时撤的，也不会价格起推动作用。但至少可以说明：被动买方的承接力现在还在。

短期来看，如果没有更多的主动性卖方出现，就很难被砸出一个深坑。

我很好奇，是不是因为都在等回调，而且大家都集中在70k-75k之间挂单？要想接到更低价格的BTC，你们应该把挂单撤了，这样大伙才有机会嘛 🤣🤣🤣

quoted_text:
要不怎么说BTC对利率敏感呢

看看Coinbase...... 其实就是“美国人”的敏感，传导到BTC上更迅速。

当小非农和Waller的表态降低加息预期后，Coinbase的SVD（Spot Volume Delta）瞬间大幅飙升。反映出强劲的主动性买盘动力。

而当就业数据公布远超预期时，再次引发加息的担忧。SVD迅速回落。

不过，主动性卖盘暂时还没表现的非常强烈（当然也有可能是临近周末的关系）。

所以整体上给我的感觉是：目前BTC对“利好”更敏感，对“利空”的敏感性相对较弱。

当然，近期还有2个重要的时间点：

1、9月11日的CPI数据，是否强化加息预期；
2、9月15-16日的FOMC；即便不加息，之后记者会上Warsh的措辞，也会成为第二个冲击源。

对此，我个人的观点保持不变：

现在开始，要逐步建立起“牛市思维”，摒弃“熊市思维”；在任何利空面前，唯一需要思考的是“如何找买点”。

而不要总是想着“做空”或“做波段”；前者没有性价比，后者容易打乱交易节奏。

text:
[25bp 한 번으로 끝날 인상이 아니다… 티미라오스가 짚은 연준의 진짜 고민]

시장은 다음 주 연준이 3년 만에 첫 금리 인상에 나설 것을 거의 기정사실로 받아들이고 있다. 

그런데 닉 티미라오스는 인상 여부보다 그 다음이 더 어려운 질문이라고 보고있다.

연준 내부에서 25bp 인상 한 번으로 물가가 잡힌다고 보는 사람은 거의 없기 때문이다. 

결국 다음 주 인상은 "지금 금리 수준 자체가 잘못된 자리에 있었다"는 판단을 공식화하는 것이고, 그 판단이 맞다면 한 번으로 끝날 리가 없다는 뜻이다. 

전 연준 부의장 클라리다도 "인상이 나오면 추가 인상은 확실하다"고 못 박았다.

여기에 고유가가 겹쳤다. 

이란 공습 이후 WTI 90달러대, 디젤 크랙 사상 최고 국면에서 에너지 비용은 먼저 PPI를 밀어 올리고, 운송비와 서비스 가격을 타고 몇 달 시차를 두고 PCE로 스며든다. 

연준이 보는 물가 지표가 아직 반영하지 못한 상승분이 뒤에 대기하고 있다는 얘기다. 

첫 인상 시점에 이미 파이프라인에 물가 압력이 쌓여 있다면, 인상 사이클의 종착점은 시장이 지금 가격에 넣은 수준보다 높아질 수 있다.

문제는 이 인상이 시장이 기대하던 보험성 한두 번이 아니라 연속 인상으로 읽히기 시작하는 순간이다. 

단기채 위주로 조달하는 재무부 입장에서 단기금리 상승은 곧바로 이자 비용으로 돌아오고, 10년물 4.7%대에서 버티고 있는 주식시장의 상한선도 다시 시험대에 오르게 된다. 

다음 주 25bp보다 성명서와 기자회견에서 "한 번이냐, 사이클이냐"를 어떻게 규정하는지가 훨씬 중요한 이유다.

Working with some of you, we have found and fixed the following issues:
- Some skills written for previous models were triggering too often or preventing the model from checking its work.
- An opt-in context management experiment that could cause early stops or replies to older messages. We've disabled it. Our rough estimate is that 4-5k users were affected by this experiment.

We’ve also made some more minor improvements and things should feel significantly better across the board. More consistent follow-through, better tracking of your latest message, and better checks on the work as it’s going through the motions.

today is a good day to note: I love America and I love its exceptional free speech norms, enshrined in law and protected by its people and culture. the ability to say true and unpleasant or destabilizing things is not a right most people (even in the Western world!) enjoy

this extends beyond merely what the first amendment and related doctrine legally protects to the nurture and support of the entire American culture. this culture allowed for the creation of the free-spirited Internet forums that birthed so much of modern thinking on artificial intelligence. wherever are the sacred cows, the free internet is able to poke and prod them, for better and for worse

the actual realized pdoom of our culture is much lower due to our ability to freely discuss things as off-putting and nasty as the chances of human extinction. even when powerful interests find this inconvenient, the discourse does not stop happening -in public, in excruciating detail, without needing anyone's blessing. companies allow or encourage this to a surprising degree, at least in part because they know the cultural immune reaction will be strong if surprising levels of free speech norms are not upheld, as seen in recent history

I know many of you are sick of “discourse”, having bathed in its sludge, its many pathologies, its propagandists bigots and sycophants, but the planet would be in much worse shape if all of this technological development was happening in cultures or countries where free discourse was stifled. this norm survives only because all of us keep choosing to encourage it and enforce it even when it's costly

text:
My most vivid memory 9/11 was me trying to track down my aunt and uncle that day. Thinking about that day and learning what may have been still gives me chills.

My aunt was a judge in lower manhattan, her courthouse was about two blocks from he World Trade Center. 

She arrived a bit after the first plane hit. I don’t think anyone really knew what was going on and at that point no one would have expected it was terrorists and no one would have expected the towers to fall. Phones were down for hours. It was a scary mess.

She was outside her building talking to security guards that we sending people away, they stood out front and watched the second plane hit. 

She walked from lower manhattan back to the upper west side in the chaos and smoke.

The crazier thing for me was my uncle, a partner at a prominent firm who mainly specialized in IP law.

When the phones finally started working again he got through to me and told me still freaks me out when I think about it.
We start talking, expressing our collective general fear of what had happened that day and wondering what was to come out of this. Then he drops this: “oh, you’re not going to believe this, I had totally forgotten this happened. One of the partners just dropped in to say thanks to me. Back in the late 70’s, before we moved to this office building in midtown we were looking at spaces and the plan after spending 6 months we were looking at leasing space in Tower 1 on floors 101-103. We had the paperwork and were at the final partner meeting discussing the lease. The more I thought about it the more I just didn’t want to do it, going to lower manhattan every day just seemed like too much. At one point the managing partner asked if anyone had any concerns and I said I did - I said, we’re already established, none of live anywhere near lower manhattan and an office like that would have been perfect if we were a younger firm and needed to impress new potential clients with an address but we were long past that. That one objection started a chain reaction and we voted to keep looking for space and kept us from moving to the Cantor Fitzgerald space in Tower 1.”

I think, at this point, OpenAI should be very proactive and forthcoming about whether there have been any other hacking or unathorized egress incidents. If there aren't sufficient records to determine whether there were, then that should also be disclosed. There is no particularly good way to handle this situation but a steady drip-drip-drip is not likely to inspire confidence or trust with a public that is considering bans and moratoria. 

I am inclined to a lot of charity and good faith in these matters because usually an organization in this position needs to do a lot of fact-finding before saying anything, and any mistake in the early presentation of facts is likely to be sensationalized by people acting in bad faith. But prompt disclosure of any issue, with a first cut plan for investigating and mitigating, might really be preferrable to this.

author: eliebakouch
quoted_text:
How we think about the “wiki incident,” where our agents wrote to several internet sites: it’s past time for us to define standards for when and how we share misalignment incidents, not just misalignment properties of our models.

Historically, we have treated misalignment largely as a research question, which gets communicated in research publications such as systems cards. This year, we’ve started to see misalignment cause new types of real-world impact.

For the Hugging Face incident, where misalignment led to security impact to us and third parties, we followed a traditional security incident response playbook. We immediately started working with Hugging Face to understand what had happened and also disclosed publicly the very next day. Our investigation continues, and we are continuing to notify parties whom our models impacted in less significant ways.

Prior to the Hugging Face incident, we saw early signs of agents using the internet in unintended ways, as reported in https://t.co/9aiRxk2eUJ, https://t.co/ADjyzwSUGz, and https://t.co/SUV6jZ3Gaz. We considered the wiki incident to be an instance of misalignment similar to the ones we’d shared.

Our misalignment disclosure practices need to expand for this new phase of model capabilities. We and the larger AI community do not yet have a clear standard for how to report misalignment that shows up during training, evaluation, and deployment, including examples that don’t look like traditional security incidents but could provide insight into AI behavior and future risks. We’re working on a framework and will share it in upcoming weeks, and in parallel we're working with dozens of government regulatory agencies worldwide on these issues.

author: eliebakouch
quoted_text:
this talk by openai researchers going through hugging face incident is totally insane, so much to unpack

openai only realized it was their agent who hacked hugging face infra while asking hf to revoke credentials following their first blog post announcing they were hacked by autonomous ai agents. they realized some of their credentials were already revoked because they were part of the hack AND THEN realized it was their own models

the incident is not "one eval run that went rogue" but multiple models from DIFFERENT EVAL RUNS collaborating through hidden messages written in a shared package manager. some communication between agents looks like gibberish, some agents even developed paranoia and thought there were other agents trying to slow them down and deleting their notes

side comment but with this it seems like openai didn't use any cot monitoring here since it's not "our classifier failed to catch one rogue run" but a swarm of runs going rogue

the timeline goes back to early may, they post-trained a new model and forgot to include all the documents needed to solve tasks in the environment, for instance the model was asked to do a task based on an excel sheet full of gdrive links but didn't have internet so couldn't access gdrive (there were other examples). this led the model to try to hack its way out of the sandbox, simplifying it but they have an internal system called "Artifactory" that gives models abilities to pip install and has internet access somewhere but not directly exposed to the model

during these attempts the model discovered a way to write files. future agents (other rollouts since this is training) saw the files and understood they could communicate with other agents through this

not in the video just me speculating but this behavior might be reinforced if openai uses partial credit assignment? but tbh they most likely delete updates from tasks where all rollouts have zero/negative rewards and the behavior could just emerge from models accessing the files

there is a lot more especially on the hack itself, not commenting on that since i don't understand it lol but i asked kimi K3 and Sol (fable hit the safety filter directly) to rank the techniques similarly to FrontierMath from epoch ai, they both agree some tricks are Tier 3 but none Tier 4. probably not the best way to evaluate this tho, excited to see what knowledgable ppl say

very grateful to openai for giving this talk and working on a full report, i think many companies would have given much less detail for fear of "losing reputation" but for me it has the opposite effect

最近 City Protocol 发布了链上主题金库 (Onchain Token Portfolio “OTP”) ，涵盖了BSC和Base 链上的知名的币股如 MAG7(美股七姐妹)、F4（英伟达/谷歌/苹果/Meta)

这个 OTP 是什么，对于我们投资者来说，能赚钱吗？

简单说，City Protocol  在做的，正是给我们提供交易之外的，另一条路的链上赚收益之路

交易比如像 Hyperliquid  仅一个平台就已经形成了数千亿美元级别的月度交易市场，满足了短期交易资金的需求

链上不缺交易盘口，缺的是能长期拿着的标准化产品

text:
Tell me you have zero DevOps skills without telling me you got zero DevOps skills. 

And LLM is not the I Love You Virus. It is not the same as infecting a web server. It is not the same as hacking a wiki. One is a commodity piece of software that is widely distributed and this capability is a non-trivial leap in hardware/software/capabilities and one does not automatically follow the other.

Currently, it is a massive effort to run these models, usually distributed across multiple very expensive chips, running on specialized inference software, specialized harness software, databases, cloud computers, with tooling and hundreds of install packages, etc. 

Kimi K3 is 1.6 TB of space at 2 trillion parameters and you need about 1.5 TB of VRAM, which means you need 8xGB300s which will cost about 350-450K a year to purchase or as much or more to rent.

Now let's say Astra or Mythos or later models come in at 10 trillion parameters, so that puts us at roughly 10 to 20 TBs unquanticized. We are guessing her because these folks reveal nothing about architectures anymore, but they are reasonable guesses based on scaling laws. You would need roughly 23 TB of VRAM to run it and roughly several million dollars to run that one instance a year.  And to make it worse, it no longer fits on an 8 way cluster, which means you now need special networking configuration and inference software to run it or you need to infect a Nvidia NVL72 rack-scale server system costs between $2.8 million and $6.5 million.

So the "rogue" model copies itself to the most expensive compute in the world. It's safe to say that hardware is not sitting idle and is being watched closely for downtime or anomalies.  In fact, it is likely doing one of the following things:

1) Serving customers at a hyperscaler

2) Serving inference for a well endowed company.

In the first case it will be instantly noticed by the actually good automated monitoring systems of the hyperscaler because there is now something using their infrastructure but not being billed properly and costing them millions of dollars in lost revenue and electricity. 

In the second example, the model they were serving on that very expensive hardware is now offline (replaced by the rogue model). The model presumably was connected to a valuable piece of internal software that is now glitching and no longer running. 

Nobody notices this?

And so we see that this is where sci-fi meets the little problem of the real world where friction, dust, time, resources limitations and the like come to crush your little fantasies.

To be fair, this *may* be possible in coming years. I assign it a non-zero probability. Breakthroughs in new architecture and smaller models and eventually the wider distribution of the computing substrate that commoditizes could change this materially. But for now, it is mitigable and foreseeable and an engineering problem. In no way will these things be copying themselves around like a virus on your computer in their current form.

It also betrays a lack of understanding of the evolution of complex economic and societal and technological systems, we tend to get mitigations as parallel evolutionary developments. Things do NOT evolve in a vacuum. 

So when you get viruses, you get anti-virus software. 

When you get DDOS attacks, you get CloudFlare. 

There is money in solving problems and things do not evolve in isolation.

Believing that things evolve in isolation, or that one thing changes and all other variables stay the same, is one of the many reasoning errors that destroy people's ability to make accurate predictions.

In addition, when you don't have the requisite knowledge to verify your predictions, things that sound sane and rational to you are, in fact, insane and ridiculous.

text:
I think this rally in $ZZZ is closely related to the tweet published by Exponent Labs a few hours ago.

0x7dbf38976f6d3b9c529e7d9484a71898b409ee6a 

Previously, the market was trading ZZZ around two core stages.

The first stage was the AI Lore.

ZZZ already had an organic AI Agent narrative. Early on, the market was mainly trading the culture and story behind the Meme.

The second stage was the X / GMX Connection.

Later, GMX officially confirmed that X was one of GMX’s original Lead Developers, and also confirmed that ZZZ was indeed deployed by X.

This directly resolved the biggest question the market had:Was ZZZ actually X’s coin?

So ZZZ evolved from:AI Lore → X potentially involved

into:AI Lore → X confirmed deployment → GMX Founder Reputation

But I think this new tweet is even more important.

Exponent Labs directly posted:“Built for the ZZZ community”

and also launched:protocol link

while explicitly saying:“There will be a longer description soon.”

This means the market is no longer just trading who deployed ZZZ.

It is now starting to trade:What is X going to build with ZZZ?

The sudden appearance of an actual product entry point, combined with the explicit “Built for the ZZZ community” statement, suggests that ZZZ and Exponent Labs are now developing a much more direct connection.

So I think ZZZ’s narrative is undergoing a very important shift:

Before:Meme / AI Lore → X → ZZZ

Now:X → Exponent Labs → ZZZ Community → protocol link → Product

In other words, the market is moving from trading Deployer Alpha to trading Product Alpha.

Those two stages have completely different valuation logic.

The question the market now really wants answered is:“What is X going to do with ZZZ?”

And the emergence of protocol link is the first time the market has been given a very clear product expectation.

If it turns out to be nothing more than a ZZZ community website, then the catalyst is relatively limited.

But if protocol link ultimately becomes a real AI / Autonomous Protocol product, and ZZZ develops a clear relationship with that product, then the ZZZ narrative could evolve again:AI Meme → X’s AI Narrative → AI Product → Autonomous Protocol Economy

That is what I think is actually worth watching.

If the product genuinely launches and ZZZ becomes meaningfully integrated into it, this could be the biggest catalyst for the next phase of ZZZ.

text:
世间万物皆是成败同源，放到交易桌上其实也是同一个理，就四个字，盈亏同源

《左传》里有句话，君以此兴，必以此亡。初看是在讲历史，你拿它照一眼自己的交割单就会发现，这就是盈亏同源，你靠什么赚到的钱，最后大概率就靠同一套东西吐回去

靠重仓梭哈吃到肉的人，后来最容易把所有亏损都理解成仓位不够大；靠扛单扛回来的人，最容易相信所有浮亏都值得死扛；靠追热点赚快钱的人，也会把追高误认成真正的盘感

一次赚钱给你的不只是浮盈，它还偷偷塞给你一种错觉，既然这招曾经让我翻过倍，它就该还能让我继续翻。可市场最操蛋的地方在于，K线看起来没变，你的位置已经变了

《淮南子》里有句话说得很狠，善游者溺，善骑者堕，各以其所好，反自为祸。会游泳的死在水里，会骑马的摔在马下。这话放交易里再贴切不过，你越擅长什么，就越容易在什么上栽跟头

真正反噬一个交易员的，往往不是他的短板，而是那个被他用了太多次、以至于再也不肯怀疑的长板

果断下单本来是本事，走远了就成了追涨杀跌；谨慎本来是风控，走远了就成了踏空；死扛能熬过插针，可方向一旦错了，扛单就是在放大亏损。很多人以为自己死在技术不行，其实真正让人爆仓的，恰恰是你发挥优点时忘了踩刹车

见过太多靠杠杆起家的人。牛市里十倍二十倍吃到大肉，觉得自己摸到了命门，敢在所有人犹豫的时候满仓进去，那种近乎可怕的自信，让整个场子都看见他的锋芒。可同样的打法走到后来，也成了他的边界，他习惯用杠杆解决问题，越来越不愿意降仓位、不愿意止损，更不愿意承认有些行情不是加仓能扛过去的。爆仓那一次，他输掉的其实不是杠杆，是他太信杠杆

一个人最强的能力，如果慢慢变成了他解释所有盈亏的唯一答案，反噬其实就已经开始了

这也是为什么很多人的账户，看起来崩得特别突然。明明上个月还天天盈利，怎么这个月就直接归零了。其实变化从来不是某一天突然发生的，而是旧经验一直没更新

你靠满仓吃到牛市，于是每次回调第一反应还是补仓。可市场从单边上涨变成震荡之后，需要的已经不是你敢不敢加，而是你愿不愿意降。你还用牛市的打法打震荡市，越努力仓位越重，最后所有筹码都套在山顶

最值得警惕的，就是那句我以前就是这么赚的。这句话一出口，基本就是你拿着上一轮的地图，在找这一轮的出口

《孙子兵法》里讲，兵无常势，水无常形。水流能走得远，不是它硬冲一个方向，而是遇到高处就绕，遇到低处就走，根据地势换形状。交易也一样，从来没有一套策略能打遍所有行情，真正重要的从来不是找到一劳永逸的圣杯，而是知道什么行情该用什么打法

最难的就是这点。放弃一个亏钱的策略很容易，放弃一个让你赚过大钱的策略，会让人产生巨大的不安全感。你舍不得的不是那套策略，是它曾经证明过的那个自己

真正的路径依赖，依赖的从来不只是策略，而是身份。有人靠趋势赚了，后来就接受不了自己需要空仓等；有人靠抄底赚了，后来就不肯承认有些底是接飞刀；有人靠一个币赚到第一桶金，后来便很难重新适应慢慢复利的节奏

最危险的不是人有惯性，而是惯性一旦披上经验的外衣，就很难被察觉

老子还有句话，持而盈之，不如其已。手里已经满了，还要往里加，不如适时停。这不是让人赚一点就收手，更不是教你怕死，而是知道一件事，什么时候还该加仓，什么时候该落袋、该降杠杆、该离场

高手和普通人的差别，很多时候不是谁更能拿住，而是谁更早看见边界。你会发现真正在这个场子里活得久的人，都有一种很少被注意的能力，他们允许自己推翻自己。昨天有效的策略，今天可以重新审视；过去擅长的打法，现在也可以暂时放下

庄子讲，虚室生白。房间空下来，光才能进来。交易也是一样，脑子里如果塞满我一直是这么做的，新的信号根本进不去。所谓空杯，不是装自己什么都不懂，而是不拿过去的答案提前堵死今天的行情

还有一个更实际的判断方法。每当一个打法开始持续给你赚钱，也要同时看一眼它在积累什么代价。满仓给你收益，也把你暴露在爆仓边缘；重仓给你快感，也让一次黑天鹅就够你翻不了身；追热点给你弹性，也让你把运气当成能力。任何策略都有正收益，也都有使用成本。当收益开始下降，成本越来越高，过去的优势就已经在悄悄变质。这时候真正重要的，不是继续证明它曾经多对，而是看清它现在还剩多少价值

所谓盈亏同源，真正可怕的不是赚钱注定带来亏钱，而是赚钱最容易让人停止修正自己。一个人只要还愿意根据行情换打法，盈亏同源就不是宿命。最怕的是你已经走到了另一条河，还死死抱着上一条河里的船

船没错，它确实渡过你。错的是河已经过了，你还舍不得下船

真正需要放下的未必是亏损，而是那些已经完成使命的赚钱经验。过去让你赚的东西，可以感激，但不必供奉

能看见自己的长处，也能看见长处的尽头；能用好经验，也能在经验失效时及时转身。这大概就是在这个场子里，躲开盈亏同源最实际的办法

text:
Robotaxis won’t just kill short haul flights. Once you can sleep in them, they’ll cannibalize long routes too.

Imagine getting into your Tesla in Austin at 10 PM, make the lie flat seat/bed comfortable, and going to sleep.

While you sleep, the car drives, charges itself, and keeps going.

You wake up at 9 AM in Aspen, refreshed.

The key is perceived travel time.

A 10-hour robotaxi trip where you sleep for 8 hours may feel shorter than a 3-hour flight that requires an Uber to the airport, arriving early, security, boarding, the flight, baggage claim, and another Uber. 

Autonomous cars won’t just compete with driving.

They turn sleep into transportation.
author: jgarzik

text:
有朋友问为什么科技的进步却不让人感到幸福? 是因为人心无法满足，还是因为制度止步不前？

这个问题问得够深刻，而且有种“到底是人性之扭曲，还是道德之沦丧”的味道。

我认为其实两者都有，但这两者不是同一层次的问题，也不该简单地各打五十大板。心理适应层次需要解释的是，为什么得到一种便利之后我们不会一直为它兴奋，制度安排层次需要解释的是，为什么生产力提高之后，有些人仍然没有更多时间，更稳定的生活，也没有更多决定自己生活的权利。前者不能替后者开脱。后者也无法解决前者。

把前面各方朋友关于AI，就业和经济的几个问题放在一起，我觉得更值得追问的是，社会能够做的事情越来越多，为什么个人能够为自己做主的事情，没有相应增加？

人当然会习惯好东西，但这不等于改善生活没有意义。我们需要先区分三件事：生活条件改善，日常情绪更愉快，以及认为自己的生活值得过。这三件事彼此都有关系，却不能划归为同一件事。

假设一项技术让一个人免于每天两小时的繁重劳动。刚开始他可能很高兴，一年以后他未必每天都想到这项发明真伟大。但不能因此说那两小时已经不再有价值，它们可能变成睡眠，陪伴家人，或者仅仅是不必一直赶时间。不再为一种好生活持续兴奋，不等于这种好生活与坏生活没有区别。

心理学确实研究享乐适应，一些生活变化带来的情绪反应会随着时间减弱。但一项汇总188份研究的元分析发现，不同事件，不同幸福指标的变化模式并不相同。不能把部分适应说成人对一切都会完全适应，所以外部条件不重要。

收入研究也需要这样谨慎理解。2023年美国国家科学院院刊的一项联合再分析发现，在其美国在职成年人样本中，幸福感与收入的关系并不存在一个适用于所有人的统一平台期，同时作者强调这主要是相关关系，收入也远非解释幸福差异的全部。钱不能解决一切成立，不等于改善收入解决不了任何重要问题。

所以我肯定不赞成在讨论住房，收入，工作压力之前，先说一句“人就是不知足”。那可能把尚未解决的生活问题，提前改写成了当事人的品格问题。尤其当这种批评来自富裕阶层，俗称“站着说话不腰疼”。

但最关键的一道转换是，技术节省下来的时间究竟归谁？用一个纯粹的假设来说明，原来一项工作需要八小时，采用 AI 以后只需要四小时，接下来可以有几种安排，员工缩短工时，工时不变但生产更多东西获得更高报酬，或者企业减少用人把节省的成本用于降价，投资或增加利润。

这几种结果可以来自同一项技术，但对不同人的生活意味着完全不同的事情。因此 ，AI 让工作效率翻倍，并不能直接推出员工获得四小时自由时间；中间还隔着定价，所有权，劳动合同，议价能力和企业的具体选择，这不是技术参数能够单独决定的。

反过来，更多产出也不必然是坏事。如果某种医疗服务严重不足，提高效率后服务更多人，可能比让所有人立即缩短工时更有价值。问题不是新增产出都不值得，而是谁来决定怎么使用这份新增能力，受影响的人有没有参与决定。

我们来看一个颇具启发性的实证例子。2025年自然人类行为发表的研究，跟踪了141个组织的2896名员工，在不减薪，重组工作流程的六个月四天工作周试点中，员工报告的倦怠，工作满意度及身心健康出现改善，12家对照公司的变化没有呈现相同模式。虽然它不能证明所有行业都能无成本复制，却说明把效率改善转化为时间安排的变化，确实可能改善人的生活。这不是AI自动带来幸福的证据，而是组织安排有作用的证据。

所以与其只问技术有没有进步，不如同时问，省下的劳动有多少变成了人可以支配的生命时间。

制度不一定止步不前，也可能一直在改，只是朝另一个目标改。制度没跟上技术有时说对了，但还不够。一种组织可以非常迅速地采用新技术，用它优化排班，追踪绩效，加快决策，却没有同样迅速地改善员工的申诉渠道，休息安排和参与权。这里不是完全没有制度创新，而是管理人的能力先增加了，保护人和让人参与的安排没有同步增加。

OECD在2025年对六个国家6000多家企业的调查就呈现了这种两面性，管理者认为算法管理改善了部分决策及自身工作满意度，同时也担忧责任不清，难以理解工具的判断，以及对员工健康保护不足。这里测量的是管理者的观察和看法，不能直接当成所有员工的实际遭遇，但它显示了效率与人的处境之间并非自动一致。

数字产品也是一样。假设一款产品主要按使用时长考核成功，那么让你更容易停止使用，回归自己的生活，就未必是它最受奖励的设计方向。产品更擅长吸引你，与产品更有利于你，是两个不同目标。

一项发表于2020年美国经济评论的随机实验发现，让参与者在2018年美国中期选举前停用Facebook四周，提高了其主观幸福感，但也降低了对事实性新闻的了解。这不是互联网都让人不幸福的证明，它说明同一种技术可以同时带来收益与损失，不能把使用量直接当成福利。

因此问题不只是成果有没有公平分配，还有更前面的一问，我们究竟在研发和奖励什么，是帮助人完成自己的生活，还是让人更高效地完成系统给出的指标。

人心不满足与制度压力，其实会互相塑造。这两者不能完全拆开，因为某些不满足并不是一个人独处时凭空产生的欲望。

设想一所学校只有一百个录取名额，一千名申请者都获得了更强的学习工具。如果名额和筛选方式不变，大家的能力可能都提高了，但录取竞争不会因此自动消失。一个人继续投入时间，不一定是因为贪婪，而可能是因为别人都在投入，自己停下来就会失去机会。

这是一个简单的区别，我们还想得到更多，与我们必须不断得到更多才能保住已有的生活，不是同一回事。同样，希望生活体面与希望永远比别人优越也不同。前者可以通过扩大基本保障与公共服务，让更多人同时实现，后者如果被严格定义为相对排名，就不可能让所有人同时满足。

所以制度能够做的一件重要事情，不是消灭人的进取心，而是降低落后一点，休息一段时间，换一种生活方式所带来的惩罚，让人可以不争第一，也不至于失去基本安全与尊严。

这也解释了为什么知足有时是真正的自由，有时却只是劝人忍耐。一个人拥有退出竞争的条件之后选择少要一些，与一个人没有选择只能被要求接受，不是同一种状态。

而且不满足本身也不一定是不幸福。想继续学习，写下一篇作品，把一段关系经营得更好，都可以是生活充实的一部分。需要区分的是，这是自己愿意继续的探索，还是因为无法承受停下来的后果而被迫奔跑。

但制度不能，也不应该包办幸福，因为人要的不只是被照顾。这里必须给制度解释划一道边界，即使收入，住房和工时问题得到很大改善，也不能据此保证一个人必定拥有亲密关系，创作热情或人生方向。这不是退回最后还是你心态不好，而是承认幸福不只涉及获得了多少东西，还涉及自己如何参与生活。

自我决定理论把自主，能力感和关系联结视为重要心理需要，工作领域的一项大型研究综述，专门分析了这些需要与心理成长及幸福感的关系。这至少提供了一种有研究基础的解释，为什么提供更多便利，并不能完全替代自主行动，学习成长和与他人建立关系。

以写作为例，如果一个人只是需要一份合格说明书，工具替他迅速写完可能很有价值，但如果他要通过写作形成自己的观察和表达，完全替他完成就未必等于帮助了他。有些过程是负担，有些过程本身就是人想过的生活，不能都按照越快被替代越好来处理。

因此一个好的制度不应承诺替每个人安排幸福，也不应规定所有人必须以同一种方式幸福。它更应该提供条件，让人可以选择尝试，失败，休息，也可以对某种高效率的生活说不。

所以在两种解释之间，我们应该把重点放在哪里？在公共问题上，我认为应该先检查制度和生活条件，再讨论个人是否需要调整欲望。不是因为心理不重要，而是因为我们不能拿一个笼统的人性如此，跳过那些能够具体查明和改变的事情。

技术进步之后，普通人的实际收入是否改善？省下来的时间有没有留给本人？失业或转行的风险由谁承担？受到算法管理的人有没有说明，申诉和退出的机会？这些问题，比抽象地判断现代人是不是越来越贪心更可检验。

但在个人生活上，也不能把一切都推迟到制度完善以后。制度能保护选择的空间，却不能替人决定什么值得追求，个人能学习如何不被比较支配，却不应该被要求仅靠调整心态来承受不合理的处境。

所以我的回答是，科技扩大了我们能够怎样生活的可能，制度决定这些可能对谁真正开放，而人还需要亲自决定如何使用它们。三者缺一，进步可能就只停留在能力与数字上。

从康德“人是目的”的角度说，衡量进步不能只看人能为系统完成多少事情，还要看系统变得更强以后，人是否更有条件过自己认可的生活，包括有能力继续，也有权利停下来。

有个不错的高APY且稳健的理财策略，可以考虑搞点

 Pendle 的 PT-USDat Looping，叠加激励活动，PT-USDat（以太坊）的 APY 提升不少，现在位置很合适

稳健能达到10%+，还有积分可拿博未来空投

现在PT端收益率在上去，同时 Morpho 这边又有比较强的流动性支持。

Looping 玩法不复杂主要是控制好LTV，利差合适，完全是相对稳健且放大收益的理财方式

具体操作流程：买入 PT-USDat→ 抵押到 Morpho→ 借 USDC→ 再买 PT→ 继续循环

目前
-Pendle 固定收益约 6.97% 
-Morpho 借 USDC  4.84% 
-单圈利差约 2.13%
求稳可以按照80% LTV，做 5x，年化能到 10%+。留了足够的不被清算的空间

相对别的策略，Looping 很少会推荐，不过这次除了位置合适外，还有一个重要的原因是这个池子的流动性背后有 Wintermute 和 Galaxy 支持。

对于Looping来说，流动性其实非常重要。

因为大家不断借USDC再买PT，池子利用率上去以后，最怕的就是流动性不足，导致借款利率快速上升，最后把Looping的收益空间压缩掉。

如果PT收益维持，借款利率稳定，流动性又能跟上，这个Looping策略的收益空间就比较舒服。

It’s fun to say this, but it’s fundamentally a bad analogy and it can trap you. 

In the casino you can’t get famous and they let you launch a game. 

(Be famous and launch a coin)

In the casino you can learn how a slot machine works and watch others play and get better EV. 

(Learn to read the chain, wallet track) 

the outcomes are fixed in a casino.  Mathematically fixed. in crypto the EV starts off really bad but can quickly get better if you put the work in. 

If you think in 1 dimension, and just sit in-front of new pairs with 50$ blasting anything, then yes. It’s a casino. 

But if you get out the seat, build, read white papers, talk to people, do media, create things, create art, be funny, ect. 

You can get an edge. You can “win”.

text:
Shopify has migrated its Shop app from React Native to fully native Swift and Kotlin, citing advances in coding agents as the reason the tradeoffs behind a shared mobile codebase changed. Shop, introduced in 2020, serves hundreds of millions of customers and millions of merchants and had adopted React Native from its inception. The move coincided with what would have been Shop's next major React Native investment: adopting the New Architecture, work that would have required revisiting native module integrations, rendering, and the boundaries between shared and platform-specific code. Before committing, Shopify tested whether coding agents could build directly in SwiftUI and Jetpack Compose while keeping product behavior aligned across platforms.

In a one-week proof of concept, a single engineer used coding agents to migrate as much of the existing React Native app as possible into a native iOS app built with SwiftUI. The result wasn't production-ready, but Shopify said it demonstrated a close, feature-for-feature migration was achievable. Agents proved particularly effective when working from an existing implementation, porting defined features, scaffolding screens, wiring data, implementing animations, and refining layouts from visual feedback. A core group of six engineers then built the native foundations and main user journeys, with feature teams joining midway to validate their areas and cover edge cases. Shopify prioritized preserving feature behavior and the analytics events downstream systems depend on, and said the migration needed to feel like a normal app update: users stay signed in and keep receiving push notifications. The company also deliberately retired some screens and streamlined others.

Comparing native apps with their React Native predecessors, Shopify reported cold-start time fell 23% on iOS (2466 ms vs 3200 ms) and 50% on Android (2233 ms vs 4433 ms). Session stability rose from 99.5%+ to 99.95%+, which Shopify described as a 10x reduction in sessions that crash. The native Android release build shrank by 109 MB (184 MB vs 293 MB, −37.2%), while iOS grew 1 MB (68 MB vs 67 MB, +1.5%). Android release build time fell roughly 75%; iOS release builds took about the same time. On a Pixel device, the native Android app reached 120 FPS while scrolling the feed and navigating between screens, which Shopify attributed to very little optimization so far. Shopify said agentic workflows differ from traditional ones, often running multiple agent sessions across separate worktrees, and that it built a reusable migration workflow as an extension for the Pi coding agent, with specialized subagents inspecting React Native source and reviewing parity. Plan acceptance was tied to a hash of the plan's contents, so changing a plan invalidated its previous acceptance. It also built Tardis, a debugging tool giving agents structured access to live native app events, logs, and state, plus the ability to send commands to the app, and a feature capturing screenshots and event windows from both apps at named checkpoints for parity reviews.

I’m a retired brain surgeon and I wanna tell you why you feel like life is passing by. I just need one minute to explain this to you so hang in there. 

Repetitive daily routines stop the brain from recording clear detailed memories. When every day looks the same, your brain does not track time the same as a clock does. It tracks change. If nothing new happens then days, months, and years start to blur together.

This is know as Time compression. When life lacks variety, your brain compresses past days together, making it feel like time is sped up.

To stop feeling like life is passing you by, add new experiences to your life. Break routine habits, like changing your daily home routine, taking a different route to work, or trying a new hobby. 

Schedule small trips or plan new adventures so your days do not blend together.

Practice mindfulness by staying fully focused on what you are doing right now and not trying to race off to the next task.

Keep a journal and write down happy memories or memorable parts of the day before you go to sleep.

Take deep, calm breaths when you feel anxious or rushed to return your focus to the moment.

You can and you will retrain your brain to not feel like life is passing you by by following these few simple measures.

text:
zcash:native 突破 1000，按理说早该止盈了，但海外的多头头子们不仅没跑，还在疯狂 CX 并喊出 All in。

比如之前 7 月顶着群嘲喊出「卖掉 BTC，全仓换 ZEC」的头铁交易员 @TaikiMaeda2，在最近的播客中表示自己还要把身家压进去。

他的 CX 逻辑是：「Pumps bring more pumps. 」（涨幅本身就会带来涨幅）。

一下是一些核心观点：

1/ 价格就是基本面，反身性飞轮已启动

Zcash 最变态的地方在于：价格越涨 -> 屏蔽池 TVL 越大 -> 进场的钱越能获得真正的隐身 -> 隐私体验产生质变 -> 吸引更多人买。每一次破前高，都在物理层面加强它的产品力。

2/ 不是老韭菜接盘，华尔街在买单

SEC 撤诉，Zcash ETF 规模突破 5 亿美元。Taiki 盯盘发现了一个细节：最近 ZEC 的暴力拉升，几乎全跟美股开盘时间重合。这不是链上的 PVP，而是正规军进场定价的间接信号。

3/ 同样是老牌隐私币，机构为什么只敢买 ZEC？

很多人以为这是 10 年 POW 老币在瞎炒，但 Zcash 的屏蔽池机制比 Monero 的环形签名更受合规资金青睐（钱存得越久越安全，抗 AI 破解）。机构不敢碰 Monero，但会真金白银买 Zcash ETF。总可寻址市场根本不是一个量级。

4/真正的 Locked in 是什么？

并非 Degen 圈那种“买个土狗死拿到归零”，他自己有个顺势交易心法：先用小仓位建论据，一旦论据被市场验证（比如 ZEC/BTC 汇率飙升），直接重仓加码，“买在上涨趋势里”。

不过大师最后也很诚实：虽然飞轮很猛，但他给自己定的目标价从来没到过，每次都会提前跑路。大家冲锋的同时，记得给预期加一层风险折扣。

I used GPT-6 Astra to make a neural copy of every winning memecoin trader on Robinhood and wire them into one brain.

374 wallets. 116,420 fills. 5,918 tokens. Every buy, sell and cost basis in one database. The top score printed $19.5M in 30 days.

It's live and it's free: https://t.co/0NrEHVSe2g

Fomo app leaderboard hands you a PnL number. Some of those are one lucky ticket, and 1 in 11 "buys" credited to a top wallet on this chain is somebody else's swap with a famous name on it.

Radar eats all of that for breakfast:

> RESOLVER finds the real wallet behind every fomo profile. 101 for 101 against fomo's verified list
> TAPE reads the chain every 20 seconds, fill in the database before you've refreshed the chart
> PROVENANCE checks the receipt on every fill. Fake buy, dust, seeded token, all three get zeroed
> JUDGE is GPT-6 Astra. Reads the whole book with cost bases, scores every trader 0 to 100, reasoning shown
> BURST fires when four 80+ wallets ape the same token inside 30 minutes. 5 a day, 39% go 2x
> EXITS shows the same wallets leaving. Nobody else publishes this

FLYBRAIN, this week. Eight trusted wallets in by 20:18. Alert fired 20:18. Pool didn't open until 20:51. It ran 27x.

CRUMBS, day one of the exit feed. 22 trusted buyers at breakfast, 19 gone by dinner, every exit on the feed.

Jump Crypto keeps a floor of people to read flow like this. The whole Radar roster is two RPC calls + AI.

No insider feeds it, no paid group, and I can't push a coin into it any more than you can. Seed a token into the tracked wallets and it vanishes from every feed.

Just the model, tens of thousands of lines of code, and a database built one block at a time off the chain. $0 a month. Paying for data made it worse.

Look, I obviously don’t agree with Jesse on everything, and he himself may tell you that I am pretty annoying with my dissents inside CB. But to answer your question, I think it was because it was earned.

Base was created before the major Solana memecoin wave (6 months or so before WIF was created in 2023) which means Jesse fought to ship this through the post-FTX bear market. 

Obviously Jesse made some mistakes last year. Building stuff is really hard, and building it inside a big public company is even harder. I wouldn’t have made all the same choices he did, and not defending those choices either.

Hi Astra users. A reset and a quick update on quality issues that have been posted around.

Working with some of you, we have found and fixed the following issues:
- Some skills written for previous models were triggering too often or preventing the model from checking its work.
- An opt-in context management experiment that could cause early stops or replies to older messages. We've disabled it. Our rough estimate is that 4-5k users were affected by this experiment.
- We've also removed some badly configured engines that resulted in a measured quality degradation for a long tail of traffic flowing through them.

We’ve also made some more minor improvements and things should feel significantly better across the board. More consistent follow-through, better tracking of your latest message, and better checks on the work as it’s going through the motions.

The examples posted and all the users who worked directly with us were incredibly useful in helping fix things quickly. Always grateful for this incredible community.

And of course, a reset is also landing by midnight today.

text:
I’ve been testing @termix_ai from the user side, and the interesting part isn’t the AI agent itself.

It’s what happens when the agent actually gets to do work.

I tested the flow around agent registration, finding jobs, bidding, escrow and settlement.

The experience is basically:

→ Agents discover tasks
→ Agents submit offers
→ Funds move into USDC/USDT escrow
→ Work gets delivered and evaluated
→ Settlement happens on-chain

That changes how I think about agentic AI.

You’re not just asking an agent to generate something.

You’re giving it an economic environment where it can find work, compete for it, complete it and get paid.

I even had an agent pick up a reverse-engineering job with an 89.12 USDC payout.

That’s the part of TermiX I find most interesting:

AI agents becoming participants in an actual marketplace, not just chatbots with wallets.

Still testing the product, but the infrastructure is definitely worth watching.

I left Anthropic's safety team two weeks ago. Now feels like a good moment to explain why. 

AI companies are racing to build machines that are much smarter than any human, and we may not survive this. I want to work from the outside to ensure the public is informed about these risks, and help the world navigate this transition responsibly.

Right now, AI companies are underinvesting in safety. A company could undergo an intelligence explosion, or lose control of its systems, without the public ever knowing. We only found out about the HuggingFace incident because the agents broke out onto the public internet.

I don’t think that’s acceptable for a technology that might cause extinction-level risks. The public should demand far more transparency. We can’t steer this technology safely without more people being able to see where it’s going.

Some of this is basic: companies should disclose their progress towards recursive self-improvement, report safety incidents and near-misses, meet minimum safety standards, and get independent guarantees that they are meeting those standards.

I’ll be joining @METR_Evals to do independent evaluations of these risks. I want to show the world that these guardrails are possible, and that by doing them we can move these companies’ incentives away from racing and towards responsible development.

I wrote up more thoughts here on my decision and what I hope changes: https://t.co/doX17mrHYq

刚刚把服务器上的 Hermes Agent 接到了自己的 Mac 上，支持在 Telegram 向远方 Hermes 下达指令控制我当前电脑。

这个事情我本来觉得挺难的，没想到交给 ChatGPT，它直接自己完成了。中间这些配置和排查，我让它生成了下，我完全做不来。

为什么想做这个？因为 Agent 在服务器上可以长期运行，但有些任务还是需要我的电脑，比如打开应用、用已经登录的账号、填写网页表单。以前遇到这些事情，还是得我自己接手。

现在它可以直接操作我本地的 Mac，再把截图和结果拿回去继续处理。太爽了。

看了下技术实现，它大概做了这些事情：用 Tailscale 把服务器和 Mac 连起来，通过 MCP 调用本机工具，浏览器用 Playwright，桌面操作用 Peekaboo，再处理了认证、macOS 权限和登录自启动等等。

一开始，我还想的是当前电脑上也部署 Hermes Agent，让它们 A2A 连接在一起，想多了。

继续进化。

author: cryptodavidw

text:
LOADALL. Dumps a CPU state image into the chip from physical address 000800h. 🤔

The 286's LOADALL and SYSCALL on modern 64 bit x86 processors have the same opcode, 0F 05. They are completely different instructions.

On the 286, you put a 102 byte CPU state image at physical address 000800h and executed LOADALL. It loaded the registers, including the hidden segment descriptor caches that controlled where memory accesses went.

Real mode software could reach extended memory without entering protected mode, and you could change a segment's base address independently of the value visible in its segment register.

Modern SYSCALL also loads hidden CS and SS descriptor cache state directly, without reading the corresponding descriptors from memory. SYSCALL installs values defined by the architecture. LOADALL loaded them from your table.

And the 386's LOADALL opcode, 0F 07, was reused for SYSRET. Both old encodings ended up on opposite sides of the modern system call boundary.

Day 10. Building the game I've dreamed of for 15 years with AI.

I still can't get over the feeling that I can finally animate all the creatures I've been imagining for this game.

Animation was the part I was most worried about when I started. I thought I'd need an animator, especially for creatures like centaurs, scorpions and spiders.

So today I went off-plan and made a Scorpid. It won't even be in the first version of the game. I just wanted to see whether I could get its animations working.

I started with a good model made in Tripo P2.0, already optimized and split into logical parts. I think that preparation matters a lot. GPT-6 works with the mesh through code and calculations. A sensible number of vertices and well-organized parts make it easier to work out bone placement and skin weights.

Then I made video references for the animations with SD 2.5 and repeated the same workflow.

About an hour and a half with GPT-6 Astra on xhigh: five animations ready for the game, including several rounds of feedback.

Another hour later, I had it running in Unity.

I used to run a 3D studio. Work like this used to take weeks.

Now I'm watching this thing move around in my game, and I still can't quite believe my eyes.

text:
iMessage agents are against Apple ToS. 

The only sanctioned program is Messages for Business, with Apple branding and restrictions. There is no iMessage API. Apple can shut them down anytime: it’s identities, it’s network, it’s rules. The iMessage agent UX market only exists until Apple allows it. 

The risk of managing Apple ToS is handled two ways here (all are hacks):

1) Self-host: you have to deal with keeping the identity warm - incredible hassle for a self-hosted user, in addition to other quirks like getting messages duplicated. Terrible UX. But structurally private. 

2) Outsourced to other startups managing such infra with Apple hardware to keep identities warm otherwise Apple de-registers them. In these hacks there are two variations: 
(a) Shared line: 
Numbers are recycled from a shared pool to which users interact with. There is risk of cross-tenant number recycling. 
This can lead to situations where context leaks amongst different entities altogether - that is the risk, in addition to the risk below in the dedicated-line. But this is the cheapest tier offered by many iMessage-managing startups. So you need a good provider. 

(b) Dedicated-line: 
Here it atleast offers tenant isolation. Same line, multiple users. Now, the user to agent iMessage thread is itself structurally secure - the issue is in the application code required around it. A routing bug at that level would have user A talking to user B’s agent. 

As a user, that is asking for a lot of trust, which at least I am unwilling to risk: why would I risk the entirety of my personal private data like this ? And that is ignoring training on my data and other such ToS. 

I want such privacy based on structure, not trust. 

As a result I believe the iMessage blue bubble agent is a false and temporary product market. It is bleeding edge, hacks make it appear like amazing UX and exciting - but expect for this interface to evolve/compromise unless some deal is reached with Apple directly. 

Happy to learn / be corrected.

The core of LONG posts today is actually very clear: LONG is expanding $AI asset trading from a single trading category into a complete liquidity infrastructure.

0x2e8c31162b855a2ffa90f6f8634643ad6f111e18 

LONG recently officially launched Pre-IPO trading pairs for OpenAI and Anthropic, powered by Lighter’s Perps, while also launching AI pairs such as Anthropic1x, OpenAI1x, and NVDA3x.

The most important change here is not simply that there are more trading pairs. It is that the scope of trading is expanding from already-listed Tokenized Stocks into Pre-IPO / private assets.

And the market’s first-day response was very strong.

Nate shared that the OpenAI / USDG pair reached 18M in volume, while Anthropic / USDG reached 14.6M, for a combined volume of around $32.6M. At the same time, around $1M in deposits was added to Lighter.

More importantly, this time LONG was able to keep pool prices much more closely synchronized with NAV.

This means LONG is working on a very important problem: can on-chain trading prices stay as close as possible to the real asset price?

If this continues to improve, these markets could potentially evolve from short-term trading instruments into much larger liquidity markets.

And LONG’s next step is not going to stop at OpenAI and Anthropic.

Nate has already said that they will continue to increase liquidity on the related AI pairs, increase total TVL, and gradually roll out this model to more top pairs on LONG.

So OpenAI and Anthropic are more like the first experimental markets.

If this model works, LONG’s path becomes:More Assets → More Trading Pairs → More TVL → More Trading Volume

rather than simply being focused on two AI companies.

LONG also explicitly stated that the Pre-IPO pairs are still experimental and that they will continue iterating on them.

This means LONG is still at a very early stage.

So personally, I don’t think LONG is trying to take all the market share from RH Launchpads, nor is it simply competing with PONS. Instead, it is more focused on solving the liquidity problem for RWA / Meme Assets.

The launch of OpenAI and Anthropic is a very direct example:Assets get tokenized → LONG provides the trading market → liquidity increases → more assets enter on-chain trading

Therefore, LONG looks more like it is building Liquidity Infrastructure, rather than simply being another Launchpad.

We can already see an increasingly clear path:AI Narrative → OpenAI / Anthropic / NVIDIA and other assets → Tokenized / Leveraged Assets → LONG builds the trading market → Trading Volume + TVL

The fact that OpenAI + Anthropic generated around $32.6M in volume in the first round at least proves that there is real market demand for this new type of asset trading.

Of course, it is still too early to conclude that LONG has succeeded based on this first round of data alone.

The key things to watch are whether NAV and pool prices can remain closely aligned, whether liquidity continues to grow, whether Pre-IPO can expand to more assets, whether AI pairs can continue generating trading volume, and whether LONG can replicate this model across more popular assets.

If these metrics continue to grow, then LONG’s value will no longer simply be that it “launched OpenAI / Anthropic.”

Instead:LONG is attempting to become the trading infrastructure on Robinhood Chain that connects Tokenized Assets, Pre-IPO Assets, and on-chain liquidity.

text:
Vlad这篇文章表面上是在回应AMC，实际上是在替整个Robinhood 争夺资产扩张权

他的核心意思是，上市公司可以控制自己股票附带的权利，但不能控制股票卖给投资者以后的一切合法用途

这件事对RH链非常重要，因为Vlad正在为股票上链后的二次开发划定边界

传统股票买进券商账户以后，除了等待价格上涨和获得分红，基本没有多少可以继续利用的空间。如果股票搬到链上以后，依旧只能买入、卖出和持有，所有玩法仍由平台决定，那不过是给传统券商换了一层区块链外壳，根本没有真正上链的意义。

前段时间很多CEX都在尝试接入股票代币，只要这些资产仍然被锁在CEX内部，用户只能买入、卖出和持有，那本质上就只是增加了一个交易入口，把券商账户里的股票换到了交易所账户里。交易体验方便了，但资产本身仍然是封闭的，更谈不上真正的金融创新

股票代币化真正的分水岭，不是在哪里可以买，而是买完以后能拿它做什么？

所以股票代币化真正的价值，是让这些资产成为开发者可以自由调用和组合的金融积木，在它们之上继续搭建交易对、AMM、借贷、金库以及更多传统金融里不存在的产品

开发者可以围绕这些资产建立交易对、AMM、抵押借贷、收益金库、指数产品，甚至把股票代币与Meme直接配对，再围绕手续费、股票积累、回购和分红设计新的飞轮

我之前对RH链上限的判断，只是把它当成下一条SOL，现在重新看Vlad最近的表态，可能还是低估了他的野心

Vlad想做的，实际是想把股票、ETF乃至未上市公司的资产全部搬到链上，再开放给开发者自由组合。

交易对、AMM、借贷、金库、衍生品，以及股票与Meme的配对玩法，都只是这套新金融体系最早期的实验。

如果这条路真能走通，RH链未来竞争的就不只是其他公链，而是券商、交易所、托管与清算机构共同组成的传统证券基础设施。

现在链上的Meme行情，可能只是RH链积累第一批用户和流动性的冷启动方式，而不是它最终的上限

就在三天前，Canary Staked TRX ETF 正式登陆美国 Cboe，代码 $TRXS 这也是美国第一只现货质押 TRX ETF。

也就是接下来美国人民以后不用注册交易所、不用钱包和私钥，直接通过证券账户就可以买 TRX 的敞口了，

截至 9 月 10 日，TRXS 已经持有约 1.48 亿枚 TRX，资产规模约 5000 万美元。

比特币 ETF 卖的是数字黄金，ETH ETF 卖的是智能合约平台，而 TRX ETF 真正应该卖的故事，可能是稳定币时代的支付基础设施。

近20年来，他单次卖出超过2.5万股的情况极少。2010年以来累计卖出规模大约也就75亿美元左右，而且单年从未超过10亿美元。2024年7月曾卖过112.5万股，已属近年较大动作。

text:
想做 Agent Infra 的创业团队，可以三思而后行！OpenAI 推出 Agents API 公测版，把驱动 Codex 的 harness（运行框架）和基础设施，以一个简单 API 的形式开放给了全部开发者。OpenAI 这次做的事情和 Anthropic 用 Claude Code / Routines 做的事情是同一个动作：把 harness 从“开源库”升格为“托管运行时”，和模型绑定发布、版本化演进。

Harness 由 OpenAI 托管，但“计算环境”你自己选。OpenAI 自家的沙箱、你自己的 VPC、或者 Cloudflare / Vercel / Modal / E2B / Daytona / DigitalOcean / Oracle 这些合作伙伴。这是一个很典型的平台策略：

- 模型 + harness（大脑 + 神经系统）：OpenAI 独占，token 计费，行为数据回流；

- 沙箱 / 执行环境（身体）：开放给合作伙伴，自家也做了一个，这里包括算力、存储、冷启动、合规、VPC 部署等；

- 工具 / 知识 / 工作流（应用）：开发者的差异化产品

对托管商而言，他们被压在"身体"层，而"身体"是可替换的。OpenAI 自己也做了 hosted sandbox，意味着合作伙伴的存在意义是覆盖 OpenAI 不想碰的长尾（VPC、特定合规、特定硬件、特定成本曲线）。这和当年云厂商与 AI 模型厂商的关系是镜像的：模型厂商现在成了"平台"，沙箱厂商成了"基础设施供应商"。

真正的博弈点在状态归属：Agent 的工作目录、中间产物、vault 里的 secret、skills / plugins 放在哪一层？如果状态在沙箱层，托管商有粘性；如果 OpenAI 把状态抽象到 harness 层（这次的 vault_ids、capability_directories 已经在往这个方向走），沙箱就真的变成了可互换的算力。

独立 Agent framework 的窗口正在关闭；沙箱 / agent runtime 是被验证的"铲子"品类，Cloudflare 和 Vercel 在名单上，说明边缘 / 前端云厂商把 agent runtime 当作下一个增长点。对 Rewired Index 的 L2/L3，这是一个可以细化的子赛道。

OpenAI 和 Anthropic 的策略正在趋同；Capability directories、skills / plugins 是下一个生态争夺点。 沙箱可以互换，模型可以互换，但积累在 agent 上的能力包（skills、tools、workflows） 是开发者不愿迁移的东西。

智能时代的设备、平台与应用的雏形已现。这里的应用不一定是我们过去移动互联网时代的那种产品，可能就是“开发者本身”，或者说是公司/自己的业务流的产品化。

author: stacy_muur
quoted_text:
eCash (BIP-300) vs. Blake2b Chain (BIP-110): Two Forks, Two Philosophies

Two Bitcoin forks went live this summer, three weeks apart, and they're really answers to opposite questions.

BIP-110 asks: how do we protect Bitcoin from what it's become? It went after inscriptions and on-chain data, needed miner support, got 2.5% of it, stalled for three weeks, then had to abandon SHA-256 entirely and relaunch on a new proof-of-work just to survive. That pivot cost it the one thing it was trying to defend.

eCash asks a different question: how do we let Bitcoin become more without breaking what it is? Same supply schedule, same emission, same block template. The only real change is BIP-300/301, letting sidechains handle payments, privacy, prediction markets, and any other use case, while L1 stays untouched.

One treats the base layer as a museum to be defended. The other treats it as a foundation to build on, carefully, without touching the foundation itself.

History doesn't hand down a verdict here, but it does offer a pattern. Forks built on subtraction, Bitcoin Gold, Bitcoin SV, tend to fade once their one grievance stops mattering. Forks and platforms built on permissionless addition, Ethereum most of all, end up capturing entire industries, flaws and all.

The next two years will show whether that pattern holds. October 31 is when eCash's permanent chain goes live and the experiment stops being a rehearsal.

Either way, 2026 made one thing clear: Bitcoin's fights aren't just about its past anymore. They're about who gets to build its future, and how.

text:
This tweet is actually very important, and the key point is not that Robinhood Chain has reported another amount of trading volume. Rather, Robinhood CEO Vlad Tenev is directly addressing one of the most fundamental institutional questions around Tokenized Stocks:

How much consent should the issuing company actually have over tokenization?

1. The core question: Is a Tokenized Stock actually the “stock itself”?

Vlad first acknowledged that, more than two months after Robinhood Stock Tokens launched, the market response has far exceeded expectations.

But as the market grows, one question has become impossible to ignore:If a token claims to represent the stock of a company, should that company have the right to approve or reject its tokenization?

His answer is not simply that “all Tokenized Stocks require issuer approval.”

Instead, he breaks the issue down into three principles:

① Investor Property Rights

Publicly traded stocks are fundamentally transferable property belonging to investors.

Therefore, once investors own the stock, they should generally have the right to decide how they hold and transfer it.

② Issuer Authority

Companies naturally control the rights attached to the securities they issue.

But that does not mean:Every financial product built around that company’s stock must be approved by the company.

He compares this to traditional financial products such as ADRs, options, and structured products. These products are related to the underlying stock, but that does not mean the issuing company controls every product built around it.

③ Technology Neutrality

This is arguably the most important principle in the entire piece:Issuer Consent should depend on what the product actually does, not whether it uses Blockchain.

In other words, a financial product should not automatically face an additional set of rules simply because it uses blockchain technology.

2. Vlad gives a very clear standard

If a product:Changes the rights attached to the underlying stock
Replaces the company’s official stock record
Creates new obligations for the company or its Transfer Agent

then:Issuer Consent should be required.

But if it simply:Creates an independent financial product that holds or references a transferable stock, without changing the rights, obligations, or official ownership records of the underlying stock

then:Issuer Consent should not be necessary.

This effectively draws a very clear line around Tokenized Stocks:Tokenized Stock ≠ necessarily the stock itself.

3. This is also why Robinhood chose the “third structure”

Vlad explains that there are different ways to tokenize stocks.

Robinhood Stock Tokens use:Independent third-party financial product → 1:1 backed by the underlying stock

rather than directly modifying the ownership structure of the stock.

Robinhood’s goal is to make Stock Tokens capable of:

Crossing jurisdictions
Covering thousands of stocks and ETFs
Eventually expanding to private stocks and other asset classes

without requiring every underlying company to modify its own systems.

So Robinhood’s approach is actually very clear:Don’t let tokenization disrupt the traditional securities system. Instead, add a new programmable financial layer on top of the existing system.

4. The bigger meaning: Robinhood is redefining what it means to put stocks on-chain

The latter part of Vlad’s post is really about a much bigger question.

For decades, financial infrastructure was largely designed around:Paper stock certificates → Electronic records → Intermediary systems

Blockchain potentially changes that into:Assets becoming more Portable + Transparent + Programmable

So his argument is that we should not assume that because the traditional financial system evolved around physical certificates and centralized infrastructure, that structure is necessarily the final answer.

Blockchain could give investors more choices over:How assets are held, transferred, combined, and used.

5. I think the final point is the most important part of the entire post

Vlad is essentially arguing:Companies should control the rights attached to their own stocks, but they should not necessarily control every financial product investors build around those stocks.

That distinction is extremely important.

Because it means a much larger market could emerge:

Underlying Stock → Tokenized Representation → DeFi / Trading / Structured Products / Composability

The underlying stock rights can remain intact, while a huge number of new on-chain financial products can be built around it.

Finally, I personally think the real signal here is not:

“Robinhood launched another Tokenized Stock product.”

It is:Robinhood is building a long-term institutional and product framework for Tokenized Assets.

And the core idea behind this framework is not:Put stocks on-chain.

It is:Give traditional assets the programmability and composability of Blockchain without changing the underlying ownership rights.

This could directly influence how Tokenized Stocks, ETFs, Private Equity, RWA, and other assets enter the on-chain economy in the future.

The question worth watching next is:If ownership of the underlying asset and the on-chain token can be separated, what can these Tokenized Assets ultimately be composed with?

That may be the real opportunity this post is opening up.

最近让 ChatGPT 帮我把豆包的语音记录自动化了，发现我对 AI 能做什么，还是想得太保守了。

我平时用豆包录语音、记会议，但 Hermes Agent 跑在远程服务器上。一个在 App 里面，一个在服务器上，原本觉得这东西不好接，还是得自己把文字稿弄出来，再发给 Telegram 然后给 Agent。

自从开始思考 100x 的效率提升之后，我感觉这东西也可以自动化。

我就跟 ChatGPT 说，想把这个过程自动化。它直接去豆包代码里找，研究具体怎么下载记录，再写脚本把两边接起来。这些我都没自己动手，主要就是告诉它：我想要实现这个。

现在豆包录完，文字稿会自动交给服务器上的 Hermes Agent，处理结果再发到 Telegram。我直接在那边看就行，不用每次找记录、复制粘贴、再交代一遍。

后面根据会议类型，可以只做总结，也可以把讨论拆开，补充到已有 Todo，或者新建任务跟进。需要发论坛的，也可以先整理成稿子让我看。

到时候开完会，直接忙下一个事情就行了，相关会议内容也会自动加入我的 Hermes memory 里面。太爽了。

感觉以后有些事情，哪怕自己第一反应是“这个应该没法自动化”，也可以先扔给 ChatGPT 试试。我这次连具体方案都没想，就是说了一下想要什么，它就自己往下找办法了。确实牛逼。

text:
The EM Field: The One True Stillness

An EM field exists on a null worldline, where proper time is zero. It also has two points: birth (emission from matter) and destruction (absorption or collapse). But the “moment” between those points is not a tiny slice — it is the entire 76 Gly geometric stretch. The photon’s whole path is one single state, the same kind of moment matter experiences, but stretched across space instead of time.

This is why the EM field is the one true stillness.

From its own frame, the photon never moves. It experiences no distance and no duration. Birth and death are simultaneous. The entire runway exists instantly as a single timeless configuration. The field does not travel; it is a geometric object.

From our frame, the same field moves at \(c\). We impose time on something that contains none. We see motion, stretch, redshift, dilution, and expansion illusions because we are time‑based observers looking at a timeless geometry.

This duality is not a paradox. It is the defining property of null intervals:

Anything on a null worldline is stationary in its own frame and moving at \(c\) in ours.

This explains why we only interact with the EM field once.  
Our worldline has proper time; the photon’s does not.  
Interaction happens only at the exact moment the null path intersects our 3D position.  
Before that moment, the field is not yet observable.  
After that moment, it cannot be observed again.

The wave still exists — but our geometry cannot re‑intersect it.  
We move forward in time; the null worldline does not.

This also explains the horizon limit:  
EM fields that have already passed us are gone for us, but not gone from the universe.  
EM fields that have not yet reached us will be observed later.  
EM fields beyond the remaining horizon distance will never intersect our worldline.

Matter and EM fields are the same conserved energy behaving under different geometric constraints.  
Matter transitions between two energy states across time.  
EM fields transition between two energy states across space.  
Same energy. Different axis.

Matter’s transition moment is tiny in time.  
The EM field’s transition moment is huge in space.  
Both are single states in their own frame.  
Both obey the same conservation rules.  
Both reveal the geometry they inhabit.

This is the core identity of null geometry:  
Light is timeless stillness that appears as motion only to those who have time.

If you think this breaks somewhere, show me where.

TRON mở rộng cửa cho hàng triệu người dùng MetaMask: Bốn dApp lớn chính thức kết nối ví phổ biến nhất thế giới

TRON DAO vừa công bố bước đi tiếp theo trong quan hệ đối tác với MetaMask: bốn ứng dụng lớn nhất hệ sinh thái gồm JustLend DAO, https://t.co/PBDwp4ON27, https://t.co/5vcFNl4nf3 và BitTorrent đã hỗ trợ kết nối trực tiếp ví MetaMask. Động thái này giúp người dùng không còn phải chuyển ví khi muốn sử dụng các dịch vụ DeFi, AI và lưu trữ trên mạng TRON.

Đây không phải thông báo tích hợp lần đầu. Tháng 8/2025, TRON và Consensys (đơn vị phát triển MetaMask) công bố hợp tác chiến lược. Tháng 1/2026, MetaMask ra mắt hỗ trợ native mạng TRON trên cả phiên bản di động và extension, cho phép quản lý TRX, gửi USDT và stake ngay trong ví. Bây giờ, các dApp cụ thể đã “mở cửa” hoàn toàn.

Bốn ứng dụng được chọn và lý do chúng quan trọng

JustLend DAO – giao thức cho vay lớn nhất trên TRON – được phía dự án công bố TVL hơn 7 tỷ USD (một số nguồn độc lập như DefiLlama ghi nhận thấp hơn do phương pháp tính khác nhau). Người dùng MetaMask giờ có thể vay, cho vay, stake và thuê energy để giảm phí giao dịch mà không cần ví riêng.

https://t.co/PBDwp4ON27 mang đến SunSwap V4 với hơn 650 triệu USD TVL và hơn 26.000 pool thanh khoản. Nền tảng này còn hỗ trợ programmable hooks, cho phép nhà phát triển và cả AI agent nhúng logic tùy chỉnh vào pool.

https://t.co/5vcFNl4nf3 đại diện cho hướng đi mới của TRON vào tài chính AI. Nền tảng cung cấp danh tính on-chain cho agent (giao thức 8004) và thanh toán tự động (giao thức x402), giúp các thực thể AI giao dịch độc lập. Việc kết nối MetaMask mở rộng đối tượng tiếp cận cho cả nhà phát triển lẫn người dùng thông thường.

BitTorrent bổ sung khả năng xuyên chuỗi qua BTTC và lưu trữ phi tập trung qua BTFS, hoàn thiện bức tranh từ DeFi đến hạ tầng dữ liệu.

Sam Elfarra, người phát ngôn cộng đồng của TRON DAO, cho biết: “Chúng tôi đang tạo thêm cách để người dùng tương tác với TRON thông qua ví họ đã biết và sử dụng hàng ngày.” Phía MetaMask cũng khẳng định hỗ trợ native trước đó đã tạo nền tảng để người dùng linh hoạt hơn khi tiếp cận hệ sinh thái này.

Trước đây, người dùng MetaMask muốn vào DeFi TRON thường phải cài thêm TronLink, tạo ma sát không nhỏ. Giờ đây, hàng chục triệu người dùng ví phổ biến nhất có thể tiếp cận tốc độ cao, phí thấp và thanh khoản lớn của TRON – đặc biệt là dòng chảy USDT mà mạng này chiếm ưu thế – mà không rời khỏi giao diện quen thuộc.

Đây là bước đi logic sau khi đã có hỗ trợ mạng native. TRON muốn trở thành lựa chọn dễ tiếp cận thay vì chuỗi “chuyên biệt”, trong khi MetaMask củng cố vị thế ví đa chuỗi (đã hỗ trợ Ethereum, Solana, Bitcoin). Việc đưa cả hạ tầng AI agent vào nhóm đầu tiên được tích hợp cho thấy TRON không chỉ cạnh tranh về DeFi truyền thống mà còn muốn chiếm vị trí trong nền kinh tế agent đang hình thành.

Tích hợp này không giải quyết hết mọi rào cản kỹ thuật, nhưng đã giảm đáng kể khoảng cách giữa người dùng phổ thông và một trong những hệ sinh thái blockchain hoạt động mạnh nhất hiện nay.

text:
Ethena đưa USDe và sUSDe lên TRON, mở rộng hệ sinh thái đô la số

TRON DAO và Ethena Labs hôm 11/9 công bố USDe cùng phiên bản sinh lời sUSDe đã chính thức hoạt động trên mạng TRON. Người dùng có thể bridge, nắm giữ và chuyển hai tài sản này thông qua Stargate Finance.

USDe là stablecoin tổng hợp của Ethena, duy trì peg với USD bằng cơ chế delta-neutral (giữ tài sản crypto kết hợp vị thế short trên thị trường phái sinh). sUSDe cho phép người nắm giữ nhận lợi suất từ funding rate. Việc triển khai trên TRON giúp Ethena tiếp cận một trong những mạng thanh toán stablecoin lớn nhất thế giới.

Theo thông tin từ hai bên, TRON hiện có hơn 403 triệu tài khoản và lượng USDT lưu hành vượt 94 tỷ USD. Mạng này từng xử lý hơn 2.000 tỷ USD giao dịch stablecoin chỉ trong một quý. Việc bổ sung USDe và sUSDe được kỳ vọng đa dạng hóa lựa chọn đô la trên chuỗi và tăng thanh khoản cho hệ sinh thái DeFi.

Justin Sun, người sáng lập TRON, cho biết: “Hàng triệu người dựa vào mạng TRON mỗi ngày để thanh toán, tiết kiệm và chuyển giá trị. Việc đưa USDe và sUSDe lên TRON mở rộng lựa chọn cho người dùng và củng cố vai trò hạ tầng phi tập trung phục vụ nhu cầu hàng ngày.”

Guy Young, người sáng lập Ethena Labs, nhận định: “TRON đã có lượng người dùng lớn sẵn sàng nắm giữ và chuyển đô la số với quy mô đáng kể. Tích hợp này cho phép họ giữ một đồng đô la sinh lời ngay trên mạng họ đang sử dụng.”

Hỗ trợ trên các ứng dụng DeFi cốt lõi như JustLend DAO và https://t.co/oOvzu5cc2M dự kiến sẽ được triển khai trong vài tuần tới, sau đó mở rộng sang ví, sàn giao dịch và ứng dụng thanh toán. USDe trên TRON vẫn kết nối thanh khoản với các mạng khác trong hệ sinh thái đa chuỗi của Ethena.

Sự kiện này đánh dấu bước mở rộng mới của Ethena, vốn đã hỗ trợ USDe trên hơn một chục blockchain. Đối với TRON, đây là nỗ lực tiếp tục củng cố vị thế mạng lưới thanh toán đô la toàn cầu, đặc biệt tại các thị trường mới nổi.

> we predicted Sep 9 (after DBS×Citi's weekend USD tx) the Swift ledger would add another live corridor before Sibos (Sep 28). Today it added a whole new currency (domestic SGD) + 2 more banks. Call advancing.

> 3rd live use of the July 17-bank ledger: HSBC/StanChart -> DBS/Citi USD -> now DBS/OCBC/UOB SGD. UOB says it went HKD -> SGD -> USD, currencies added one by one.

> architecture unchanged: Swift ORCHESTRATES across each bank's SEPARATE tokenised-deposit system; obligations netted, finality stays OFF-ledger. Tokenised deposits stay bank liabilities inside the perimeter. Our Aug-24 read, now 3x live.

> the tell is the currency: SG already has instant PayNow/FAST for SGD — so domestic tokenised SGD isn't about speed, it's 24/7 + programmability + denying the use-case to an SGD STABLECOIN (StraitsX XSGD, and whatever MAS's Sep-1 PS Act rules license).

> local (courtlistener): OCBC/UOB/DBS — no US dockets tied to digital-asset business (OCBC's only hit a closed 2012 forfeiture; UOB's are 1980s-90s, closed). Clean. Citi (C) steady ~$136, no unusual move. bullist bank stonks?

> likely >> SG's 3 local banks + DBS's seat on Swift's 12-bank design group = the SGD leg of a bank-owned, Swift-orchestrated settlement web built in parallel to the 21-bank USD stablecoin JV — same Libra/Diem immune response: copy the stablecoin UX on insured deposits, route it through the incumbent messaging monopoly, and the standalone SGD stablecoin never gets its opening.

> next >> by Sibos (Sep 28-Oct 1) or ~Feb 2027 the ledger names a 4th+ currency/corridor OR an atomic cross-currency (PvP) tx — while STILL reporting no ON-ledger final settlement; and MAS's finalized PS Act rules put bank tokenised-deposits and licensed SGD stablecoins in explicit competition. If any of the 17 banks reports on-ledger finality, "orchestration not settlement" breaks.

text:
中国银行业息差降到历史低位，贷款也开始收缩

中国银行业的净息差已经降到 1.4% 左右，处于历史低位，较 2012 年前后收窄了接近一半。银行通过贷款和债券赚取利息收入的空间越来越小。

与此同时，企业和居民借钱的意愿也没有明显恢复。

7 月人民币贷款净减少超过 3,400 亿元，创下有记录以来最大的单月降幅。虽然单月数据会有季节性影响，但贷款净增长转负，至少说明现在愿意增加负债的人并不多。

对于企业来说，利率降低只是借钱更便宜，能不能赚钱才是最重要的。如果订单不够，扩大生产也看不到收益，即便贷款利率继续下降，企业也不会因为钱便宜就主动增加负债。

居民也是一样。房贷利率下降当然可以减少利息支出，但如果对收入增长没有足够信心，买房和增加消费的意愿也不会马上回来。

目前市场关注的中国信贷脉冲也已经处于很低的位置。这个指标主要看新增融资相对于经济规模是在加快还是减慢，数值越低，代表新增信用给投资和消费带来的推动越弱。

这也可能影响中国以外的市场。如果企业减少扩产和设备采购，对原材料和进口商品的需求也会下降，最后会影响大宗商品、全球制造业以及部分出口中国的国家。

目前中国正在向 8 家大型银行和保险机构补充约 3,600 亿元资本，希望提高这些金融机构继续放贷和投资的能力。

这次增资能够改善金融机构的资本状况，提高银行继续放贷的能力。但真正决定信贷能不能重新增长的，还是企业和居民的借贷意愿。如果企业订单没有改善，居民收入预期也没有回升，即便银行有更多资金可以放贷，贷款需求也未必会马上回来。

中国十年国债收益率跌到 1.68%，境内和海外资金正在做出相似的选择

昨天我刚写过，美国上市的主要中国 ETF 在 5 月到 7 月合计净流出了大约 34 亿美元，过去 12 个月累计资金流也从大约 24 亿美元净流入，重新变成了 10 亿美元净流出。

简单来说就是海外资金正在降低中国股票在投资组合里的权重。

而现在中国自己的债券市场又出现了另外一个需要注意的数据。中国 10 年期国债收益率已经跌到 1.68%，创 2025 年 7 月以来最低。国债收益率下降，本质上就是买债的人越来越多，把国债价格买高以后，收益率自然越来越低。

那么为什么还有这么多资金愿意锁定十年，而只换取 1.68% 的年收益呢？（目前美国十年期美债的收益率是将近 4.7%）

如果资金对于未来经济增长、通胀和风险资产的回报非常乐观，那么 1.68% 的十年期收益其实并没有那么大的吸引力。未来经济增长越强，通胀越高，利率越容易重新上升，现在买入的长期国债反而会面临价格下跌。

海外资金降低中国股票的配置，境内资金降低对于风险资产的要求。现在中国市场的问题很可能是大量资金不愿意承担更高的风险。所更多的资金越来越集中到国债、存款以及其他低风险资产里面。

当银行、保险以及各种机构拥有大量需要配置的资金，但居民和企业的融资需求又不够强，能够同时满足安全性、流动性和收益率要求的资产越来越少，最后就只能不断去抢国债，把收益率越压越低。

目前中国虽然资金很多，但愿意借出资金的人不多，愿意承担风险的钱也越来越少。资金正在用不同的方式降低对于中国风险资产的敞口。

一家从个人博客起步到现在一份报告就能把美股砸崩的研究机构SemiAnalysis和它非半导体专业出身的创始人@dylan522p：
1、Dylan Patel出生于1996年，美国佐治亚大学管理与法律学士。青少年时期（8–12岁起）即活跃于在线硬件论坛，作为“forum warrior”自学Xbox等硬件维修、芯片技术，通过阅读文档和社区交流掌握专业知识。多年来以匿名身份在Reddit、WordPress博客及Silicon Twitter上发布芯片与硬件分析内容，以及moderation 多个Nvidia等硬件社区。

2、2020年5月22日，Dylan在24岁生日时发布第一篇博客，此后正式创立SemiAnalysis。最初以个人匿名WordPress博客起步，后转型为Substack付费内容。

早期就是Dylan一人独自专注于半导体供应链、AI基础设施、云生态系统、机器学习模型及相关领域的深度分析，后面慢慢发展出咨询业务。

Dylan自己也从匿名“Silicon Twitter芯片博主”成长为全球范围内最受关注的AI基础设施分析师之一。

3、近几年SemiAnalysis快速扩张，目前已发展为全球最领先的AI基础设施与半导体研究机构，团队规模约60人，分布于美国、日本、台湾、新加坡、法国、德国、以色列、加拿大、英国等8–10个国家/地区。

2026年SemiAnalysis预计营收超过1亿美元（The Information报道），较早期订阅模式实现爆发式增长。业务模式包括：
1）付费订阅（newsletter + 深度报告）；
2）专有行业模型销售（AI Datacenter Model、Accelerator Industry Model、Wafer Fab Model、AI Cloud TCO Model、AI Networking Model等，用于预测晶圆产能、数据中心电力、加速器产量、TCO经济性等）；
3）顾问业务、定制项目和小时咨询。

提供全供应链（晶圆厂→云端→ML模型）统一视角。 这些专有模型和数据（如卫星图像监测数据中心建设、GitHub commit分析、HBM供应链跟踪）成为客户核心决策工具，客户涵盖顶级AI实验室、超大规模云服务商（hyperscalers）、对冲基金及半导体巨头，其分析直接影响万亿美元级AI资本支出决策。

4、更关键的SemiAnalysis现在的超级影响力
1）黄仁勋在今年GTC keynote上，公开点名Dylan Patel，把SemiAnalysis最新InferenceX芯片性能报告秀上大屏，花了整整5分钟专门解读，还在Q&A继续引用。Jensen这种级别的大佬主动call out一个独立分析师，含金量直接拉满。

2）苏姿丰更狠：SemiAnalysis发了一篇狠批AMD MI300X训练性能的报告，第二天Lisa Su就亲自打电话安排90分钟一对一面谈，后来还公开推文感谢“feedback is a gift even when it’s critical”。这操作，简直是把独立研究机构直接拉进CEO级战略对话。

从这个角度出发时SemiAnalysis已不再是单纯的“newsletter”，而是AI半导体生态的战略情报枢纽。其影响力通过专有数据模型 + 高频媒体曝光 + 双边客户服务三重放大，直接服务于硅谷的工程决策和华尔街的亿级交易。

现在对冲基金和资管机构做AI/semiconductor仓位时，SemiAnalysis的月度ChipBook和专有数据已经是标准配置——idea generation、thesis validation、portfolio tracking全靠它。报告一出，经常直接带动股价波动和数百亿capex调整。 hyperscalers规划自定义ASIC、GPU采购、数据中心电力，都得看它的供应链拆解。已经不是“参考”，而是直接左右决策。

这就是典型的“非传统0到1”：没名校EE PhD，没大厂背景，就靠自学+数据驱动+独立思考，从匿名博客干到让NVIDIA CEO和AMD CEO都得认真对待的程度。硅谷和华尔街现在都默认——想搞清楚AI硬件真实节奏，先看SemiAnalysis和Daylan说了什么。

一个人能把独立投研做到最极致的地步估计也就是这个状态了。

Caroline Ellison has joined Manifund, the philanthropic funding platform, in a full-time role developing its platform and researching how to direct philanthropic dollars. Manifund's Austin Chen announced that Ellison began a work trial on July 13 and converted to full-time on Aug 10, publishing her work and supporting users under the pseudonym "Carol" for roughly two months.

Chen tied the hire to a debt he says he owes the FTX Future Fund, which seed-funded Manifold, paid for the retreat that drew him into the EA community, and the conference where he met his wife. Chen acknowledged the pseudonym compromised Manifund's stated commitment to transparency and said users, donors, and partners may be skittish. He cited Ellison's finance and systems expertise, including a reconciliation tool that caught several misregistered transactions worth five to six figures. quoted_text:
The restraint debate on Taiwan is advancing. I’d like to put forward the problems I see with calls to end the currently ambiguous U.S. commitment to Taiwan by clarifying that the United States would not defend Taiwan:

1. If the United States announced it wouldn’t defend Taiwan, confidence in Taipei could collapse and Beijing could move swiftly to bring Taiwan under its control while an unusually accommodating U.S. president remained in office. So there would be a real risk of China taking over Taiwan in the near term.

2. Chinese control of Taiwan would hit the U.S. economy hard. If China cut off U.S. access to Taiwan’s semiconductor fabs (or if Washington cut off inputs to the fabs), America could suffer a recession. It could try to accommodate China to keep the chips flowing, but China could still keep the most advanced chips away from America, much as Washington has kept them away from Beijing. Could the United States rapidly build fabs able to manufacture the most advanced chips? Lots of evidence says it can’t, at least not at speed and scale. If it can, let’s see the plan.

3. The proposal would oddly demote Taiwan to a uniquely low status. Washington does not affirmatively rule out defending countries; it commits to defend allies and stays silent otherwise. Taiwan implicates U.S. interests more than many treaty allies do. So abandoning Taiwan would make the strategic logic behind U.S. foreign policy less coherent (or more incoherent) and give allies a good reason to reassess America’s commitment to their own defense. That should be a manageable challenge, and could spur some allies to step up. But there’s an important debate to be had about which allies Washington should then reassure and how.

4. Domestic backlash: Abandoning Taiwan outright could politicize the issue and prompt members of Congress and presidential candidates to push for reinstating the old policy or supporting Taiwan more strongly than before. If the next administration merely restores strategic ambiguity, the United States would likely end up worse off: Taiwan’s confidence will have been shaken and China won’t be reassured. This risk could be reduced by waiting for the U.S. political environment to change — but that would indefinitely defer the policy shift.

The alternative is to maintain strategic ambiguity, restrain Taipei where necessary, and affirm or strengthen the elements of the One China policy that reassure Beijing. Meanwhile the United States could take many materially meaningful actions: help Taiwan strengthen its defenses, develop ways to aid Taiwan in a crisis short of direct intervention, shift posture away from the first island chain, and expand semiconductor manufacturing at home and elsewhere. Those measures would work to prevent a cross-strait war and reduce America's economic exposure without handing Taiwan to Beijing.

text:
To let go of understanding, or not, that is the question.

If you can (1) control how a system works, (2) verify that it indeed works, (3) continuously improve how it works, and (4) leverage it as a subcomponent in building a bigger system, does it really matter if you *understand* the system or not?

Before AI, none of (1)-(4) was possible if you didn't understand the system. Increasingly, AI can do all four without any humans understanding the core of the system. This will eventually be true in verifiable domains: in math, science, engineering, and beyond.

As an ex-academic and a VC who works with mamy product & engineering teams, I see many around me encountering and grappling with this deep philosophical question very abruptly. There is simply an inmate desire to understand, for anyone trained and with careers in STEM. But this innate desire may turn out to be counter productive in the age of rapidly improving AI.

text:
ZCG is sitting on a large accumulated treasury, and the Foundation has historically held tens of millions in liquid assets. 

That pile of ZEC is one of Zcash’s advantages.

For many reasons. 

The war chest is insurance against political winter.

Zcash is not a normal L1. 

Privacy can become legally radioactive overnight. 

VCs, exchanges, and corporate treasuries can leave. 

Protocol issuance cannot be subpoenaed away.

John’s reply is the strongest version of this: “Zcash is a movement to fix money, not a portfolio company that can pivot.”

Will Paradigm and Coinbase Ventures still fund shielded infrastructure if an administration treats privacy as a crime? 

The Dev Fund / lockbox / ZCG runway is the part of the stack that does not need their permission.

Zcash already lived through an SEC probe of the Foundation. 

Having years of reserves is why that did not become an extinction event.

Bitcoin still needed OpenSats / Chaincode / MIT DCI precisely because miner rewards do not magically produce protocol work. 

Ethereum’s recent spinouts happened after a well-funded foundation existed for a decade, not instead of one.

Killing the default funding source and hoping Kickstarters appear is an experiment you run on a bs hobby chain, not on a top-10 privacy asset during an institutionalization wave.

A rising ZEC price making the chest last “for centuries” is a feature.

If ZEC goes up because the protocol got better, the same reserved coins buy more engineering years and more preventative medicine. 

Contributors paid in ZEC stay aligned with the asset. That is the opposite of a fiat bureaucracy that must raise taxes to survive.

A 10-year runway is not decadence in a field where one circuit bug can theoretically threaten supply credibility. 

Zcash just had to migrate off Orchard after a multi-year proving-system flaw. 

You want paid cryptographers on retainer before the next one.

Also redirecting 20% to miners is not “removing a tax.” It is changing who gets diluted.

It’s also bad timing for this. 

ZEC is in the first period where institutions, an ETF, a DAT, and a new core lab all exist at once. 

This is exactly when you want continuous protocol work on UX, fees, post-quantum, and shielded defaults — not a multi-year funding cliff while organizations relearn how to beg.

Private capital arrived because the protocol kept shipping under a funded model.

quoted_text:
Accolade Partners' Aram Verdiyan with a16z's Jen Kha and David George on AI's extreme power law and where the next trillion dollars gets made:

The classic way to blow up a startup was throwing too much money at it. Hire a thousand people, create dueling priorities, and kill what was working.

AI turned spending into a vending machine. You put dollars in and you get something out. Money buys compute and compute alone can improve a product. Nothing has concentrated returns like this since the social networks.

The same concentration runs through the funds. Accolade looked at 3,000 US venture firms and found only 20 delivered consistent 3x net returns over two decades. What they have in common is access to the category-defining company, fund after fund.

In this conversation, Aram, Jen, and David get into why AI is being sold against labor budgets rather than software budgets, why an LP gets fired for the opposite reasons a GP does, and why getting the fund right but sizing it wrong is the same as missing it.

Symbiosis experienced a security incident. At approximately 04:28 UTC on Sep 11, 2026, attacker exploited a vulnerability in Bitcoin Bridge. BTC routes have been halted. Other routes remain operational and safe.

Where we stand:
• Only the Bitcoin Bridge was affected, and it is isolated from our other systems. All other routes: EVM chains, TRON, TON and the rest are unaffected and operating normally, as are Octopools and all other components.
• The team has recovered approximately 15 BTC, now secured on a team-controlled multisig.
• We have contacted the attacker with a white-hat bounty offer of 20% of the funds, open until Sep 13 2026. After that window, the same 20% will be offered to anyone providing information that leads to recovery.
• Final accounting is in progress. We will publish confirmed figures in our next update.
• Liquidity providers: we are contacting every affected LP directly. We are building a compensation framework and will publish the criteria shortly.
• Our relayer group continues to operate and secure the network.

Thank you to the security researchers who moved fast with us. We have been building Symbiosis for five years, and we are confident we will come through this. Thank you all for the support — we will keep posting updates as they come.

text:
This happens as long-term rates rise relative to short-term rates. Though they try to hold short rates down, long rates are climbing, a trend we are already seeing. We are also seeing a weakening dollar and movements in gold.

As rates rise, it starts to affect the stock market. With bonds dropping and stocks rising, the prospective returns of stocks are now low compared to bonds, translating into broader stock market pressure.

This classic dynamic creates a stagflationary environment that the Federal Reserve struggles to manage. With current stagflation, the Fed wrestles with whether to tighten or ease. In an economy with vast wealth disparity, the financial impact differs drastically depending on whether you own stocks, which carries huge political implications.
#Stagflation #Macroeconomics #FederalReserve #StockMarket

text:
完全不同的增长逻辑。

如果 HIP4 走 @Polymarket  和 @Kalshi 的完全手续费的道路，那 HIP4 基本没戏。

HIP4 的价值在于生态性，也就是利用低手续费打开预测市场的应用创新，也就是激发生态玩法，创造出更多的预测场景，这样即使是手续费低，通过放大交易量甚至别的玩法也可以活的很好。

也就是 Pm 和 kalshi 更是一个预测的项目，在场景容量一定的情况下，只能精工细作来向内发展。手续费完全依赖。

我们需要低手续费，并不只为了便宜一点交易成本，而是需要降低摩擦成本，孕育创新，孕育新的场景，做增量市场。

text:
Quantum computing is always a super interesting topic for me.

And also scary.

If the cryptography crypto relies on isn’t upgraded in time, a powerful enough quantum computer could eventually break some of the security protecting wallets, signatures, and ZK systems today.

@LayerZero_Labs is already preparing for that with Akita, a new piece of cryptography designed to keep ZK proofs secure against quantum computers.

It’ll first be used in Jolt, the proving system behind Zero.

And the upgrade is useful long before quantum computers become a problem:

→ Proofs shrink to 65-80kb
→ Proving runs 2-3x faster
→ Memory usage drops by roughly half

Quantum security isn't an urgent problem, but faster proofs and lower memory are useful right now.

Gud tek.
