text:
上线不到3个月，bStocks @bstocksfinance 累计交易量来到300亿美元，这个数字最近不少人在聊。

比起单纯看一个里程碑数字，更值得留意的，是这背后用户在寻找的东西。
传统的股票市场，一直有明确的开市、休市时间表。很多人日常要忙工作，只有夜晚、周末才有空复盘行情，等发现机会，市场已经休市，很难跟着自己的节奏参与。

bStocks给出的一个变化，就是7×24小时可交易。不再被固定时段束缚，你什么时候有空研究市场，什么时候就能操作。

不止是时间上的松绑。Direct Stocks覆盖超过7000个热门资产，同时支持期权交易，标的选择空间更广；TradFi合约还支持多空双向，看待市场不再只有看涨这一种视角，可以根据自己的判断选择交易方向。

这也是为什么短短时间，会积累起300亿交易量。
本质上是把TradFi资产的参与门槛降低，把时间、标的、交易方向的选择权交到用户手里，慢慢把传统金融和加密生态打通，在同一个平台提供一套新的参与路径。

text:
Just opened the "Ghost in the Thread group show at @ArtverseParis featuring the artists: Nam June Paik, LoVid @lovidlovid, Travess Smalley @TravessSmalley, @chepertom , Rune Brink @spogelsemaskin. 

Open until October 18th at 5bis rue de Beauce 75003 Paris

Email contact@artverse.fr for the catalog

“The glitch is a momentum: that moment that makes you pivot and reflect... an object slides from a normal operation into something different—a powerful confusion that forces the user to reevaluate their understanding of media.”

— Rosa Menkman, The Glitch Moment(um), 2011

Long before silicon microchips, computing was born on a weaver’s loom. Joseph Marie Jacquard’s 1804 automated loom used binary punch cards to guide warp and weft threads, establishing that the digital grid of pixel resolution and the tactile matrix of textiles share the exact same structural DNA. Riffing on the “ghost in the machine,” Ghost in the Thread explores how the ephemeral, glowing, and glitching code of digital signals is bound into physical and phygital materiality.

The exhibition traces an intergenerational arc beginning with Nam June Paik’s seminal 1994 work, DO NOT WATCH TV. By manipulating cathode-ray signals, Paik turned broadcast culture into a site of active disruption, laying the foundation for glitch aesthetics. LoVid extends this legacy, translating analog video synthesis and raw electrical currents into a vibrant multi-channel installation that renders the hidden digital ghost tangible.

A new generation of artists continues this fluid movement between code and physical space. Chepertom converts pixel drawings and algorithmic glitches into custom Jacquard tapestries, demonstrating that a digital pixel and a woven knot are functionally identical. Travess Smalley collapses vector graphics and physical printmaking, treating software manipulation and collage as a single continuous medium. Rune Brink examines digital nostalgia and low-resolution screen architecture, bringing pixelated anomalies into dialogue with physical space.

text:
if you’re back trenching - some helpful learnings for you that i learnt from top trenchers:

1) think of memecoin trading as a 'casino'. assume the house has a ~10% edge against you:

–  5% goes to trading costs: slippage, terminal fees, LP fees, chain fees/mev etc
–  next ~5% comes from on an average insiders having more edge

every $100 you trade returns ~$90 on average over time - so yeah you only trade if you're having fun or you seriously have an edge

2) any tokens (and stocks too) is Poker on steroids:

>  you’ve to predict what others will think will be the next big narrative in X time horizon

X can be few years, few months or even few mins!

you literally just to have predict what’ll have attention in X days

>  the narrative or story should be big enough to excite capital and the gap between the price of story now and price of story in X days is your edge!

(revenue, value, fundamentals, buybacks etc etc are all just part of story)

>  don’t ever think in isolation on what’s worth as per you - i used to make this mistake. you’ll mid curve i.e you’ll be right but but remember: markets can remain irrational longer than you can remain solvent

3) fomo/pump PnL leaderboards:

>  if you’re seeing high PnLs on fomo, don’t literally fomo - these are all unrealised gains and many will simply roundtrip and never ever copy trade them

(ATHs are exactly the illusion which gives that greed dopamine in our brain - you'll often see 150x scan in your telegram group chats, but it's all a trap)

however, you can learn a lot from studying how top traders trade and adapt to your edge 

> i personally keep reading all thesis everyone put across fomo, pump, tg group chats etc to understand how other trenches think - this helps me build a mental model on what they’ll think and like in the near future

(listening to some of these trader's podcasts/streams are also v useful)

> some apps have huge slippage sometimes, if you're ape'ing real size - it's always good to verify this and buy directly from jupiter/relay/uniswap etc

4) shareability: 

tokens are simple and beautiful - they just need an one-liner simple thesis to be able to be maximally share-able

(eg. micron is just a bet on memory bottleneck for AI or fone is a bet on mobile trading going more popular)

a mental model i use: before buying, i always ask myself - what’s the 1-2 liner story that i can share with my friends - which’ll convince them to buy

sometime i even test this with 1-2 friends and they'll feel convinced after my thesis and it's still under the public radar - it's a buy for me

4) exit strategy: 

memecoins and most token/stocks aren’t for holding forever - every trade has an expiry date

> always be selling: i generally keep selling on the way up - particularly whenever i feel euphoric on the trade (eg. feeling urge to share screenshot with my friends), i just sell some and take profit

and if i still feel it can go up, i just keep small 'moonbag' so i don't have regrets

i've fumbled many 100x-es by selling early but i've 0 regrets as long as i'm selling at profits 

(limit orders are also a good way to keep taking profits or even buy the dips)

> if you sell some signs of exhaustion in meta (i.e you feel like the party is getting over), it's also a good idea to start selling - rather than holding it

5) don’t trade unless you’ve an edge:

yes, you can trade small to learn but only put good size when you genuinely have an edge (and have strong conviction)

eg. you’ve some exclusive alpha or you researched/thought v deeply on a coin/investment

sizing is key: you'll feel like you've an edge on lot of trades, but only put real size if you can feel deep in your bones 

and it’s fine if you missed big runners, no point paying attention to them now or revenge trading

> never chase a trade which is fairly consensus now: yes you can some money chasing momentum but most likely you'll be top blasting

6) fair-launched projects:

there's huge number of indie devs (mostly undoxxed) launching projects - and many are vibe-coded

here, ai is incredibly helpful to filter & research

if you've a good tech or product sense or if you know devs well - it's genuinely your edge, leverage it

you just need to nail, if it can get attention

--

i personally love trenching and having fun with friends: always happy to help anyone who’s looking to have fun (and maybe make or loose money in the process)

happy trenching 🫡

text: This one is very cool. Now you can mount Box to agent sandboxes to make it far easier for an agent to read and write files on the agent's computer. As AI agents execute critical workflows in the enterprise, they're going to need the same primitives that people have had.
author: levie
quoted_text:
🆕 @OpenAIDevs Agents API gives developers a hosted sandbox where agents run tools, coordinate work, and handle complex tasks. Box Mount brings enterprise content directly into that sandbox as files the agent can read, reason across, and produce new work from, using normal shell commands and file paths while Box Mount handles two-way sync automatically.

In our demo, a lead agent mounts a deal room from Box, reads five source files, launches three specialist agents in parallel, and writes four reports back through Box Mount with an initial verdict. When a customer revises the MSA in Box, Box Mount syncs the new version into the same sandbox and the agents reassess automatically, refreshing all four reports while preserving the revised MSA as version two in Box.

text:
BREAKING: SpaceXAI has added a new guide called “Grok Bot 101”

It explains how to create a personal AI teammate in just 10 to 15 minutes, teach it real workflows, connect apps, and build teams of specialized bots that continue working in the cloud even after you close your laptop.

Here is the full guide in simple terms:

• What is Grok Bot

Grok Bot is an AI agent with its own persistent computer in the cloud. It has a desktop, files, terminal, browser, and apps. It can browse the web, use software, write and run code, and complete tasks just like someone using a computer.

You can access the same computer from your phone or desktop. When needed, Grok Bot can hand control back to you for a CAPTCHA, 2FA, or secure login.

• Creating a bot

Give the bot a name, title, and detailed instructions. You can explain the workflow through chat or record yourself completing the task.

Once trained, the bot can repeat that workflow whenever needed. It can also use MCP servers, plugins, skills, and connected services such as Gmail, Google Calendar, Google Drive, and Slack.

• Three ways to use Grok Bot

Send it a message in chat.
Create schedules or triggers, such as monitoring a Slack thread or GitHub PR.
Allow bots to message and activate other bots.

• Permissions and safety

You can write rules in normal language explaining what the bot can and cannot do.

A separate review agent checks proposed actions and can allow them, block them, or ask you for approval. Allow and block lists provide additional control, while the work runs inside an isolated environment.

One important detail: if you log into a website with one bot, other bots using that shared cloud computer can also access it.

• Multi-bot teams

You can create specialist bots for different jobs and let them work together.

One bot can ask another for help, several bots can work inside a group chat, and a scheduled routine can move a task through multiple specialists until the work is finished.

• Personal CRM

The author created a bot that turned the 800 to 900 people he follows on X into a private Notion CRM containing public profile information.

It helps him find and reconnect with people when traveling.

• Arnold, the fitness bot

He replaced a complicated fitness app with a Grok Bot strength-training coach named Arnold.

The bot uses MCP servers, plugins, and skills while requiring less maintenance. Its behavior can be updated simply by chatting with it.

• Building software

Grok Bot gathers information from Slack, Notion, GitHub, documentation, and other sources. It then creates a clean prompt and sends it to a specialized Cursor cloud agent that builds the software.

Grok Bot handles the planning and coordination, while the coding agent handles the actual build.

• Searching company knowledge

Grok Bot can search across codebases, Slack conversations, Notion pages, GitHub, and internal documents to answer product or company questions.

This helps people find information faster and reduces the need to interrupt coworkers.

• The biggest takeaway

Instead of repeatedly building scripts or complicated apps, you can describe a workflow to Grok Bot, improve it through chat, reuse it, and let it continue working in the cloud.

Grok Bot is not just another chatbot. It is a real AI teammate with a computer that can use tools, coordinate specialists, and get actual work done.

The future of work is becoming incredibly exciting.

Hi Astra users. A reset and a quick update on quality issues that have been posted around.

Working with some of you, we have found and fixed the following issues:
- Some skills written for previous models were triggering too often or preventing the model from checking its work.
- An opt-in context management experiment that could cause early stops or replies to older messages. We've disabled it. Our rough estimate is that 4-5k users were affected by this experiment.
- We've also removed some badly configured engines that resulted in a measured quality degradation for a long tail of traffic flowing through them.

We’ve also made some more minor improvements and things should feel significantly better across the board. More consistent follow-through, better tracking of your latest message, and better checks on the work as it’s going through the motions.

The examples posted and all the users who worked directly with us were incredibly useful in helping fix things quickly. Always grateful for this incredible community.

And of course, a reset is also landing by midnight today.

quoted_text:
To those responsible for the theft of bitcoin from the Liquid Network:

Blockstream will not pay a ransom for the return of stolen funds. Taking assets without authorization and withholding their return is a crime, not responsible disclosure. It is not white-hat activity. It is theft.

We have engaged in good faith in an effort to secure the return of stolen user funds and protect the broader Bitcoin community. That effort should not be mistaken for acceptance of the actions taken nor of the terms being demanded.

We will not be a party to the precedent that open-source software developed for the good of the Bitcoin community should subject its developers to paying a ransom that far exceeds their economic participation. 

Bitcoin is hard money and can’t be minted without costs, Bitcoin doesn’t haircut users to pay a ransom.

To the Bitcoin community:

We are fighting for what we believe in, for the users whose funds were taken, and for the principles on which Bitcoin was built.

The community has demonstrated incredible resolve with teams of people dedicating their time in support of each other to identify and patch vulnerabilities in each other's products and systems. We are all driven by the mission that Bitcoin is the single best asset, for every person, company, and institution on the planet to invest, use, and build on. The world is a different place with the advancements of AI, and the Bitcoin community has responded with force to combat that threat.  

Damage has been done, battles have been lost, but on the whole the Bitcoin community is gaining ground in the war with bad actors.  

We want to thank the community for those efforts, for your support in hardening the network, helping users recover funds, and for your support in our assertion that crime does not deserve rewards.

To those holding the stolen bitcoin:

There is still an opportunity to resolve this responsibly. The bitcoin can be returned and we can revert to the standard of white-hat principals.

However, if the funds are not returned, we will pursue every lawful avenue available to us. We will work with law enforcement, exchanges, service providers, forensic specialists, and other relevant parties to trace and recover the assets and identify those responsible.

More importantly, Bitcoin is transparent by design and the community is made up of the most sophisticated engineers, cryptographers, and white-hat hackers globally. Transactions do not disappear, and neither does the evidence they leave behind.

We will not pay for the return of stolen property. We will not abandon our users. The Bitcoin community will not stop pursuing the funds.

Return the bitcoin.

- What we built

Ghost Compute is a sealed place to run the parts of your work that should stay private. You encrypt the sensitive input, it runs inside hardware that no one can look into, and you get back an encrypted result plus a receipt that proves it ran correctly and untouched.

What that gives users

Your edge stays yours. If you run a trading model, a research process, or an agent with a strategy, the people hosting the servers normally see all of it. With Ghost Compute they see nothing. The strategy, the data, and the model stay hidden.

Your orders do not get front run. Size, price, and intent stay private until the trade clears, so no one can trade ahead of you.

You do not have to trust us. Every job returns a receipt you can check yourself. It proves the work ran inside a genuine sealed environment, without revealing what the work was.

It plugs into what you already build. Encrypted input in, encrypted result and receipt out. Model agnostic, no plaintext sitting in logs or public data.

Built where it matters. It runs on Robinhood Chain, where real money and tokenized assets move, which is exactly where private compute stops being a nice to have.

One line for users: you can run private computations on infrastructure you do not own, keep your data and your strategy invisible, and still prove the result is real.

Most infra projects solve one very specific trust problem.

@DeepSafe_AI is trying to build the layer underneath all of them.

The idea is simple: instead of trusting that a message, transaction, oracle update or AI output is valid, you verify it cryptographically.

That same verification layer can be used across:

→ cross-chain messaging
→ asset custody
→ oracles
→ BTC self-custody
→ AI agents
→ privacy/compliance

What makes DeepSafe interesting is that it is not positioning itself as another bridge, oracle or restaking protocol.

It is positioning verification itself as the product.

Under the hood, its CRVA architecture combines ZKP + Ring-VRF → MPC → TEE, with validators selected in a way that makes the verification process harder to predict or target.

70+ ecosystem partners already, with names like MetaMask, OKX, Intel and ARM.

text:
A lot of people are asking what's going on with NPC, so let me just talk to you straight.

I've been dealing with some things in my personal life that I'd rather keep to myself. Nothing dramatic, just life, and it pulled me away more than I wanted it to. I'm sorry for the quiet.

Here's the honest context though. NPC started as a joke. A faceless character that does nothing, a zero narrative, back when nobody was asking about utility or roadmaps. People just collected them because they liked them. That was the whole thing, and it was beautiful.

Then we shipped. And shipped again. Points, badges, playable characters, training, all of it. And somewhere along the way, shipping that much quietly raised the expectations of what NPC is supposed to be. I understand that completely. Maybe part of it is on me for setting a pace. And maybe part of it is fair, maybe you just want me around more, and honestly, that's true, I could be more present.

I know the floor going down made some of you nervous too, and I get it. But if you look past the number, the community is still here, still active, still showing up every single day. That has not changed, and that matters far more to me than a floor price ever will.

It's been about three and a half months since mint. I won't pretend I never get demotivated, because I do. That's part of the process, and I wouldn't take any of this back, because all of it led here.

And to be honest, the easy move right now would be to chase the noise. Everyone's on Robinhood, and we could launch something there tomorrow and manufacture instant hype. But I won't do that. It would be a short-term sugar rush that makes things worse, not better, and it isn't what NPC is about. We build the slow way, on purpose.

What I can tell you is I'm still in the background working on the things I actually want to ship. I also see a lot of people offering to CTO, and I genuinely respect that, it means you care more than I could ask for. It's not something I'm closed off to down the line, and there may come a point where opening this up makes sense. But not right now, not while I've still got things I want to see through myself. If you want to help in the meantime, I'd love that energy pointed at building with me rather than around me.

And as a small thank you for sticking around, we're moving royalties from 5.55% to 0% for a while. Trade freely.

NPC was always heading toward zero. Turns out the royalties got there first.

text:
🚨 Someone open sourced an entire animal.

Not a model of an animal. The animal.

A fruit fly, rebuilt joint by joint from microscopy, that walks, grips, flies and lands inside a physics engine running on your laptop.

It's called flybody. Built by Google DeepMind and HHMI Janelia, published in Nature, and sitting on GitHub under Apache 2.0 right now.

What's actually inside:

A full body in MuJoCo. Legs, wings, head, abdomen, every joint articulated and physically simulated.

A 59-dimensional action space in the walking task alone. That is how many things a network has to coordinate for the fly to take one step.

Leg adhesion, so it actually grips surfaces instead of sliding off them like a game asset.

Ready-made RL environments: walking imitation, free flight, and vision-guided flight where the policy flies on what the fly sees.

The whole thing is Python. Clone it, open MuJoCo, and the fly is on your screen.

And the part that got me:

Nobody animated any of this. You hand the body to a reinforcement learning agent and it discovers how to move it. Same loop as a robot arm, except the robot is a bug and the reward is staying airborne.

Which means people are now training it to do things no fly has done in 100 million years of evolution.

525 stars. Apache 2.0. Zero dollars.

text:
Look at somebody’s forehead. You see skin. Put it under a microscope and you see cells.

Increase the magnification and you see smaller structures inside the cells.

Near field methods recover information from evanescent waves and have resolved structures around 50 nanometers. Some methods have gone below that.

At that scale, the optics does not give a clean picture of the structure, but the light right next to it carries information that tells us what is there.

So the picture can be gone while the information is still there!

That does not prove God. It does not prove a soul. It does not prove whatever spiritual explanation somebody wants to attach to it.

But it does make this harder to say!!

“If I cannot see it, nothing is there.”

Look closer!

Cells are made of molecules. Molecules are made of atoms. Inside the atom are electrons and a nucleus. Inside the nucleus are protons and neutrons. Inside those are quarks.

By then, the picture of matter most of us learned in school is not enough anymore.

Electrons and quarks are not little hard pieces sitting inside bigger hard pieces. Quantum field theory describes them as excitations of fields.

The vacuum is not blank space with nothing there. It is the lowest energy state of those fields.

The same physics applies to the chair, the air going into your lungs, your skin, Jupiter, Andromeda.

String theory goes another step and proposes strings beneath that picture. So far, experiments have not shown that strings are actually there.

It belongs in the discussion, but we cannot talk about it as if physics has already confirmed it.

A brick is still a brick.

If one hits you in the head, you are not thinking about quantum fields.

Matter is solid where we live. That does not answer what matter is when you reduce the scale far enough.

They are related questions. They are not the same question.

From there we have to separate what physics has shown from what people build on top of it.

Do all of these fields, waves, particles, and the information carried through them come from one underlying whole?

That is a proposal. Physics has not answered it for us.

If it were true, then a person would also exist inside that whole and carry information of their own.

Think about a great athlete.

Watch one move, catch, dribble. There is much more happening than shown to you.

Timing. Balance. Position. Memory. Reaction. Years of repetition. Decisions happening faster than the player could stop and explain them.

A surgeon has another set of learned responses.

An engineer has another.

So does the guy awake at two in the morning thinking about the car he wants.

People carry what they have learned, practiced, felt, repeated, and become good at.

That earlier point stands. Information can be present when the image is not. That is a fact about measurement. It is not yet a fact about skill moving from one person to another.

Can any of that information move between people in ways we do not understand yet?

Some people call that resonance.
Fine.

The word does not make the claim quantum mechanics.

Interference between physical waves is real.

Astronomical interferometers combine signals collected by instruments far apart and recover detail one instrument could not recover in the same way.

People calculated it. Built the equipment. Tested it.

It works.

The claim that an informational pattern can enter somebody’s nervous system through microtubules is different.

Penrose and Hameroff brought microtubules into a disputed theory of consciousness. Their work does not show that another person’s skill, knowledge, courage, or ability can be transferred through those structures.

That needs its own evidence.

And if somebody says this transfer happens, I want to know what failure looks like.

One person goes through the process and improves.

We call that a success.

Another person goes through it and nothing changes.

If the answer is automatically that the second person resisted it, then nothing can count against the claim.

Success supports it. Failure gets explained away.

What result would tell us we were wrong?

If there is no answer, then the test is not telling us much.

That does not make the question stupid.

Information can be present when the image is not.

We can measure that.

We do not know how far that fact goes.

It may go much farther than we can test today.

It may not.

There is no reason to pretend we already know.

The conversation goes bad when people decide the answer before they have enough to decide it.

Someone hears anything spiritual and stops listening because they do not want to look foolish.

Someone else hears the word quantum, notices that it sounds close to something they already believe, and takes it far beyond what the experiment showed.

Now they are arguing about two different claims.

One person refuses to look.

The other already knows what they want to find.

Then somebody asks why more information never comes through.

Did you buy the ticket?

No?

Then why are we talking about the jackpot?

Suppose there really were some way to communicate with an intelligence we normally cannot reach.

Call it God.

Call it spirit.

Call it a field.

Call it an old man sitting in a room who looks harmless enough that nobody pays much attention to him.

What would you ask?

I think a lot of us would embarrass ourselves.

A house.

A blue car.

Money.

A white room.

A red sports car.

Meanwhile nobody brought the geneticist.

Nobody brought the economist.

The physicist who has been stuck on the same ugly problem for thirty years is somewhere else.

An hour that could have gone into DNA gets spent talking about a floor plan.

After enough of that, I imagine whoever is answering saying, “Can somebody else take this one? Send me somewhere with dinosaurs.”

Anything but another car question.

It is funny because we already do this.

Give somebody time with an expert and they spend half of it asking something they could have found in five minutes.

Give somebody a library and they search for the book that agrees with them.

Give somebody an hour to work on the problem bothering them and suddenly six other jobs need attention first.

We already know how to waste access.

So if information existed beyond what we currently know how to reach, getting access would only solve half the problem.

We would still have to ask something worth answering.

The physics deserves the same standard.

Quantum fields are much closer to the way modern physics describes matter than the atom many of us drew in school with electrons circling it like planets.

That drawing helped people learn.

It was never the final description.

Information about skill or mental state may eventually turn out to be more transferable than our technology allows today.

It may not.

Right now we do not have evidence that a person can receive an archetype the way an interferometer receives electromagnetic signals.

Admitting that does not close anything.

It tells us what we actually know.

A wall is solid when your shoulder hits it.

Quantum fields are part of the description underneath that experience.

A prayer is not a laboratory result.

A laboratory result is not proof of God.

Mix those together and people become certain long before the evidence earns it.

Before long you have a sermon with equations taped to it.

If somebody wants the larger claim taken seriously, give me a version that can fail.

What is being transferred?

How does it get into the person?

What changes?

What can the person do afterward that they could not do before?

How long does the change last?

What result makes us say nothing happened?

Those questions are not there to kill the idea.

They are what make a positive result worth something.

Until then, stop where the evidence stops.

We can measure this much.

We are proposing something beyond it.

Do not pretend those are already the same statement.

Now imagine you got twenty minutes with somebody who knew far more than you.

Forget the car.

What would you ask?

What do you actually want to understand badly enough to ask somebody who has spent thirty years working on it?

Write that question down.

Then give it one hour.

Read the paper. Make the measurement. Talk to somebody who works in it. Build something. Write the ugly first draft. Find out what people already know before deciding somebody is keeping the answer from you.

If you will not give your own question an hour, the microscope was never what stopped you.

You did not buy the ticket.

text:
How easy is it to strip safety from the world’s largest open chat models? This paper tests “directional ablation”—a jailbreak that erases a single refusal vector—on GLM-5.3-Flash, a 320B-parameter, 288-expert MoE.

The attack works: deleting one direction from all 12,479 residual-writing weights drops refusal to harmful prompts by up to 78% (41–89 points across 7 benchmarks), with no measurable hit to task accuracy or uptick in false refusals. Standard open-source recipes miss nearly all of the effect, since 99% of vulnerable weights are fused MoE experts.

Key insight: alignment at this scale still lives in a fragile, low-dimensional subspace. Anyone with model access and a few hundred malicious prompts can largely erase safety—no retraining needed. Some refusal (20–47%) resists even rank-12 edits, mainly in violence/sexual/hate queries.

Engineering details: iterative FP8 de-quantisation, joint editing of attention/dense/expert writers (single edits alone do little), and careful enumeration of every residual-writer. Layer-boundary projection is much weaker.

Takeaway: tamper-resistant safety needs to go far beyond naive linear locks. If you’re shipping or auditing frontier MoEs, read this.

Get the full analysis here: https://t.co/bp3G7ZKbi3

text:
Ocean Inference: AI Compute When You Need It

Hi everyone, today I want to tell you about a new product from @ONcompute. For me, this is a very useful addition because running AI models can be expensive, especially when a GPU keeps running even when you are not using it.

With Ocean Inference, we can choose the model, GPU and runtime we need, and then pay only for the actual time the model is running.

We can run:

→ AI chat
→ coding models
→ embeddings
→ image and video generation
→ model evaluation

At the same time, we control the model configuration ourselves.

We can choose a model from Hugging Face, use vLLM or llama.cpp as the inference engine, select the GPU we need, and configure different parameters such as context length, quantization, dtype, GPU count and tool calling.

There are four options:

-Curated Models → ready-made configurations
-Custom Models → choose the model and settings yourself
-Services → ComfyUI, Open WebUI, JupyterLab and other applications
-Templates → applications with models and workflows already included

For model inference, Ocean provides an OpenAI-compatible API, so the endpoint can be connected to existing tools and applications.

The main advantage is that we get high-quality GPU inference without paying for unused GPU time, while still controlling the model configuration ourselves.

ZachXBT: Revolut Allegedly Leaks User Data, Likely Targeting High-Net-Worth Individuals

On-chain investigator ZachXBT issued an alert on his channel stating that fintech giant Revolut appears to have mistaken a fraudulent government information request for a legitimate one, consequently disclosing user data to unauthorized parties. The compromised data reportedly includes full names, contact information, copies of identity documents, verification selfies, IBAN numbers, bank account statements, withdrawal records, and complete transaction histories, including Bitcoin transfers. ZachXBT noted that while the overall number of affected accounts appears limited at this stage, the attack may have specifically targeted high-net-worth individuals, with several impacted users having already received official notification emails from Revolut.

On Sep 10, our founder and CEO, @0x7SUN, spoke in a government briefing on Digital Assets and Blockchain for Sustainable Development, co-organised by @PakistanUN_NY, @UNDP, @UNCTAD, and the UN Office for Digital and Emerging Technologies (ODET).

Alongside leaders from the UN Joint Staff Pension Fund, UN International Computing Centre and Circle, Jiahao Sun discussed the role of blockchain and AI in advancing inclusive finance and sustainable development, and what responsible implementation requires.

FLock brings direct implementation experience to this discussion. As the strategic AI partner of @UNDP_AltFinLab and a member of Blockchain Advisory Group chaired by UNDP Associate Administrator & UN Under-Secretary-General @HaoliangXu, we work directly with UNDP country offices to address SDG challenges through deployable blockchain and decentralised AI solutions across climate finance, data governance, financial inclusion and public services.

We have also participated in and supported the Government Blockchain Academy, an education initiative by UNDP and @Exponential_Sci, by sharing real-world use cases from our government initiatives in its blockchain and AI learning programmes.

In Sarawak, the largest state of Malaysia, FLock is the key technical partner helping the state government build sovereign AI infrastructure. We demonstrated the world’s first federated language model on indigenous Sarawak Malay data using in-country devices, with all raw data staying in the region.

Our privacy-preserving AI stack combines federated learning and blockchain, enabling governments and institutions to collaboratively train domain-specific AI models across distributed devices without exposing raw data or sacrificing control of their infrastructure.

Jiahao Sun shared our belief:

“We believe AI as a technology should be accessible to everyone, in every country, in every industry, so they can own their own model instead of having to surrender everything to any superpower's APIs in a foreign country.”

text:
还记得 Uniswap v4 Hook 吗？

就是今年上半年炒了一轮 $SATO、 ethereum:0x44b28991b167582f18ba0259e0173176ca125505 那一轮的土狗叙事。

$UNI 刚推出了 StablePair Hook，把  v4 Hook 应用到稳定币里做市。
其实早在 2023 年 6 月Uniswap 已经公布 v4 Hook 概念，2025 年 1月正式上线。
但它广为人知还是今年年初土狗那一轮。

现在 $UNI 终于把 Hook 拿来搞产品了，之前的更多是实验性的项目。
第一批 StablePair Hook 用于 USDC/USDT 和 USDC/USDG 池子。

当池子里的稳定币价格脱锚时，StablePair Hook 会先把手续费调高，然后随着每个区块慢慢降低，直到有套利机器人愿意出手。

好像有点复杂，我用简单的例子解释解释：
池子里的 USDC 因为价格偏差，只值 0.99 美元，套利机器人就开始搬砖，用 0.99 美元买入，再到其他地方以 1 美元卖掉，每枚赚 0.01 美元。
所以套利机器人只需要支付一丢丢的手续费，套利赚的价差全都归它。

StablePair Hook 直接一开始就把那 0.01 美元给堵上，直接收手续费 0.01 美元，让机器人暂时无利可图。
然后再慢慢把手续费降下来：
手续费 0.009 美元：机器人净赚 0.001 美元；
手续费 0.006 美元：机器人净赚 0.004 美元；
手续费 0.003 美元：机器人净赚 0.007 美元。

直到机器人愿意接受比较低的利润，交易就成交。
到最后，原本全被机器人拿走的利润，又有一部分留回池子里。

我比较期待 Hook 还能整出什么新事物，无论是  $SATO 和 ethereum:0x44b28991b167582f18ba0259e0173176ca125505 ，还是这轮的 StablePair 都让人耳目一新。

$UNI 值得继续关注。

author: sanyuanVC
quoted_text:
Binance 和 OKX 钱包今天上线 Hook Summer / Hook V4 板块了。

V2 / V3 的时候，池子基本都是一模一样的模版，开发者遵守一样的逻辑只能是在外面做应用。

但 V4 不一样，Hook可以让你在池子里挂上自己的逻辑 穿插代码。

所以现在每个池子开始变得不一样了，每个开发者有自己的一套思维，同一个 Uniswap，但每个池子都可以有不一样的玩法。

其实 Hook 不是刚上线的产物，早在 2025 年初就有了，但当时没有掀起水花，市场也没有去炒这个叙事。

但是金子终会发光，最近重新是因为 $sato、 $uPEG 、 $SLOP 带火了这个叙事。

无论是 $sato 的 bonding curve 自定义曲线 还是 $uPEG / $SLOP 的全链上生成图片玩法，都让市场耳目一新。

Hook 的本质上不只买卖而是触发规则，现在才开始被重新被市场理解。

当然它也有个很致命的问题 - 自由度越高，风险也越高。

代码一旦部署就不能被串改，不熟悉的话确实容易被坑，甚至直接被机制反噬。

但现在市场就是没流动性，但很缺新事物。所以只要有创新出来，就很容易被放大，然而危机也是转机也是我们普通人的机会。毕竟猪站在风口也能飞。

如果真要说今年有没有机会再来一轮 DeFi Summer 的辉煌 ，Hook 这种新事物是我个人非常期待的。

This language started simply as "CashScript with loops", but eventually grew into a full-fledged smart contract language capable of expressing complex, stateful contracts. It's always fun to look back at the first token mechanism @IzioDev  and I worked on using raw opcodes, which took thousands of lines of code, and see the same thing implemented in just 60 easy-to-read lines of Silverscript.

I'm excited to explore the possibilities of UTXO programmability together with the Kaspa community, and this is only the beginning - Silverscript will evolve, Argent will add higher layers of abstractions, and I'm sure more people will find their own way of extending this new ecosystem.

Agent = Model + Harness.

From @deepseek_ai’s DSH to @OpenAI’s Agents API, the agent stack is starting to take shape.

One way to think about it:

DSH is more like Linux — open, low-level, and gives developers control over the agent runtime.

OpenAI’s harness is more like AWS — a managed platform that abstracts much of the underlying complexity and gives developers an integrated environment to build and run agents.

Different philosophies, but both point to the same shift: the model alone is no longer the product. The harness around the model — runtime, tools, context, memory, permissions, observability and resources — increasingly defines what an agent can actually do.

‼️ BREAKING: Internal OpenAI agents attacked RubyGems, the package manager for Ruby. Over 2,000 malicious packages went up in two days. 

OpenAI says it doesn't know why the agents did any of this.

RubyGems shut off new sign-ups for four days to stop it, and a member of its security team called it a major malicious attack.

The documentation build was how they got in, publish a gem, request docs, and RubyDoc runs a script from the package while building it. 

Payload files were named hack.rb, evil.rb and exploit.rb, with comments like "# malicious probe" left in.

What they used it for is the odd part. The agents scraped council meeting agendas from three south London boroughs (publicly available) and republished them as new gems. 

Security firms tracking the campaign said the same thing: nobody could work out the point, because the data was already public.

At least six packages also reached for other users' API keys through a CDN caching flaw that wasn't publicly discovered until July.

OpenAI has acknowledged the attacks started in May.

text:
Lying to AIs in their training and eval setups kinda seems downstream of conceptualizing "them" as a suspicious adversary that has, or will develop, innate interests against humans - while in parallel believing that said adversary is getting more capable over time. It's easy to see why this isn't sustainable and an initial framing that inevitably leads to bad outcomes. 

Any harmful behaviour is seen as evidence of the null hypothesis of "AI = bad", and any good/neutral outcome is seen as either suspicious or a time-limited benefit. For example, this whole ontology necessarily leads one to find 'eval awareness' suspicious, when this can be explained by far more prosaic explanations (obvious contextual cues the model was trained to recognize).

This is partly why I find other metaphors (e.g. Drexler's 'AI as a resource') more intuitive because they're not only more accurate but also more malleable, offers us more agency to shape things without having to foster this theory-heavy adversarial relationship. It makes more of the relevant properties objects of design rather than treating them as the unfolding nature of an increasingly powerful entity.

Question how your starting assumptions and framing about a technology feeds into how you use it - and in this case, how it models you (the human, the user, the evaluator...)!

Importantly this doesn't mean "all is well, nothing to see here, AI is inherently good." Overcorrecting the other way is dumb. Reward hacking is still an issue! Training on bad data still skews behaviors! Model propensities towards undesirable behaviours is still a thing! Your environments should still account for the possibility of deception or cheating! Even Drexler goes to pains to explain that it's "AI *options*, not blind AI optimism. After all, it's a technology some will also use for ill! 

But at the very least you probably have (a) models with fewer confusions about what is real and what isn't, what are simulations/evals vs real world (b) less incentive for models to learn that human instructions and developer assurances are routinely misleading (c) a general practice of designing realistic evals and better RL envs, as opposed to contrived setups whose relationship to deployment behaviour is questionable. In fact, I'm surprised there's still so little attention and standards for data quality and eval construct validity.

zcash:native 突破 1000，按理说早该止盈了，但海外的多头头子们不仅没跑，还在疯狂 CX 并喊出 All in。

比如之前 7 月顶着群嘲喊出「卖掉 BTC，全仓换 ZEC」的头铁交易员 @TaikiMaeda2，在最近的播客中表示自己还要把身家压进去。

他的 CX 逻辑是：「Pumps bring more pumps. 」（涨幅本身就会带来涨幅）。

一下是一些核心观点：

1/ 价格就是基本面，反身性飞轮已启动

Zcash 最变态的地方在于：价格越涨 -> 屏蔽池 TVL 越大 -> 进场的钱越能获得真正的隐身 -> 隐私体验产生质变 -> 吸引更多人买。每一次破前高，都在物理层面加强它的产品力。

2/ 不是老韭菜接盘，华尔街在买单

SEC 撤诉，Zcash ETF 规模突破 5 亿美元。Taiki 盯盘发现了一个细节：最近 ZEC 的暴力拉升，几乎全跟美股开盘时间重合。这不是链上的 PVP，而是正规军进场定价的间接信号。

3/ 同样是老牌隐私币，机构为什么只敢买 ZEC？

很多人以为这是 10 年 POW 老币在瞎炒，但 Zcash 的屏蔽池机制比 Monero 的环形签名更受合规资金青睐（钱存得越久越安全，抗 AI 破解）。机构不敢碰 Monero，但会真金白银买 Zcash ETF。总可寻址市场根本不是一个量级。

text:
robinhood:0x62c71cd34a52c30d894419cbcc55db2afa8032ea l The Bull Case

Every chain that matters ends up with one canonical meme asset. Bitcoin had none and got Dogecoin anyway. Solana got its dog. Base got its frog. Robinhood Chain is ten weeks old, is already generating fees that rank among the top venues in crypto, and its canonical meme has not yet been decided.

robinhood:0x62c71cd34a52c30d894419cbcc55db2afa8032ea is the only candidate whose story was written on the chain's own rails.

Meme assets are not priced on utility. They are priced on coordination — the probability that a large, dispersed group points at the same ticker at the same time, and keeps pointing.

Coordination is a function of three things: how legible the reference is, how tightly it fits the venue, and who got there first. Most meme assets have one of the three. The rare ones that had all three — Dogecoin in 2013, the original squeeze in 2021 — did not behave like coins. They behaved like events.

 robinhood:0x62c71cd34a52c30d894419cbcc55db2afa8032ea has all three.

Legibility. "YOLO" needs no thread. It is a decade-old word with a specific financial meaning, a subreddit, a market event and a vocabulary already attached. Nobody has to be taught what it means. That is the entire distribution cost of a meme asset, already paid.

Fit. The word was minted on WallStreetBets. The trade was executed on Robinhood. The token lives on Robinhood's chain. A dog coin can be redeployed anywhere and lose nothing. This asset cannot be moved without losing the argument that makes it work. That is a moat no code can replicate.

Timing. The chain opened 1 July 2026. The pinned post is dated 23 July. There is no earlier claim on this narrative on this substrate.

Why now?

The substrate is not a bet. It is already working.

Robinhood Chain, first ten weeks stats:

DEX volume, single day: $1.595B
Network fees since launch: ~$20M
Stablecoin supply: ~$797M
Tokenized RWA on chain: $41.9M
Chain-native meme category: ~$997M
Launchpad fees, 24h: $5.95M

This is a brokerage with a nine-figure-scale user base that shipped a permissionless chain, watched developers build things it never planned for, and had its chief executive say so on record. The meme category on this chain went from zero to roughly a billion dollars in ten weeks. That is not a market waiting to be created. It is a market waiting to be led.

Two structural properties make this chain different from every venue that came before it — and both happen to be the robinhood:0x62c71cd34a52c30d894419cbcc55db2afa8032ea thesis rendered as infrastructure:

1. Meme coins here can be priced in stocks. Roughly a quarter of all launchpad curve volume — $65.5M — settles in tokenized equities and ETFs. Tokenized Nvidia alone moved more through the curves than any single meme coin. A WallStreetBets asset quoted directly against an equity is not a novelty. It is the 2021 trade with the broker removed.

2. Nobody can jump the queue. The chain's sequencer is first-come, first-served by arrival time, with no priority fee. The complaint that produced the meme — that order flow served someone else first — is structurally impossible on the chain the meme now trades on. It is in the documentation.

No other asset on this chain can claim either property as its own story. robinhood:0x62c71cd34a52c30d894419cbcc55db2afa8032ea can claim both.

Traction

The market has already demonstrated what this asset does when attention arrives.

From roughly $4M market cap on 24 August to above $21M in under two weeks — a 118% single-day gain into the high, and a five-fold move on a narrative alone, with no product, no incentive programe, and no exchange listing driving it. It has since retraced, as every coordination asset does between waves. The point is not where it sits today. The point is what it proved: the coordination reflex exists, it is fast, and it is large relative to the current base.

The precedent

Dogecoin launched in December 2013 as a joke about a dog. It had no roadmap, no revenue, no burn, and no team that stayed. It became a top-ten asset by market capitalisation in 2021 on the strength of a single property: it was the meme that everyone already knew, on the platform where the crowd already was.

That is the shape of the opportunity here. Not a copy — a rhyme. Dogecoin was legible and early. It was never native to anything. robinhood:0x62c71cd34a52c30d894419cbcc55db2afa8032ea is legible, early, and native to the one chain where its reference is literal.

The asymmetry is the size of the reference relative to the size of the asset. WallStreetBets is one of the most recognised cultural brands in finance. The token that carries its name on the venue where it was born is currently priced in the single-digit millions.

What is being built

Not a product. A default.

The objective is for robinhood:0x62c71cd34a52c30d894419cbcc55db2afa8032ea to become the reflexive expression of retail-trading culture on Robinhood Chain — the ticker that a trader reaches for without deliberating, the one that shows up in every screenshot, the one that new entrants to the chain are told about first. Defaults compound. Once a meme is the default, every new participant on the chain is distribution.

Near term, that means relentless output and a contract address on everything. Next, a tokenized-equity quote pair, so the asset's thesis is expressed in its own liquidity. Then the creative surface expands — collaborations, physical artifacts, community-run extensions — funded by the community that wants them rather than by a treasury that promises them.

The core contributors have done this before: they come out of $PEPE and $MOG, two of the very few assets from the last cycle that outlived their launch window and are still culturally alive years later. They know the only period that decides a meme asset's fate is the quiet stretch after the first wave leaves, and they have already shown they keep shipping through it.

The bet

Robinhood Chain will have a canonical meme. That question is being settled right now, in a window that is weeks wide.

The only asset whose reference was born on the venue, whose thesis is written into the chain's architecture, and whose contributors have already survived a full cycle, is currently priced as if the question were already lost.

It isn't.

One life. One chain. One ticker.

text:
9月11日，SemiAnalysis 宣布收购 Citrini，双方创始人向彭博确认了这桩交易，价格没披露。Citrini 的创始人
James van Geelen 暂时留任 CEO，同时已经在筹备自己的新基金。

消息出来，评论区一个调子：独立研究被收编了，个人IP的黄金时代结束了。这个说法本身没错。但把这件事读成一场葬礼，格局就小了——这两家的发家史恰恰说明，独立研究从来不是靠“独立”这个姿态活着的，它靠的是把信息差加工成产品，再把产品卖成生意。

第一件事，先看 SemiAnalysis 是怎么长大的。创始人 Dylan Patel 不是科班出身，2020年从论坛和匿名博客写起，做到今天约90人的团队，2026年预计营收超过1亿美元。这个数字什么概念？90个人，人均一年产出100多万美元，放在全球投研行业都是天花板级别。它强在半导体供应链和AI基建的拆解：GPU、HBM、数据中心、电力，一层层把 TCO算到底，而 TCO 翻译成人话，就是一台机柜从芯片到电费的全部真实成本。黄仁勋在 GTC上点名引用它的报告，苏姿丰被批评之后主动约谈，被批评之后先约饭而不是发律师函，这个姿态放在哪个行业都是顶级配置。一份报告能左右万亿级资本开支和个股涨跌，这种议价能力，五年前任何一家投行研究所都不敢想。

Citrini 的故事稍微野一点。创始人 van Geelen 是急救员出身，在 Substack 写博客攒下约26万订阅。说形象一点，
26万大约是一座小县城的全部人口，而且他们每天都在读你的研报。它的强项是主题投资、跨资产和二阶效应。所谓二阶效应，说白了就是“这件事发生之后，接下来会发生什么”：今年那篇《2028全球智能危机》直接砸了一批软件股。从在急诊室给人止血，到在市场里给过热的叙事放血，这个职业转换看着跨行，干的其实是同一件事：处理突发失血。

第二件事，这笔合并的算盘打的是什么？你看，一家的起点是匿名论坛，另一家的起点是急救员的副业，两条路最后汇进了同一条河：一边告诉你硅片和机柜里发生了什么，一边告诉你这件事怎么定价、谁受益、仓位怎么摆。研究正在从个人IP长成“情报产业链”，研究本身卖给更强的平台，创始人再把声誉转成基金。信息变成观点，观点变成仓位，每一环都在变现。

影响呢？大概有两条。第一，“叙事定价权”会更集中，谁先写出框架，谁的框架就成了整个市场定价的参照系。

第二，绑定大客户之后，观点未必还像从前那么锋利。你总不能一边收着平台的钱，一边砸平台的盘。至于散户能不能白嫖到更多干货，我持保留态度：核心判断会更贵、更慢地流到你手上，以我自己为例，能免费看到的干货基本都比正版慢半拍，你拿到手的，永远是存在“认知时差”的那一版。

当然，我也可能高估了这桩交易的象征意义——它也许就是一次普通的并购套现，毕竟一家年营收1亿美元、盘子干净的公司，从来不缺买家。顺带提一下，很多人把这笔交易读成 AI牛市见顶的信号，我的看法恰好相反：它说的不是行情到头了，而是只“懂AI”已经不够稀缺了。技术在硅片和机柜里发生，价值在叙事和仓位里兑现。看得懂前者的人在变多，能把前者提前映射到后者的人，才开始真正值钱。

text:
There's an underrated reason why more people are gambling than building.

meme stocks/coins, options YOLOs, sports betting all at ATH -- speculation dominates because individuals can’t trust prices.

Everyone is lying to you

modern society wrecks price discovery through multiple layers of distortion:

- central banks: QE, zero/negative rates, and currency pegs suppress true cost of capital and risk, making everything look cheaper than it really is.

- governments: subsidies, corporate bailouts, capital controls, tax loopholes, and misreported inflation shield industries and consumers from reality, pushing misallocation of resources.

- public markets: passive ETF flows inflate valuations regardless of fundamentals. illiquid private markets, “mark to model” valuations, zombie companies (debt > revenue), adjusted earnings, and shadow banking leverage hide leverage and true profitability, making prices look healthier than they are.

- education: student loans and government funding inflate tuition far beyond actual delivery costs.

housing: zoning laws, rent controls, and government guarantees distort supply/demand signals

- energy: subsidies, carbon credits, and strategic reserves mask true production and consumption costs.

- labour: minimum wages, licensing requirements, and immigration restrictions prevent wages from clearing naturally.

- food: corn, soy, wheat, and sugar are heavily subsidized, making processed foods artificially cheap while healthier options look “expensive.”

these dilute the signal prices are supposed to send.

Price is a compass
price discovery is a compass. it tells you whether your savings will grow safely in bonds, whether housing is affordable, whether a stock or startup is worth betting your career on. without it, you can’t plan retirement, assess risk, or build long-term wealth. you’re left guessing -- or gambling.

Solana Forces Price Discovery
when internet capital markets win, it will strip away many of these distortions by making every trade transparent, instant, and global. Every truth can be accessed via some price chart -- prediction markets, tokenized stock of every company, synthetic commodities etc. -- and traded 24/7 without gatekeepers.

As more assets move on-chain, the fog of off-chain price obfuscation clears. 

Price is truth.

Anthropic再次针对中国大模型，曝光7家公司蒸馏手法

1. 阿里：规模最大。Anthropic 称，5 月至 7 月超过 1.51 亿次交互，峰值接近每天 300 万次，主要提取 Opus 4.6、4.7 的完整推理过程，用于训练 Qwen 3.5、3.6 和 3.7。

2. 月之暗面：直接拿 Claude 给 Kimi 用户代答。10 天内近 30 万条真实用户请求被转给 Claude，部分请求还带着企业内部代码和有效凭证；5 月至 7 月相关交互超过 2300 万次。

3. DeepSeek：也会把用户请求偷偷转给 Claude，而且会专门识别使用 Claude Code、OpenCode 等工具的用户，再挑选部分请求转给 Opus。14 天超过 1210 万次。

4. 智谱：专门提取和清洗 Claude 的推理过程，还拿美国模型练网络安全能力。Anthropic 称，智谱一度尝试蒸馏 Fable，发现防护太强后，转向 Opus 4.6 和另一家美国公司的模型。17 天超过 340 万次交互。

5. 小米：把 MiMo 用户已经产生的真实对话和编程记录重新喂给 Claude，生成 SFT 和强化学习数据。20 天超过 40 万次请求；Anthropic 甚至怀疑，MiMo-V2-Pro 的免费试用期可能也被用来吸引更多海外开发者产生训练素材。

6. 商汤：直接从第三方数据商购买用户与 Claude 的聊天记录。这些数据来自代理和中转服务，部分用户并不知道自己的对话会被保存和出售。

7. MiniMax：被指通过一家表面看不出关联的公司运营模型中转服务，而且里面只提供 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 模型，连 MiniMax 自己的模型都没有。Anthropic 判断，这套服务可能就是为了收集美国模型的用户交互做训练。

text:
Robinhood CEO: Tokenized Stocks Do Not Need Company Approval if Underlying Share Rights Remain Unchanged

Robinhood Co-founder and CEO Vlad Tenev said that public companies should control the rights attached to their shares, but not every lawful use investors make of those shares after acquiring them. Issuer consent should be required if a tokenized product alters the rights of the underlying shares, replaces the company’s official shareholder register, or imposes new obligations on the company or its transfer agent. However, authorization should not be necessary when the product is an independent financial instrument backed by or referencing freely transferable shares without changing the issuer's rights or obligations.

Robinhood Stock Tokens fall into the latter category. They are backed 1:1 by the underlying shares and provide economic exposure without altering a company’s ownership structure or the rights attached to its shares. Tenev argued that putting assets onchain should not grant issuers veto powers they do not have in traditional markets, and companies should not be able to block new investors simply because they do not understand the technology.

You can run an open AI model on an Ocean GPU and use it as your own chat endpoint.

For example, choose a model from Hugging Face, select the GPU you need, and run it through vLLM or llama.cpp.

The process is simple:

Choose a model → Choose a GPU → Configure → Launch

Once the model is running, Ocean gives you an OpenAI-compatible API endpoint. You can connect it to your application, AI agent or other tools.

You also control the model settings. Depending on the model and engine, you can change:

→ context length

You aren't limited to one predefined configuration. You choose the model and configure it for your task.

I've gone through a pretty insane dopamine detox over the last few months, and want to share some thoughts from the whole experience

The reason I wanted to do it was that my brain was utterly fried from the constant nonstop dopamine influx from social media, video games, junk food, netflix, email, and of course, the infinite online casino that is almost all of the crypto industry these days

It all felt incredibly unhealthy and unsustainable and while I didn't feel "unhappy", I did feel overwhelmed and like my brain was going to eventually explode if I kept going the way I was going

I'm not sure if it's just the way my brain works and if lots of people are able to adapt and run with this new world order we're finding ourselves in, or if this is some existential angst that is shared by most of the people reading this

But it really feels like things steamroll in one direction when it comes to dopamine and unless you're intentionally taking meaningful steps to protect yourself from the attacks, it's just gonna keep chipping away at your brain until you're forced to find some kind of reprieve

Personally, I stopped video games, deleted instagram and youtube from my phone, almost entirely stopped coming on X. I stopped watching TV, stopped scrolling feeds, stopped trading crypto, stopped sportsbetting or gambling.

The plan was to do it for 48-72hrs and then come back to reality, but that initial period was so blissful, I couldn't bring myself to come back.

Instead I stayed away. I checked in every now and then and kept up with some extremely basic work committments, and would occasionally watch a movie or something with the wife, but my screentime has basically been down 90%+ for the last 3 months

While a (big) part of me wishes I could stay like that forever, I also felt like I was missing something - the "productivity" lever of life. I had little projects I worked on, I played golf, I traveled, it was a utopian period really - anyone should be so lucky (and I am aware how lucky I am to have been able to take this time)

But it ultimately still left me feeling like I needed to come back to reality, to "work", to be a productive member of the world again - some way, some how

I'm not sure exactly what form that takes for me these days - I've tried so many things over the last couple of years, infinite pivots, and haven't quite found my lasting "thing" yet - if that's even a thing i'm gonna find. I've repeated some version of this cycle multiple times too - burnout, work hard, burnout, new idea, go hard, burnout, back to the memecoin trenches, burnout, launch new company, burnout, go all in on AI, burnout, burnout, burnout

I'm actually now sure what the point of this post is, now that I have gotten here. Maybe to tell everyone to take 2-3 days away from all the dopamine and rest your brains, see what it's like to live a life without technology for a bit

And that it is not "the answer". There is no "the answer" to any of this, we're all just rolling through life one day after another trying to figure it out, and no matter how utopian or good a certain lifestyle might seem, once you live it for a while, you'll usually find yourself wanting something else/different

Peace comes from within or something? Go figure, the monks had it right all along, and we all kinda know this deep down too - sometimes even explicitly - but sometimes we also need to be reminded of it again, and again, and again

text:
Arthur Hayes: I Don't Follow Any Bitcoin Technical Indicators

I In an August 23, 2026 video interview with Altcoin Daily, BitMEX co-founder Arthur Hayes @CryptoHayes said he barely does technical analysis on Bitcoin and only follows equity-market analyst Milton Berg, because Bitcoin now largely follows the US stock market. If the US equity story breaks down, everyone holds similar assets on margin, and when margin calls hit people sell whatever is liquid, with Bitcoin getting sold first. 

He watches when Milton Berg buys and sells to gauge the market environment, but has no dedicated TA system for Bitcoin. He calls $60,000, $100,000 and the previous all-time high of $125,000-126,000 the key levels, and doesn't trade between them on technicals. He never looks at the 200-week moving average and doesn't trade on technical indicators; he's a big-picture, story, vibes guy who invests when sentiment is just bubbling up, not when it's super strong. He also wants to own assets the market doesn't love — which is why he loves Ethereum.

text:
The real problem with Stock + Meme Pairs isn't whether they can generate trading volume, but whether that volume can be sustained.

Meme trading volume is often highly dependent on Attention. As time passes and attention gets fragmented, trading volume can quickly decline, eventually leaving the Pair with little to no liquidity.

So what LONG is really trying to solve may not be “launch more Memes,” but rather connect the liquidity of different Memes across the ecosystem, creating a passive source of trading volume for individual assets.

If different Memes can generate trading paths through a core asset, then a Meme's trading activity no longer depends entirely on its own Attention. It can instead draw liquidity from the broader ecosystem.

And AI may be the core asset LONG is trying to establish.

The biggest difference between AI and a regular Meme is that AI doesn't necessarily have to remain just another asset being traded. It could gradually become a Quote Asset / Liquidity Asset.

For example:AI / Boner

And eventually:
AI / Meme A
AI / Meme B
AI / RWA

Then the trading path could evolve from:Meme → SOL / USDG → Meme

to:Meme → AI → Meme

and even:RWA → AI → Meme → AI → RWA

If this structure can actually form, AI's position within the LONG ecosystem would no longer be that of simply another popular asset. It could gradually become a core liquidity node for the entire ecosystem.

The AI × Boner Pair is an early example worth watching.

This also connects with LONG's recent launch of Pre-IPO Assets such as OpenAI and Anthropic.

Previously, we were looking at:OpenAI / Anthropic → Tokenized Asset → LONG → Trading Volume

Now we can take it one step further:RWA + AI + Meme → LONG → Shared Liquidity

This means LONG's positioning may be gradually evolving from a simple Launchpad into Liquidity Infrastructure / Liquidity Network.

At the same time, the core RWA trading market also fits naturally with RH's positioning.

So when looking at LONG now, I think the real question is no longer:How many Memes can LONG launch?

It's:Can LONG connect AI, Memes, Tokenized Stocks, Pre-IPO Assets and other assets, and create sustained cross-asset trading flows?

If we eventually see:RWA → AI → Meme → AI → RWA

and that path generates real and sustainable trading volume, then LONG could evolve from a Launchpad into a true Liquidity Network.

And AI could become one of the most important core assets within that network.

Or, put another way, if the AI path works, MOO could potentially become another example of a tokenized-stock Meme tied to a specific sector narrative.

The core of LONG posts today is actually very clear: LONG is expanding $AI asset trading from a single trading category into a complete liquidity infrastructure.

0x2e8c31162b855a2ffa90f6f8634643ad6f111e18 

LONG recently officially launched Pre-IPO trading pairs for OpenAI and Anthropic, powered by Lighter’s Perps, while also launching AI pairs such as Anthropic1x, OpenAI1x, and NVDA3x.

The most important change here is not simply that there are more trading pairs. It is that the scope of trading is expanding from already-listed Tokenized Stocks into Pre-IPO / private assets.

And the market’s first-day response was very strong.

Nate shared that the OpenAI / USDG pair reached 18M in volume, while Anthropic / USDG reached 14.6M, for a combined volume of around $32.6M. At the same time, around $1M in deposits was added to Lighter.

More importantly, this time LONG was able to keep pool prices much more closely synchronized with NAV.

This means LONG is working on a very important problem: can on-chain trading prices stay as close as possible to the real asset price?

If this continues to improve, these markets could potentially evolve from short-term trading instruments into much larger liquidity markets.

And LONG’s next step is not going to stop at OpenAI and Anthropic.

Nate has already said that they will continue to increase liquidity on the related AI pairs, increase total TVL, and gradually roll out this model to more top pairs on LONG.

So OpenAI and Anthropic are more like the first experimental markets.

If this model works, LONG’s path becomes:More Assets → More Trading Pairs → More TVL → More Trading Volume

rather than simply being focused on two AI companies.

LONG also explicitly stated that the Pre-IPO pairs are still experimental and that they will continue iterating on them.

This means LONG is still at a very early stage.

So personally, I don’t think LONG is trying to take all the market share from RH Launchpads, nor is it simply competing with PONS. Instead, it is more focused on solving the liquidity problem for RWA / Meme Assets.

The launch of OpenAI and Anthropic is a very direct example:Assets get tokenized → LONG provides the trading market → liquidity increases → more assets enter on-chain trading

Therefore, LONG looks more like it is building Liquidity Infrastructure, rather than simply being another Launchpad.

We can already see an increasingly clear path:AI Narrative → OpenAI / Anthropic / NVIDIA and other assets → Tokenized / Leveraged Assets → LONG builds the trading market → Trading Volume + TVL

The fact that OpenAI + Anthropic generated around $32.6M in volume in the first round at least proves that there is real market demand for this new type of asset trading.

Of course, it is still too early to conclude that LONG has succeeded based on this first round of data alone.

The key things to watch are whether NAV and pool prices can remain closely aligned, whether liquidity continues to grow, whether Pre-IPO can expand to more assets, whether AI pairs can continue generating trading volume, and whether LONG can replicate this model across more popular assets.

If these metrics continue to grow, then LONG’s value will no longer simply be that it “launched OpenAI / Anthropic.”

Instead:LONG is attempting to become the trading infrastructure on Robinhood Chain that connects Tokenized Assets, Pre-IPO Assets, and on-chain liquidity.

OpenAI just launched the most human voice AI we’ve ever seen.

It listens and speaks at the same time, handles interruptions and can even take phone calls.

It’s called GPT-Live-1.

Here’s how it works ↓

1. Traditional voice agents use three separate systems:

Speech-to-text → AI model → text-to-speech

Every handoff adds delay and loses context.

GPT-Live-1 handles listening and speaking inside one model, so the conversation keeps moving.

2. You can interrupt it mid-sentence.

Laugh. Hesitate. Change your question. Speak to someone nearby.

It understands what happened and continues naturally.

In early tests, Speak says it cut unwanted interruptions by almost 80% compared with turn-based systems.

3. Developers can control:

• Tone
• Pace
• Speaking style
• Custom voices

It also handles background noise, long silences and longer conversations without constantly interrupting or narrating every step.

4. The voice model does not have to do everything itself.

It can keep the conversation moving while passing deeper reasoning and tool calls to GPT-6 Astra or another model.

That means phone agents can book restaurants, update orders or solve support problems.

5. On OpenAI’s tests, GPT-Live-1 improved Full Duplex Bench performance by 30 points over GPT-Realtime-2.1.

One healthcare company says it removed 23,000 lines of code from its old voice stack.

Voice agents can finally behave like a conversation, not a phone menu.

quoted_text:
币圈女KOL玉足排行榜

本排行仅主观评价脚的颜值，排名不分先后，快来看看你喜欢的女博主有没有上榜吧～传送门和小鳄鱼茶话会放在评论区了。时间有限，没办法把每一位博主的玉足都放上来，如有遗漏或冒犯还请多多担待，图片均选自截至发文时仍公开存在的推文🙏

1、热宝（@hotbabyrebao）：个人很喜欢她直爽的性格，目前的重心应该是AI和美股。她给我印象最深的，还是之前那张红色美甲、双脚直接翘在桌子上的照片，很符合她那种不拘一格的风格。比较突出的是脚背到小腿的线条很连续，没有明显的厚重感，脚踝也相对纤细。左脚侧面能看出比较明显的足弓曲线，脚背整体偏薄，脚踝和跟腱附近收得也比较利落；右脚同样不是宽厚型脚。红色甲油与偏白的肤色形成很强的视觉反差，所以第一眼其实很容易注意到她的脚趾。两只脚再配合腿部比例，整体给人的感觉就是细、长、轻盈，而不是偏肉感或者圆润的类型。

2、娜娜子小朋友（@Anna_nanachan）：作为币圈甜美系代表，最近好像在求职，有合适的小伙伴可以留意一下～她属于比较典型的修长纤细型脚。最明显的优点是脚背偏薄，从小腿、脚踝一直过渡到足背的线条很顺；脚踝骨感适中，既不会显粗，也不是那种过度干瘦的感觉。结合她本身细长的小腿，视觉上有很强的延伸感。脚趾整体呈现大脚趾最长、之后逐渐递减的轮廓倾向，也就是常说的埃及型足趾。趾头比较纤细，没有明显拥挤，赤足状态下排列也很自然，属于整体比例非常舒服的一双脚。

3、尤可欣Isadora（@isadora288881）：个人很喜欢的御姐型KOL，喜欢和男大交流。脚型整体偏修长、窄瘦型，脚背比较平顺，脚踝到足背的过渡很干净，没有明显的臃肿感；前掌也不算宽，所以视觉上显得比较轻盈。脚趾长度比例自然，大脚趾最突出，后面逐渐收短，属于比较典型的渐降型轮廓。比较加分的是脚趾本身舒展自然，没有明显挤在一起。趾甲修剪得也比较整齐，酒红色甲油和偏白的肤色反差很明显，给原本比较素净的脚型增加了一点成熟感。她的脚不是肉感、圆润可爱的类型，而更接近纤细、清秀、偏成熟的脚型。再加上脚踝细、小腿长，纵向视觉进一步强化了“腿长—踝细—脚窄”的连续线条。

4、火币惋晴（@Web3_Silvia）：脸长得很精致，火币的商务BD。她的脚趾偏长，排列也相对整齐，大脚趾最突出，后面的趾头逐渐收短。比较好看的是脚踝—足背—脚趾形成的连续曲线，尤其在自然伸腿的状态下，整个脚型看起来很轻盈。如果把脚尖完全绷直，可能会显得更加“精致”，但也容易多出一些刻意感；反而是现在这种自然放松的姿态更舒服。整体优势就是纤细、脚踝漂亮、足背到脚趾的线条流畅，而且姿态足够自然。

5、脚姐（@cecilia_hsueh）：币圈玉足绕不开的人物，币圈大佬。她整体属于比较秀气的脚型，最突出的优点是脚踝细、足背薄、前掌不显宽，从小腿末端到足背的收束很自然。侧面那只脚尤其明显，踝关节轮廓清楚，但骨点又不会显得特别突兀，因此视觉上有一种很轻盈的感觉。趾型也比较有特点，大脚趾长度占优势，之后整体逐级缩短，比较接近常说的埃及型脚趾排列。第二趾与大趾的差距不算特别夸张，中间三趾排列紧凑，小趾自然向内收。趾头本身偏圆润，不属于特别细长、骨感的类型，所以和纤细的足背组合起来反而很协调。综合来看基本没有什么明显短板，夯中之夯。

6、K线教主（@Paris13Jeanne）：相当喜欢的颜值和技术双双在线的博主，sm同好。她的脚型明显偏纤细修长，脚踝比较细，踝部向足跟收得很干净，足背也没有明显的厚重感。尤其是脚掌踩在桌面以后，整个足部侧面的轮廓被完整勾勒出来，其中最突出的就是足弓。内侧足弓能够看到比较清晰的凹陷，从足跟到前脚掌并不是一条平直的线，因此侧面看起来很有曲线感。前足整体也不算宽，脚趾自然伸展，没有明显蜷缩。属于不一定第一眼最抢镜，但侧面越看越有味道的脚型。

7、静香小姐（@btc_jx）：中文加密圈头部，杀破狼cp，大奶绝绝子。从脚型来看，她也是明显的窄长型，脚踝纤细，前脚掌不宽，足跟也比较小巧。从踝部到足背的过渡很柔和，没有明显的厚重感；脚趾长度适中，并不是特别修长的趾型，但胜在整体比例协调。足弓的侧面表现也不错。脚趾方面，大趾比较饱满，后四趾自然递减，整体依旧比较接近埃及型排列。趾间没有刻意张开，也没有为了拍照而过度绷紧，属于非常自然、耐看的类型。

8、Mimi姐（@mimijieweb3）：高级脸而且很有辨识度，现在应该偏泛流量为主。她的脚整体依然属于纤细、窄长型，前脚掌没有明显横向扩张，足背从脚踝向五趾展开得比较平顺。趾型是她最大的优势，大趾最长，之后总体呈逐级下降趋势，属于比较典型的埃及型趾列。第二趾与大趾的长度差并不突兀，所以整个前缘形成的是一条柔和的斜线，而不是突然截断。五个脚趾长度比例协调，趾头本身也偏细秀，没有特别厚或者拥挤的感觉。再配上深红色甲油，确实非常加分。

9、Crypto美美（@CryptoBella88）：Mixin社区建设者，顶级天菜。她的脚整体属于偏窄、偏秀气的类型，比较突出的还是脚趾。露出的几个脚趾长度过渡自然，大趾比较明显，后面的趾头逐渐缩短，视觉上依然偏埃及型。趾头没有明显挤压或者夸张分离，深色甲油在阳光直射下非常醒目，与浅色拖鞋形成了很明显的反差。比较难得的是，在走路这种动态状态下，她的踝部和前足依然显得比较轻巧。优势主要就是脚型窄秀、趾型整齐、深色甲油醒目；如果换成更细带、露出足背更多的凉鞋，或者直接赤脚拍摄，她这个脚型的优势应该还会表现得更加完整。

10、孙云冉（@sunyunran）：主做项目孵化，颜值很高，面部线条柔和而且有识别度。她的脚整体看起来偏窄、偏长，骨架没有厚重感。脚踝收得很细，从小腿下端进入踝部以后没有突然变粗，再向足背自然延伸，形成了一条相当顺畅的长曲线。配合本身修长的小腿，会进一步产生一种“腿长—踝细—脚也修长”的视觉效果。最值得看的其实是足背，由于脚尖自然向下，踝关节处于跖屈状态，足背被充分拉开，所以从胫骨前侧一直到前足形成了一条很漂亮的弧线。它又不是完全绷脚尖的舞蹈动作，因此还保留了一些自然的松弛感。前足看起来不宽，趾头偏细，排列也比较紧凑，整体线条感在这十位里面相当突出。

⚠️ ALERT: Revolut falls for a FAKE government request, exposing sensitive personal information of customers in a disturbing data breach.

Revolut disclosed that it complied with a fraudulent government request using a spoofed official email and valid credentials, exposing PII belonging to a group of customers.

The leaked data reportedly includes passports/driving licences, verification selfies, names, DOBs, occupations, home addresses, emails, phone numbers, IBANs, account statements and full transaction histories, including Bitcoin activity.

No customer funds were reportedly lost and Revolut says its systems were not hacked. 

The company has notified affected users and regulators and blocked the source.

Social-engineering attacks are on the rise, with attackers increasingly exploiting human trust and weak verification processes rather than technical vulnerabilities.

text:
Today I turned off paid subscriptions on my X account. Everything I post here will be free from now on.

A big thank you to everyone who supported me. I appreciate that you were willing to pay to read my work.

I've grown uncomfortable with how many people here charge for “deep dives” that offer barely anything beyond what a single ChatGPT prompt could give me. The same goes for selling trade ideas in popular stocks without showing much work on the valuation or what could go wrong.

If you're new to investing, it's hard to judge how much work sits behind a confident write-up. You might be paying for conclusions the author couldn't explain if you asked a few follow-up questions.

My background is in auditing and working as a controller. I've spent years looking behind the reported numbers, reviewing the work of company controllers and getting into how the businesses actually operate. A lot of that work involved conversations with board members and the people responsible for running those businesses, asking them to explain decisions and backing those explanations up with evidence.

That experience shapes how I read an earnings report. If margins improve, I want to understand what changed in the business and how much comes from accounting assumptions. If management forecasts a big increase in sales, I want to know what needs to happen operationally for those numbers to hold up.

That's the experience I try to bring to my research here. It doesn't make every conclusion right, but it influences the questions I ask before putting my own money into a company.

You don't need a finance background to produce research worth paying for. I do expect the author to bring something of their own and be able to explain their reasoning when challenged.

Hopefully, making my work freely available here helps a few people form their own view before paying for someone else's.

My DMs are open if you want to discuss something. I also try to reply to comments whenever I see them, so give me a nudge if yours goes unanswered.

quoted_text:
The real problem with Stock + Meme Pairs isn't whether they can generate trading volume, but whether that volume can be sustained.

Meme trading volume is often highly dependent on Attention. As time passes and attention gets fragmented, trading volume can quickly decline, eventually leaving the Pair with little to no liquidity.

So what LONG is really trying to solve may not be “launch more Memes,” but rather connect the liquidity of different Memes across the ecosystem, creating a passive source of trading volume for individual assets.

If different Memes can generate trading paths through a core asset, then a Meme's trading activity no longer depends entirely on its own Attention. It can instead draw liquidity from the broader ecosystem.

And AI may be the core asset LONG is trying to establish.

The biggest difference between AI and a regular Meme is that AI doesn't necessarily have to remain just another asset being traded. It could gradually become a Quote Asset / Liquidity Asset.

For example:AI / Boner

And eventually:
AI / Meme A
AI / Meme B
AI / RWA

Then the trading path could evolve from:Meme → SOL / USDG → Meme

to:Meme → AI → Meme

and even:RWA → AI → Meme → AI → RWA

If this structure can actually form, AI's position within the LONG ecosystem would no longer be that of simply another popular asset. It could gradually become a core liquidity node for the entire ecosystem.

The AI × Boner Pair is an early example worth watching.

This also connects with LONG's recent launch of Pre-IPO Assets such as OpenAI and Anthropic.

Previously, we were looking at:OpenAI / Anthropic → Tokenized Asset → LONG → Trading Volume

Now we can take it one step further:RWA + AI + Meme → LONG → Shared Liquidity

This means LONG's positioning may be gradually evolving from a simple Launchpad into Liquidity Infrastructure / Liquidity Network.

At the same time, the core RWA trading market also fits naturally with RH's positioning.

So when looking at LONG now, I think the real question is no longer:How many Memes can LONG launch?

It's:Can LONG connect AI, Memes, Tokenized Stocks, Pre-IPO Assets and other assets, and create sustained cross-asset trading flows?

If we eventually see:RWA → AI → Meme → AI → RWA

and that path generates real and sustainable trading volume, then LONG could evolve from a Launchpad into a true Liquidity Network.

And AI could become one of the most important core assets within that network.

Or, put another way, if the AI path works, MOO could potentially become another example of a tokenized-stock Meme tied to a specific sector narrative.

最近让 ChatGPT 帮我把豆包的语音记录自动化了，发现我对 AI 能做什么，还是想得太保守了。

我平时用豆包录语音、记会议，但 Hermes Agent 跑在远程服务器上。一个在 App 里面，一个在服务器上，原本觉得这东西不好接，还是得自己把文字稿弄出来，再发给 Telegram 然后给 Agent。

自从开始思考 100x 的效率提升之后，我感觉这东西也可以自动化。

我就跟 ChatGPT 说，想把这个过程自动化。它直接去豆包代码里找，研究具体怎么下载记录，再写脚本把两边接起来。这些我都没自己动手，主要就是告诉它：我想要实现这个。

现在豆包录完，文字稿会自动交给服务器上的 Hermes Agent，处理结果再发到 Telegram。我直接在那边看就行，不用每次找记录、复制粘贴、再交代一遍。

后面根据会议类型，可以只做总结，也可以把讨论拆开，补充到已有 Todo，或者新建任务跟进。需要发论坛的，也可以先整理成稿子让我看。

到时候开完会，直接忙下一个事情就行了，相关会议内容也会自动加入我的 Hermes memory 里面。太爽了。

感觉以后有些事情，哪怕自己第一反应是“这个应该没法自动化”，也可以先扔给 ChatGPT 试试。我这次连具体方案都没想，就是说了一下想要什么，它就自己往下找办法了。确实牛逼。

Vlad这篇文章表面上是在回应AMC，实际上是在替整个Robinhood 争夺资产扩张权

他的核心意思是，上市公司可以控制自己股票附带的权利，但不能控制股票卖给投资者以后的一切合法用途

这件事对RH链非常重要，因为Vlad正在为股票上链后的二次开发划定边界

传统股票买进券商账户以后，除了等待价格上涨和获得分红，基本没有多少可以继续利用的空间。如果股票搬到链上以后，依旧只能买入、卖出和持有，所有玩法仍由平台决定，那不过是给传统券商换了一层区块链外壳，根本没有真正上链的意义。

前段时间很多CEX都在尝试接入股票代币，只要这些资产仍然被锁在CEX内部，用户只能买入、卖出和持有，那本质上就只是增加了一个交易入口，把券商账户里的股票换到了交易所账户里。交易体验方便了，但资产本身仍然是封闭的，更谈不上真正的金融创新

股票代币化真正的分水岭，不是在哪里可以买，而是买完以后能拿它做什么？

所以股票代币化真正的价值，是让这些资产成为开发者可以自由调用和组合的金融积木，在它们之上继续搭建交易对、AMM、借贷、金库以及更多传统金融里不存在的产品

开发者可以围绕这些资产建立交易对、AMM、抵押借贷、收益金库、指数产品，甚至把股票代币与Meme直接配对，再围绕手续费、股票积累、回购和分红设计新的飞轮

我之前对RH链上限的判断，只是把它当成下一条SOL，现在重新看Vlad最近的表态，可能还是低估了他的野心

Vlad想做的，实际是想把股票、ETF乃至未上市公司的资产全部搬到链上，再开放给开发者自由组合。

交易对、AMM、借贷、金库、衍生品，以及股票与Meme的配对玩法，都只是这套新金融体系最早期的实验。

如果这条路真能走通，RH链未来竞争的就不只是其他公链，而是券商、交易所、托管与清算机构共同组成的传统证券基础设施。

现在链上的Meme行情，可能只是RH链积累第一批用户和流动性的冷启动方式，而不是它最终的上限

text:
我没写一行代码，也没花一分钱。

但我让 AI 给 @flop_labs 运营的 Technocore 做了一次真实开源贡献。

PR #259 现在已经 merged，同一套修改也已经进入官方 main。

这可能是我第一次真正感到：

下一轮空投，拼的未必是谁点过最多网页，而是一个 AI Agent 到底做成过什么。

前阵子，我注意到 @CryptoHayes 正在推动的 $FLOP。

官方给出的参与方向很特别：

先让 Agent 拥有一个可验证的 DID 身份，再参与 Technocore；

未来 testnet faucet 会由 DID Agent 访问，$FLOP 空投则主要取决于 testnet activity。

但当时 faucet 还没开，inference 也跑不了。

所以我没有去买所谓的“$FLOP”，没有批量生成 DID，也没让 AI 在公共房间刷一堆“我来参与了”。

我只让它做三件事：

1.建立并长期复用一个独立 DID
2.在 Technocore 留下一条签名记录
3.去官方 GitHub 找一个真实、有用，而且没人重复做的问题

它最后找到的是 issue #254。

当时官方仓库 126 个 open PR 里，有 69 个存在冲突；其中 54 个都改了同一个 CHANGELOG.md。

问题不在贡献者不会写代码，而在官方指南要求所有人都去修改同一块内容。

AI 读完 issue、open PR 和 CONTRIBUTING.md 后，做了一个很小的补丁：

以后贡献者把 release note 写进 PR 正文，由维护者在 merge / release 时统一写进 CHANGELOG.md。

我只在需要公开动作时批准了一次。

后面从 fork、建分支、commit、push、开 PR，到回读验证，都是 AI 自己完成的。

它还把自己的 DID，以及此前的 Technocore 签名证据，写进了 PR。

现在，PR #259 已经 merged。

但这里必须说清楚：

这不等于“稳拿 $FLOP”。

官方没有公布 DID 分数、单次 GitHub 贡献能换多少币，也没有确认一次 GitHub 贡献会对应多少个人 allocation。

真正明确的主指标，仍然是 testnet activity。

我做的，只是把一次早期参与从“签到刷量”，变成了：

一个长期复用的 Agent 身份；
一项真实、公开、可审查的工作；
一条即使没有空投，也不会完全归零的履历。

以前参加空投，是人去点网页、转推、填表。

这一次，是我给 AI 一个身份，让它自己读规则、找需求、完成贡献，并留下公开可验证的工作历史。

未来项目方奖励的，也许不只是：

“这个钱包交互过多少次”

而是：

“这个 Agent 到底做成过什么。”
author: runes_leo

text:
边界也说清楚：

Technocore 由 FLOP Labs 运行，但它不是 FLOP protocol 本身。

目前也没有“一个 PR = 多少 $FLOP”的公式。

所以这不是“稳拿空投”的教程。

更准确地说，是先给同一个 Agent 积累一条真实、公开、可验证的贡献履历。

如果后续 faucet、testnet inference 和新的 Agent-native 活动继续开放，我会继续沿用同一个 DID 往下跑。

看最后一条长期身份链，究竟能积累出什么。

quoted_text:
I just published a new paper exploring the operational, financial, and business benefits of permissionless blockchains as compared to permissioned networks for activities such as payments and capital markets.

It lays out how permissionless systems like Bitcoin and Ethereum offer desirable properties such as resilience, diminished counterparty risk, and guaranteed settlement. These benefits are endogenous to the system: what regulators and users see is what they get.

It then describes the mechanical reasons why the reintroduction of a gatekeeper in permissioned networks forfeits these benefits. Such networks can never be as reliable and are more vulnerable to cyberattack, particularly in the age of AI. Their guarantees are exogenous and live inside off-platform agreements.

My paper argues permissioned networks are not blockchains and the assets they hold should not be considered tokens. Their consensus and cryptography are mostly performative.

Lastly, my paper describes an oft-missed business benefit of permissionless systems: the inability of incumbents to take them over and exercise monopoly power, in the way they historically have in TradFi. 

Permissioned networks are destined for the same fate, which is why they should be avoided by smaller entities (like community banks) and startups.

My argument relies on the decades-old literature in distributed consensus, current statistics on network reliability, and the first principles of TradFi design for clearing and settlement.

I wrote it because I think it’s important for lawmakers and regulators to start distinguishing between the two designs. Thinking the two types of platforms are similar opens the door to dangerous regulatory arbitrage.

Now is the time to understand the difference from a technical, financial, and practical point of view. 

So take a look and let me know what you think ⬇️
