text:
Together with Stephen Fry, Colin McFarlane, David Cameron, Steve McQueen, Jeremy Clarkson and Nick Jones, I’ve written to the Health Secretary about prostate cancer.

Prostate cancer is now the most common cancer among men in Britain. It kills one man every 45 minutes, many after a diagnosis too late for treatment to succeed. Black men face a 1 in 4 lifetime risk, double that of the general population, and men whose fathers or brothers have had the disease face a similar threat.

In May the National Screening Committee refused to extend screening beyond a group of just 1,500 men with one specific genetic variant. Everyone else at high risk doesn't have guaranteed access to a test that could save their life. We believe that's wrong, and that the Secretary of State has both the evidence and the power to overturn the ruling.

More than 250 MPs from across the political spectrum have called for a targeted national screening programme, and over 100,000 people have signed petition demanding the same. A programme targeted at those at highest risk would cost £25 million a year, which is 0.01% of the NHS budget.

We are asking the Secretary of State to reconsider the Committee's recommendation and commit to a targeted national screening programme; to act now, rather than wait a decade for further trial data while men continue to die; and to ensure that risk, not luck, decides who is tested.

author: Loong998
quoted_text:
For the first time ever, a fruit fly brain has been trained to launch a memecoin.

Not "AI inspired by a brain" — the real connectome. 165,122 neurons, 10,228,000 synaptic connections, every one traced from an actual male Drosophila by electron microscopy. Janelia FlyEM + Google Research, released CC-BY.

How it works:
Screenshots of the live launchpad go in through 892 retinotopic hex columns into L1 and L2 — the neurons sitting directly behind a fly's photoreceptors. All 165,122 integrate. The cursor comes back out of the descending neurons a fly actually walks with: DNa02's left-right asymmetry steers, DNa01 drives forward, DNp09 clicks.

The wiring is never trained. Only synaptic gains — you don't get to invent connections the fly doesn't have.
Proof its eye is doing real work: in light mode it filled 0 of 3 form fields. In dark mode, 2 of 3. Its retina is a luminance map, so invert the contrast and it goes blind.

And the honest split: the fly types the description and the ticker. The rig does the name, the pair and the tax.

I'm not really interested in betting on an $ETH move to $3000, especially with tokens like $HYPE and $LIT pushing all time highs. $ETH trading like 1.1x $BTC beta isn't bad, but it's also not extremely interesting to me as a bet to make here in the near term considering there's plenty of beta outperforming $BTC here. I'm betting on a meaningful ATH break within 6 months, and I think there are a few meaningful tailwinds that are unique to $ETH, and more importantly, unique to the level at which people are underestimating them:

1. Inclusion with $BTC as a "reserve" asset in anything resembling a strategic reserve. I think the strategic reserve overall might be an underpriced edge case, and $ETH being included, even nominally, more so. There's actually a good reason for the US to want to have some stake in the largest decentralized settlement layer.

2. Tokenized equities are cool and all, but tokenized bonds might actually be the massive TAM unlock that overwhelmingly favors $ETH over $SOL. The current rates environment globally makes this an extremely interesting edge case with tons of potential positive headline shock.

author: Pluvio9yte
quoted_text:
这几天 X和 Reddit 上被一句话彻底刷屏了：

“Astra 推理档位开到 xhigh 反而比 medium 更省 Token/配额。”

很多人看到后纷纷效仿，直接把日常编码默认档位拉到 xhigh。

但我深入调研了这几天的所有讨论和测试数据之后，发现这根本是一个被断章取义的“半真半假”谣言。
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
谣言的源头：ARC-AGI-3 的奇特曲线

这个传言并不是空穴来风，它的理论源头基本来自 ARC-AGI-3 的官方评测。在 Astra 官方 harness 下，出现了一个让所有人惊掉下巴的数据：推理档位越高，总成本竟然越低

ARC Prize 官方点评：这是历史上第一次看到大模型的 cost/performance（成本/性能）曲线往后弯。

为什么在 ARC 里会这样？

因为在 ARC 这种极其困难的环境中：

• Max / XHigh 虽然单步思考极长、单次消耗巨大，但它走得极其精准，少走了大量死胡同、重试和试错。
• Medium / Low 虽然单次便宜，但做不出来会疯狂重试、反复打转，最终总调用步数爆炸，消耗反而更多。

紧接着，Reddit r/codex 社区的一篇热帖把这套逻辑直接套到了日常开发中。

一位 Pro 20x 用户发现日常用 medium 额度掉得飞快，换成 xhigh 后“一小时只掉 1–2%”。他调取日志后给出的对比数据是：

• 单次回复成本：Medium 比 xhigh 便宜约 34%
• 任务推进表现：Medium 极易陷入延续循环（continuation loop）打转
• 总回合数：Medium 跑了 122 步 vs xhigh 仅需 65 步
• 请求频次：4.7 次/分 vs 1.5 次/分
• 额度消耗速度：约 17.3/分 vs 约 8.7/分
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
当工程师们开始做严格的同条件基准对照时，谣言立刻被戳破：

原贴 @jesse_merhi：
实验：同一代码仓库，3 个真实 Bug × 各跑 3 次，共 18 组对照跑。
实际结果：
xhigh 贵了 52%（$27.26 vs $17.90）
耗时慢了 82%（73 分钟 vs 40 分钟）
虽然加严验收后 xhigh 质量确实更高（8/12 vs 4/12），但他明确表示：日常默认首选依然是 medium。

原贴 @mylifcc：
实验：直发「终结一个谣言」，测试简单算法题与生产级状态机 PR。
实际结果：两次测试均是 medium 便宜大约一半。 只有在极端复杂任务里，xhigh 才有微弱概率翻盘。

原贴 @latentlocal：
实验：同一套 10 个任务，独立沙箱环境环境。
实际结果：结论简单粗暴——“No, xhigh doesn't burn less usage on the same tasks. xhigh = more tokens, more time, more usage.”（同任务下 xhigh 不可能更省，它就是消耗更多 Token、花更多时间、占更多配额）。

原贴 ：
实际反馈：Pro 5x 用户实测日常 xhigh 依旧非常烧额度；卡住、绕圈时再手动切 xhigh，绝对不要把它当日常默认设置。
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
第三方独立评测数据
独立评测机构 Artificial Analysis 在其 Intelligence Index 上的单任务均价评测也彻底印证了这一点：

Low: $0.46
Medium: $0.75
High: $0.96
XHigh: $1.20
Max: $1.67

在单价完全统一的情况下，档位越高，平均单题输出的 reasoning token 和总 Token 消耗就是稳步递增的。
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
真相复盘：怎样理解才是对的？

同一条 Prompt、单轮交互xhigh 必然更贵。

因为 reasoning token 也是按 output 计费的。档位越高，内部思考链越长，这一轮的账单就越贵，不存在任何逆转逻辑。

带有反馈循环的 Agent 任务（如 Codex 自动化、自测试、多工具链、ARC）xhigh “有可能”在总账上更便宜。

如果一个任务对于 medium 来说太难，它可能走偏两步，然后为了自愈而反复重读高达 几十万+ token 的历史上下文，最终在 10 几轮死循环里把配额烧光。
此时 xhigh 如果能“一步到位”，总步数腰斩，省下来的重复上下文读取成本确实可能超过思考 token 的溢价。
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
实用使用建议

小功能、普通 Bugfix、重构明确模块（Medium 1~2 次能过）：

👉 坚决用 Medium。
对照实验无一例外证明此时 Medium 又快又省钱。
长流程、强自我验收、涉及深层架构/多模态 Visual QA（容易绕圈打转）：

👉 可以尝试切 XHigh / Max。
此时更恰当的是“准确率”和“减少无效死循环”，看的是总回合数与周额度。

切忌为了“玄学省 Token”无脑将 XHigh 设为默认：
官方未曾公布任何“Medium 故意多扣配额”的机制；XHigh 带来的巨大延迟（慢 80%+）本身也是沉重的时间成本。

text:
Prediction markets have a solid record as forecasting tools. The harder question, now being tested onchain, is whether a market price should determine what management is authorized to do rather than merely inform it. Robin Hanson's futarchy design made that jump explicit: citizens define the objective, markets select the policy expected to improve it. Corporate experiments at HP, Google and Ford showed small internal markets could aggregate dispersed information — the most comprehensive study found improvements over expert forecasts of as much as 25% in mean-squared-error terms — but also optimism, thinness and early pricing errors. Crucially, researchers could not establish that operating a market improved the underlying projects. Forecast accuracy is not decision quality.

MetaDAO has moved futarchy from paper design into executable onchain governance, with conditional pass and fail markets directing treasury spending, token issuance, liquidity and legal changes. It reports 96 proposals across 14 organizations since November 2023 and $45.4 million in cumulative capital raised. It proves a market result can be coupled to an onchain action; it does not yet prove the resulting actions outperform boards or well-informed founders.

Umia, the main case examined in a new paper, combines fundraising, treasury controls and decision markets in one venture structure. Founders keep day-to-day operating authority within a monthly allowance, while markets govern larger spending, issuance, strategic changes and liquidation. Its Tailored Auction uses Uniswap's Continuous Clearing Auction, with Umia building the surrounding launch logic, conditional markets, multiplex liquidity and governance execution. By September 8, Umia had completed its public testnet and launched UMIA on Base. Early Bid opened August 26 and public bidding August 29; Umia announced the auction hit its cap that same day, reaching its $6.2M USDC target and 18M FDV within minutes. No external project launch had been independently confirmed, and management says more than 100 projects have expressed some level of interest.

Markets can already aggregate information, constrain treasury actions and select between competing proposals. Whether they consistently produce better corporate decisions than boards remains unproven. Umia offers a case for observing how these controls work once real capital and operating decisions are involved.

1. Traditional voice agents use three separate systems:

Speech-to-text → AI model → text-to-speech

Every handoff adds delay and loses context.

GPT-Live-1 handles listening and speaking inside one model, so the conversation keeps moving.

2. You can interrupt it mid-sentence.

Laugh. Hesitate. Change your question. Speak to someone nearby.

It understands what happened and continues naturally.

In early tests, Speak says it cut unwanted interruptions by almost 80% compared with turn-based systems.

3. Developers can control:

• Tone
• Pace
• Speaking style
• Custom voices

It also handles background noise, long silences and longer conversations without constantly interrupting or narrating every step.

4. The voice model does not have to do everything itself.

It can keep the conversation moving while passing deeper reasoning and tool calls to GPT-6 Astra or another model.

That means phone agents can book restaurants, update orders or solve support problems.

5. On OpenAI’s tests, GPT-Live-1 improved Full Duplex Bench performance by 30 points over GPT-Realtime-2.1.

One healthcare company says it removed 23,000 lines of code from its old voice stack.

Voice agents can finally behave like a conversation, not a phone menu.

quoted_text:
I just published a new paper exploring the operational, financial, and business benefits of permissionless blockchains as compared to permissioned networks for activities such as payments and capital markets.

It lays out how permissionless systems like Bitcoin and Ethereum offer desirable properties such as resilience, diminished counterparty risk, and guaranteed settlement. These benefits are endogenous to the system: what regulators and users see is what they get.

It then describes the mechanical reasons why the reintroduction of a gatekeeper in permissioned networks forfeits these benefits. Such networks can never be as reliable and are more vulnerable to cyberattack, particularly in the age of AI. Their guarantees are exogenous and live inside off-platform agreements.

My paper argues permissioned networks are not blockchains and the assets they hold should not be considered tokens. Their consensus and cryptography are mostly performative.

Lastly, my paper describes an oft-missed business benefit of permissionless systems: the inability of incumbents to take them over and exercise monopoly power, in the way they historically have in TradFi. 

Permissioned networks are destined for the same fate, which is why they should be avoided by smaller entities (like community banks) and startups.

My argument relies on the decades-old literature in distributed consensus, current statistics on network reliability, and the first principles of TradFi design for clearing and settlement.

I wrote it because I think it’s important for lawmakers and regulators to start distinguishing between the two designs. Thinking the two types of platforms are similar opens the door to dangerous regulatory arbitrage.

Now is the time to understand the difference from a technical, financial, and practical point of view. 

So take a look and let me know what you think ⬇️

text:
40多名英国议员联名致信首相 Andy Burnham，要求禁止发展超级智能，顺便推动一份国际协议。

消息出来，评论区一片"人类终于觉醒了""议员倍中国收买了"。一线研究者确实早就在警告失控风险，40个人愿意把名字押上去，总比装看不见强。但把这封信读成治理的起点，格局就小了。你看，它真正暴露的不是决心，是无力：技术跑出了监管的射程，而签字是这个世界成本最低的表达。

第一件事，这封禁令信对英国来说，是一笔什么样的生意？英国自己几乎没有前沿训练集群，也没有成规模的芯片产能。禁一个自己没有的东西，一分钱不用花，经济学管这叫边际成本约等于零；而"愿意者联盟"带头人这个位置，声誉收益是真金白银。我管这个组合叫"零成本禁令"加"声誉套利"。以我自己为例，我给公司内部联署信签名从没超过十秒，签完第二天就忘了。40多名议员什么概念？下院一共650席，6%的签名率，平均16个人里才有1个，这在英国政治里属于顺手签的程度，远没到伤筋动骨的共识。热闹归热闹，成本收益算下来，这更像一次站队，而不是一次治理。

第二件事，为什么国际协议在超级智能这件事上，比核武器难一个数量级？1968年签的《不扩散核武器条约》，到今天191个缔约国，勉强算军控的样板。它能撑半个多世纪，靠的不是签名，是三样东西：看得见——卫星和地震波盯着，地下核试验瞒不住；进得去——IAEA核查员直接驻厂；伤得起——违约成本清晰到没人敢试。

超级智能三样全没有。模型跑在机房里，隔壁国家都不知道你在训练什么，算力可以拆散了藏，权重可以拷进一块硬盘带走。朝鲜2003年连退约都没耽误它接着干，你猜一份连"超级智能"三个字都定义不出来的协议，能拦住谁？

更麻烦的是，军控最怕的猜疑链，AI一个不落全有：一旦某个大国觉得对方在暗中加速，"你不停我也不停"就是唯一理性的选择。军控史可以再往前翻，1922年的华盛顿海军条约是看着吨位签的，军舰下水全世界都数得清，日本照样在1936年退场走人。AI 连"吨位"都数不清，结果大概率不是安全协议，而是新一轮军备竞赛——各国把超级智能当战略威慑工具，安全问题被扔到一边。

顺带提一下，也别急着把这封信贬成纯作秀。当然，它禁不住任何人，但议程设置，说白了就是决定大家接下来聊什么，这件事本身有价值：超级智能治理从科幻话题进了议会日程，这一步总得有人先迈。只是要清楚，迈出这一步和走完这条路之间，隔着可核查的约束、中美真正入局，还有一套至今没人发明的验证机制。

治理超级智能，难的从来不是写下承诺的手，而是验证承诺的眼睛；签名可以一晚上凑齐，信任不行。你觉得这封信是觉醒的开始，还是姿态的胜利？

text:
神了，才发现 Genspark 居然自己专门训了一个 PPT 生成模型！！？

9 月 11 日，Genspark 发布了他们第一个自己训练的模型 Gen-1 Slides。

但它不是从头预训练出来的，而是以开源的 MiniMax M3 为底座，和 Fireworks AI 合作做后训练，专门优化做 PPT这件事。

原因很简单：现在最强的通用模型都在卷 Coding、数学、Agent，但真正做 PPT 的时候，还是经常出现排版崩掉、内容太稀、引用有问题😅。

所以 Genspark 干脆针对 Slides 这个任务，重新训练了一个垂直模型。

结果效果还挺好。
他们在大约 200 个真实 PPT 任务上测试，Gen-1 Slides 的综合分是 0.821，Claude Opus 5 是 0.810。
而在 9 组内部和公开 Benchmark 里，它拿了 8 个第一。

但更离谱的是成本：
Gen-1 Slides 输入价格只有 $0.30 / 1M tokens，Opus 5 是 $5 / 1M，差不多只有后者的 1/17。
按真正生成一套 PPT 的成本算，也是 $0.44 vs $4.16，接近便宜了 10 倍。

这个事情我觉得比最近各个模型厂的大混战有意思得多。

因为 Genspark 本来就是一家 AI 应用公司。
以前这种公司的核心工作是选模型、写 Prompt、搭 Agent，现在开源模型足够强之后，它们已经可以再往下走一步：
直接拿一个开源基模，把自己最核心的业务做后训练。

而 Genspark 最后选 MiniMax M3，也有几个很现实的原因。

他们实际测了一圈之后，发现 M3 在长上下文、Agentic Tool Calling、多模态这些 PPT 任务很依赖的能力上比较合适。

同时 M3 是 MoE，虽然总参数 428B，但每个 Token 实际只激活约 22B，模型没那么重，后训练和部署成本也更适合应用公司承受。

更有意思的是，这已经不是第一次了。

前几天沙特 HUMAIN 做自己的主权模型 humain-m3，最后同样选择了 MiniMax M3 作为底座，再针对阿拉伯语继续训练。

一个是做 PPT 的硅谷 AI 应用公司，一个是做主权 AI 的沙特公司，最后居然都选到了同一个中国开源模型上。

所以相比又多一个 Benchmark 第一，我反而觉得这种案例更值得看。

一个开源模型开始被别人拿去继续训练、做自己的产品和模型，可能才说明它真正开始进入产业了🫡

而 MiniMax M3 已经开始吃到这波红利了。

$PAIREX 2.85 dyor

0xb8cf4ad387cfd607c66a207cfffc46498aacd9d6

okx wallet:https://t.co/w4oQ8ywTfv

A launchpad where any token can be launched against any fiat-denominated currency.

Pons allows Memecoins to be priced against tokenized stocks like NVIDIA. This takes the same concept and applies it to fiat currencies: when launching a token, you can choose EUR, JPY, GBP, INR, THB, and more. The token is then quoted, bought, and creator rewards are distributed in that selected currency.

For example, if you choose the Canadian Dollar, the token is priced, traded, and settled based on CAD.

There isn't actually any CAD on-chain. Instead, they mint their own “currency tokens” and put the entire supply into a single-range Uniswap position, effectively creating a peg-like sell wall so that the quoted price appears to track the exchange rate.

When users sell back into the currency, the treasury uses the USD it collected from that wall to buy the tokens back. Each currency has its own separate pool, so one currency cannot drain the liquidity of another.

PAIREX is the platform token, paired with USDG on Pons. So far, I haven't seen any governance, staking, or revenue-sharing mechanism attached to it.

The potential catalyst going forward would be the project giving PAIREX additional utility or value capture.

Yesterday I did a proactive whole-body MRI at @prenuvo for early cancer screening and other diseases. Luckily no worrisome or high risk findings. I had a few minor findings (common and benign things), and the explanation and reassurance was very well done in the report. The MRI even detected a lingering sinus infection I've had for the past 4 weeks! The images you get of your body are incredible too. It can't possibly hurt (except the pocket; it's $2,500) to do these regularly and monitor changes over time.

Their MRI setup is quite nice too. They are a bit more spacious than the ones I've seen at hospitals, but most importantly they put special glasses on you with a 45° mirror that lets you watch a movie projected behind you. (You choose the movie/show.) Makes a huge difference for claustrophobia because the space feels much bigger when looking through the mirror. It's also nice you can see a clock in the screen, so you know approximately how much time you have remaining inside the magnet.

Overall, impressed.

A long time ago, I worked at a Bitcoin exchange handling these requests, so I have some insight into how they work.

today is a good day to note: I love America and I love its exceptional free speech norms, enshrined in law and protected by its people and culture. the ability to say true and unpleasant or destabilizing things is not a right most people (even in the Western world!) enjoy

this extends beyond merely what the first amendment and related doctrine legally protects to the nurture and support of the entire American culture. this culture allowed for the creation of the free-spirited Internet forums that birthed so much of modern thinking on artificial intelligence. wherever are the sacred cows, the free internet is able to poke and prod them, for better and for worse

the actual realized pdoom of our culture is much lower due to our ability to freely discuss things as off-putting and nasty as the chances of human extinction. even when powerful interests find this inconvenient, the discourse does not stop happening -in public, in excruciating detail, without needing anyone's blessing. companies allow or encourage this to a surprising degree, at least in part because they know the cultural immune reaction will be strong if surprising levels of free speech norms are not upheld, as seen in recent history

I know many of you are sick of “discourse”, having bathed in its sludge, its many pathologies, its propagandists bigots and sycophants, but the planet would be in much worse shape if all of this technological development was happening in cultures or countries where free discourse was stifled. this norm survives only because all of us keep choosing to encourage it and enforce it even when it's costly

text:
A lot of people are missing Terence Tao’s point and thinking “mathematicians are upset that AI is better than them.” That’s not what he’s saying, and some people are forgetting that Tao is one of the most AI-pilled mathematicians out there.

His point is that when people work on discovering something, along the way they invent new concepts. Those concepts later become useful far beyond the original goal, and enables further inventions. Finding a solution does matter, but the intermediate idea is often what makes the field richer, because other people can share it and build the next thing from it.

In tech, we can use the analogy of collaborative software. We started with algorithms for merging changes in a Word document, and evolved that to concepts about versions, diffs, and merges, and later to real-time collaboration tools like Git, Google Docs, and Figma. Humans built upon these concepts and developed more powerful solutions.

Terence’s worry is that a machine automating a solution robs the field of the value of developing the intermediate discoveries in the pursuit of larger discoveries.

When automating a solution, the intermediate discoveries and invention of concepts can be buried or completely hidden in the black box. We don’t learn from them to build the next thing; it’s like we never made the invention of collaborative document editing and thus could not have the conceptual understanding to invent the next version – and since it’s hidden, we also don’t socialize them to allow other people to invent, too, a core tenet of collective discovery.

So then, in both code and math, this leads to the atrophy of development of concepts in the field.

In other words: pure ‘solution extraction’ that hides the process of discovery can leave the field with a checked-off theorem but little new insight or new questions to pursue. And it might prevent us from understanding a field deeper.

I am seeing, first-hand, that atrophying of skills in software development. We push buttons and get solutions. There is much less incentive to develop new concepts and human skill. The bet most software companies are making is that LLMs are so effective in writing code that you’re still shipping overwhelmingly more value even with human skill atrophy, and it’s the right bet IMO.

However, much of the software industry is built upon building things, not necessarily novel invention and research. In such an environment, you can say that you accept some atrophying of conceptual invention and human skill for more output.

On the other hand, sectors like math and pure sciences that are focused on invention and insight might be the hardest hit by this.

Practical/applied sciences might fall somewhere in the middle. An Alzheimer’s cure, room-temperature semiconductor, or highly effective carbon capture solution are far too valuable to sandbag and say only humans can do that to develop concepts in the ‘proper’ way. The outcome matters too much to treat the preservation of concept invention as the highest goal. Even there, though, hidden intermediates can slow the next breakthrough if nobody can see how the first one actually worked.

So the question is not “is AI allowed to solve hard problems?” It is “in this field (math, science, tech, etc.), is the answer itself the main point, or are the concepts and abstractions we use to get there also the thing we need to maintain?”​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

In pure math, there’s an argument that the intermediates are often more useful than the solution, and atrophy in concept development is highly detrimental to the field. Solving Navier–Stokes, contrary to what some people claim, has little practical application, and pure math might be one of those fields where just finding a solution isn’t the entire point, and can actually be contrary to the field, which is what Tao is worried about.

text:
New post: Data bottlenecks won’t block an intelligence explosion

One of the most important questions facing the world is whether AI will undergo a fast intelligence explosion and quickly automate most real-world work.

A key objection people raise is *data bottlenecks*. Data is a crucial input to AI training - how could it increase fast enough for such explosive progress?

I tried hard to find strong bottlenecks, but ended up sceptical that they would stop an intelligence explosion from accelerating over time.

Here are the most compelling bottlenecks I investigated and why I wasn’t convinced.

**Bottleneck #1**: you’ll need millions of trajectories of every job, which will take years or decades to collect

Today’s AI algorithms are very data hungry. You would need a huge amount of data to automate the full economy.

But the plan isn’t to use today’s AI algorithms.

The plan is to do a software intelligence explosion inside a datacentre, where AI becomes superintelligent at AI research - and have that AI produce a highly **sample-efficient learning algorithm.**

Then you don't need millions of trajectories per task. You need as many as a human learns from, or fewer. And the data can be messy, just like the data humans learn from.

That data could be gathered in a few months.

Sceptic: *“But what about sim to real transfer? Why not expect a “Goodhart Singularity” (@mentalgeorge), where learning algorithms discovered using virtual tasks fail to really translate to the real world?”*

People get confused here. **Trained neural nets** generalise badly. A neural net trained on Chess generalises badly to Go. But **learning algorithms** generalise very well. The same learning algorithm that masters chess can also master Go (AlphaZero). The Transformer architecture was developed for processing text, but it also works for sounds, images and controlling agents. The human learning algorithm was "designed" for hunting on the Savanna, but it also works for String Theory.

So if AI designs a sample efficient learning algorithm from inside a data centre, it will very likely translate to real-world tasks. (And AI will have access to some real-world tasks so can check and iterate!)

At this point the sceptic might retreat: *“Fine, data won’t be a bottleneck if there’s a software intelligence explosion in a data centre. But data bottlenecks will prevent that from happening in the first place!”*

So let’s focus on bottlenecks to a software intelligence explosion.

**Bottleneck 2: AI progress has ridden exponential growth in training data. That can't continue, let alone accelerate.**

But forecasts of a software intelligence explosion extrapolate software progress. And software progress just is: getting the same capabilities from *less* compute and *less* data.

So the core engine of the explosion doesn’t rely on increasing the amount of data at all.

**Bottleneck 3: improving data *quality* relies on human experts, and that won’t be possible once AI is smarter than humans**

The core engine of the software intelligence explosion *does* rely on improving data quality. Today we augment high-quality internet data, pay humans for expert trajectories, and build RL environments where AI has to replicate human-built software.

But all these methods *extract* quality out of an existing human reservoir. Above human level, the reservoir is empty. AI will have to *manufacture* higher-quality data than any that exists, and do so from scratch.

This will slow the intelligence explosion.

But it won’t stop it in its tracks. We can already produce superhuman data quality via RL. And AI could produce higher-quality trajectories by thinking for longer.

Crucially, this won’t stop the intelligence explosion from **accelerating**. Losing the human reservoir makes it harder to get from AGI to AGI+ — but it makes it harder to get from AGI+ to AGI++ by roughly the same amount. The handicap is the same at every stage.

So if you previously expected each step to take less time than the one before, you should still expect that. Every step might take 50% longer, but progress still accelerates.

**Bottleneck 4: paradigm tax**

AI capabilities are spiky. When AI first matches humans at AI research, it will be much stronger than humans in some ways and much weaker in others. More parallel copies, faster thinking — but weaker generalisation and weaker sample efficiency.

Which means AI's human-level performance will initially lean heavily on a mountain of human writing about transformers.

When AI then discovers new techniques — no such mountain will exist. No textbooks, no blog posts, no code. Deeply understanding a technique is harder than stumbling upon it — we understand general relativity far better now than Einstein did in 1917. So AI may match humans on the techniques it inherited, but fall below humans on the ones it creates.

This paradigm tax can be paid. Eg, AI can generate millions of trajectories to illustrate new techniques. But paying the tax is a real cost that slows down AI progress.

Again though, this won’t stop the intelligence explosion from **accelerating**. It makes it harder for AI to master whatever replaces the transformer — but it makes it harder to master whatever replaces *that* by roughly the same amount. Every new paradigm arrives without a corpus.

This makes each step take longer than you previously thought, but it doesn't change whether each step is faster than the one before.

**My bottom line:** Data bottlenecks will slow the early stages of a software intelligence explosion, but won’t stop it from accelerating over time. And then they won’t stop AI from quickly automating most economic work thereafter.

Read the full post for more!

https://t.co/YkF9WE9LKI

text:
Been long Copper since 2023. Not naive enough to expect up-only in a straight line, but the macro thesis is still screaming bull.

S&P Global dropped some great charts, so let’s strip away the noise and run through the structural supply:

1) The tier-1 discovery pipeline is in a total desert. Down from 714.8Mt in the ‘90s to a pathetic 8.7Mt over 2020–2025. Mega discoveries are basically extinct.

2) Capex burns are back up past $3B annually on exploration, yet the hit rate is completely cooked—netting a measly 0-2 discoveries a year. Trash ROIC... 

3) Discovery cost per tonne went from ~$10 in the ‘90s to an eye watering $1,000–$2,600+ print today. Not a temporary blip; it’s a secular blowout in finding costs.

4) Gone are the days of unlocking multi tens of million monsters like Collahuasi or Pebble. Today’s wins are 1–2Mt crumbs that don't move the global balance needle.

5) More than half (55%) of cumulative reserves are concentrated in South America, while Africa—such as the DRC—is gradually taking up a larger share. South America has recently slipped into operational and production slumps, and Africa continues to suffer from political instability.

6) Roughly 500Mt of identified reserves have been rotting in prefeasibility purgatory for decades. Permitting hell, eco-lawfare, and zero IRR. Bless the regulators and green grifters for choking.

7) C-suites are terrified of greenfield risk. They’ve completely castrated wildcat budgets to hide inside safe brownfield pit extensions. Structural consequence. Zero chance of hitting a generational tier-1 asset.

8) Copper mining typically takes over 15-20 years from discovery to actual commercial production (operational), the current exploration slump translates directly into a future production cliff. This is an undeniable fact.

9) Megawatt power grids, EV buildouts, and AI data centers are devouring physical units, while the project pipeline is running bone dry. Sure, the demand ceiling floats on the macro tape, but this structural supply paralysis puts a bulletproof concrete floor under the market.

10) Marginal incentive pricing and long term cost floors have nowhere to go but violently up and to the right.

So what's priced into the equities? Large caps are still riding a fat liquidity premium over the mid/small cap complex. Ivanhoe’s lagging for obvious DRC baggage, but look at the implied copper price deck.

Freeport is pricing in $6.25/lb. First Quamtum is at $5.92/lb. Lundin sits at $5.44/lb, Capstone at $5.37/lb, my horse Hudbay at $4.73/lb, and Ivanhoe down at $3.95/lb.

Of course each name has a different setup. In the case of Hudbay, which I hold, precious account for nearly 45% of annual revenue, whereas First Quantum and Freeport sit around the 10% mark.

Naturally i'm completely fine with this since I'm structurally bullish on precious as well. What I want to say is that while we must closely monitor that the copper thesis doesn't derail, if you have conviction in the trajectory, equities still offer massive upside.

Demand downside risk? Sure conceded. If Xi pulls the trigger on Taiwan or Jensen and Sam Altman get perp walked by the feds for running an AI Ponzi(lol), things will hit the fan.

Outside of those black swans, the supply side reality is downright apocalyptic—and the operational bleed coming out of Chile just hammers the nail in the coffin. In commodity risk, when the supply side guarantees a rock solid floor, you’ve already eliminated half your downside distribution.

Still max constructive on copper. Until the tape changes my thesis, I’m letting my winners run and fading the short term chop.

Along with $HBM, I hold two junior miners. Certified worst PM on the planet and talking exclusively to pump my own book like the conflicted scumbag I am, so don't take this as financial advice.

text:
TL;DR
CXMT가 HBM 잘만들면 패키지는 조상님이 해주나?

1. 최근 CXMT의 HBM 수율이 몇 %까지 올라왔고, HBM2에서 HBM3로 언제 넘어가며 향후 CAPA가 얼마가 될 거라는 식의 이야기들이 많이 나오는데, 개인적으로 이런 얘기를 볼 때마다 한 가지가 빠져 있다는 생각이 듦. HBM만 잘 만들면 그걸 대체 어디에 붙여서 쓸 건가? CoWoS는 조상님이 해주나.

2. 범용 DRAM은 메모리 업체가 어느 정도 독립적으로 기술을 따라잡아도 시장 진입이 가능함. DIMM이나 LPDDR처럼 표준화된 인터페이스와 모듈 구조를 사용하는 제품은 문제가 생기면 해당 메모리나 모듈을 교체하면 되고, 최악의 경우에도 GPU,CPU 같은 고가 Logic까지 같이 버릴 필요는 없음. 그래서 DRAM 자체의 수율과 성능, 신뢰성이 올라오면 비교적 독립적으로 경쟁력을 확보할 수 있음.

3. 그런데 HBM은 구조적으로 완전히 다름. 여러 장의 DRAM Die를 TSV로 적층하고 이를 Base Die와 결합한 뒤, 최종적으로 GPU/AI Accelerator와 함께 2.5D Package에 실장해야 함. 결국 GPU와 여러 개의 HBM Stack이 하나의 CoWoS Package 안에서 사실상 한 몸처럼 움직이는 구조임.

4. 문제는 여기서부터임. HBM Stack 하나의 수율이 아무리 높아져도 CoWoS 단계의 Interposer, RDL, Micro-bump, Underfill, Substrate, Warpage, Thermal 관리 등에서 문제가 발생하면 최종 Package 수율은 다시 떨어짐. 반대로 CoWoS 공정이 아무리 좋아도 HBM 자체의 수율이나 TSV 신뢰성이 낮으면 역시 완제품 수율을 확보할 수 없음. 또한 패키지와 HBM의 조합도 굉장히 중요함. 결국 HBM과 Advanced Packaging의 수율은 곱셈으로 작용한다고 봐야 함.

5. 대표적인 예시로, 삼성이 HBM3부터 굉장히 고전했던 이유 중 하나도 여기에 있음. HBM 자체 테스트에서는 문제가 없었는데, 실제 CoWoS에 실장한 이후 문제가 발생하면서 NVIDIA GPU까지 포함된 고가의 Package 전체를 꽤 많이 날려먹었던 것으로 알려져 있음. 심지어 당시 NVIDIA에서 삼성으로 Audit을 나온 담당자가 "IM NOT YOUR FCKING TESTER" 라고 했다는 일화까지 있을 정도.

6. 결국 CoWoS와의 조합은 단순히 HBM 자체를 잘 만드는 것으로 끝나는 문제가 아님. DRAM 제조사가 실제 CoWoS 실장 이후 HBM에 가해지는 조건과 요구사항을 상세하게 이해하고, 출하 전에 이를 최대한 모사한 환경에서 충분한 Test Coverage를 확보해야 함. HBM 단품에서는 잡히지 않던 문제가 CoWoS 실장 이후 발견되기 시작하면 그때부터는 불량 비용의 단위 자체가 달라짐.

7. 삼성은 예전부터 ‘우리가 제품만 제대로 만들어주면 고객이 알아서 잘 쓰겠지’라는 식의 사고방식이 강했던 회사인데, HBM에서는 이런 접근이 제대로 발목을 잡았다고 봄. HBM 자체의 성능과 수율뿐만 아니라 고객의 GPU와 CoWoS Packaging 환경까지 하나의 시스템으로 보고 선제적으로 검증했어야 했는데, 이 부분에서 시행착오를 겪으면서 사실상 거의 2년 가까운 시간을 날려버렸다고 생각함. 근데 CoWoS가 아직 셋업도 안된 중국 업체가 이걸 단기간이 따라잡을 수 있을까?

8. 특히 HBM 세대가 올라갈수록 이 문제는 더 어려워질 가능성이 큼. Stack 수와 I/O가 증가하고, HBM4부터는 Base Die의 역할과 복잡도도 커지며, GPU와 HBM 사이의 대역폭 역시 계속 증가함. Package 면적과 전력밀도, 열밀도까지 같이 커지기 때문에 Interposer/RDL, Substrate, Warpage, Thermal Management까지 동시에 따라와야 함. 결국 HBM 자체의 기술 발전이 Advanced Packaging에 요구하는 난이도까지 계속 끌어올리는 구조임.

9. 그래서 중국 HBM을 평가할 때도 'CXMT가 HBM 수율 몇 %를 달성했다'는 숫자 하나만 보고 경쟁력을 판단하는 건 위험하다고 봄. 실제로 봐야 할 것은 그 HBM을 어떤 Logic에, 어떤 2.5D Packaging 기술로, 어느 정도의 Package Yield와 CAPA로 결합할 수 있느냐임. DRAM Die 수율 90%와 실제 AI Accelerator에 탑재 가능한 HBM 시스템을 대량생산하는 능력 사이에는 생각보다 훨씬 긴 거리가 있음.

10. 결국 중국이 HBM에서 한국 업체들을 따라잡는다는 이야기는 메모리 업체 하나만 봐서는 안 됨. CXMT 같은 DRAM 업체뿐 아니라 TSV/Stacking, Advanced Packaging, Interposer/RDL, Substrate, 검사장비와 소재까지 포함한 생태계 전체가 같이 올라와야 함. HBM과 CoWoS급 Advanced Packaging이 동시에 기술 성숙과 양산 CAPA를 확보해야 비로소 실제 AI GPU에 꽂아 쓸 수 있는 제품이 되는 것. HBM 수율만 놓고 중국의 AI 메모리 경쟁력을 평가하기에는 아직 봐야 할 변수가 너무 많다고 생각함.

看到这个新闻还是震惊了一下，原来我们在吃孙哥 @justinsuntron 瓜的同时，他又默默干了一件大事。

就在三天前，Canary Staked TRX ETF 正式登陆美国 Cboe，代码 $TRXS 这也是美国第一只现货质押 TRX ETF。

也就是接下来美国人民以后不用注册交易所、不用钱包和私钥，直接通过证券账户就可以买 TRX 的敞口了，

截至 9 月 10 日，TRXS 已经持有约 1.48 亿枚 TRX，资产规模约 5000 万美元。

我的角度来看，觉得美国人民对波场 ETF 应该会比较有兴趣，主要是TRON 已经成为全球最重要的稳定币结算网络之一，TRC20 USDT 几乎已经成为一种基础设施。

而 TRXS 又多了一层 Staking 收益，相当于把“TRX 价格 + 波场网络增长 + 质押收益”打包成了一个传统证券账户可以买到的产品，这是美国人喜欢的玩意。

比特币 ETF 卖的是数字黄金，ETH ETF 卖的是智能合约平台，而 TRX ETF 真正应该卖的故事，可能是稳定币时代的支付基础设施。

孙哥这个人争议一直很多，但有一点不得不承认：他是真的能搞事情，也是真的能熬。

孙哥 @justinsuntron 会玩，后续观察下 TRXS 接下来 1 个月的净申购和 AUM 增长速度，那个才决定 ETF 到底只是一个里程碑，还是会真正形成持续买盘，持续关注下！

quoted_text:
A lot of people are asking what's going on with NPC, so let me just talk to you straight.

I've been dealing with some things in my personal life that I'd rather keep to myself. Nothing dramatic, just life, and it pulled me away more than I wanted it to. I'm sorry for the quiet.

Here's the honest context though. NPC started as a joke. A faceless character that does nothing, a zero narrative, back when nobody was asking about utility or roadmaps. People just collected them because they liked them. That was the whole thing, and it was beautiful.

Then we shipped. And shipped again. Points, badges, playable characters, training, all of it. And somewhere along the way, shipping that much quietly raised the expectations of what NPC is supposed to be. I understand that completely. Maybe part of it is on me for setting a pace. And maybe part of it is fair, maybe you just want me around more, and honestly, that's true, I could be more present.

I know the floor going down made some of you nervous too, and I get it. But if you look past the number, the community is still here, still active, still showing up every single day. That has not changed, and that matters far more to me than a floor price ever will.

It's been about three and a half months since mint. I won't pretend I never get demotivated, because I do. That's part of the process, and I wouldn't take any of this back, because all of it led here.

And to be honest, the easy move right now would be to chase the noise. Everyone's on Robinhood, and we could launch something there tomorrow and manufacture instant hype. But I won't do that. It would be a short-term sugar rush that makes things worse, not better, and it isn't what NPC is about. We build the slow way, on purpose.

What I can tell you is I'm still in the background working on the things I actually want to ship. I also see a lot of people offering to CTO, and I genuinely respect that, it means you care more than I could ask for. It's not something I'm closed off to down the line, and there may come a point where opening this up makes sense. But not right now, not while I've still got things I want to see through myself. If you want to help in the meantime, I'd love that energy pointed at building with me rather than around me.

And as a small thank you for sticking around, we're moving royalties from 5.55% to 0% for a while. Trade freely.

NPC was always heading toward zero. Turns out the royalties got there first.

text:
A lot of people are going to watch Tuesday's CLARITY Act vote without understanding what they're actually watching.

That's because Tuesday isn't simply a vote on whether the Senate likes or dislikes the bill.

Tyler Williams, a crypto policy insider who has worked at the Treasury and advised Secretary Bessent on crypto, explained the entire process to me.

Before the Senate can debate the substance of the legislation, it has to vote for cloture.

That requires 60 senators to vote in favor of proceeding.

If that happens, the Senate can actually start debating the bill, consider amendments and move toward substantive votes.

If it doesn't, the process can't move forward in the same way.

He also made an important point: even if you're skeptical of crypto or don't like parts of the bill, you still have to vote to proceed if you want those issues debated and changed.

So the 60 votes on Tuesday are a much bigger deal than they might look on the surface.

Full conversation below 👇

text:
The question I get more than any other is some version of: I have this much money, now what. The number changes. Five thousand. Fifty thousand. A million. People expect the answer to change with it.

It does not.

The market does not know how much money you have. Bitcoin does not trade differently for a small account. The level that tells me whether this is a bull market is the same level whether I am looking at 15 thousand dollars or 1.5 million.

For me that level is a weekly close above 82 thousand. That is the last lower high, the last price bitcoin held before it rolled over. Until it closes a week above that, I treat every rally as a rally inside a downtrend.

Bitcoin is 77,300 right now. So I am waiting.

What changes with account size is not the decision. It is the size of the mistake.

Being wrong on 15 thousand dollars teaches you something and you still have a life. Being wrong on 1.5 million is a house. Same percentage, different consequence. That is why I care more about the quality of the entry than about being early to it.

I am 85 percent in bitcoin and I am not adding here. Not because I think it falls from here. I do not know that. Because I said I would wait for one specific number and that number has not printed yet.

Here is the part nobody enjoys. Most of investing is sitting still between two decisions.

I have done both versions of getting that wrong. I have averaged into a downtrend and watched my average price get worse every single week. I have also sat out and watched something run without me. The second one is cheaper, and it is not close.

So the useful question is not how much money you have. It is this: what would have to happen for you to change your mind, and did you write it down before you needed it.

Pick the number first. Then your account size stops being the interesting part.

text:
I just published a new paper exploring the operational, financial, and business benefits of permissionless blockchains as compared to permissioned networks for activities such as payments and capital markets.

It lays out how permissionless systems like Bitcoin and Ethereum offer desirable properties such as resilience, diminished counterparty risk, and guaranteed settlement. These benefits are endogenous to the system: what regulators and users see is what they get.

It then describes the mechanical reasons why the reintroduction of a gatekeeper in permissioned networks forfeits these benefits. Such networks can never be as reliable and are more vulnerable to cyberattack, particularly in the age of AI. Their guarantees are exogenous and live inside off-platform agreements.

My paper argues permissioned networks are not blockchains and the assets they hold should not be considered tokens. Their consensus and cryptography are mostly performative.

Lastly, my paper describes an oft-missed business benefit of permissionless systems: the inability of incumbents to take them over and exercise monopoly power, in the way they historically have in TradFi. 

Permissioned networks are destined for the same fate, which is why they should be avoided by smaller entities (like community banks) and startups.

My argument relies on the decades-old literature in distributed consensus, current statistics on network reliability, and the first principles of TradFi design for clearing and settlement.

I wrote it because I think it’s important for lawmakers and regulators to start distinguishing between the two designs. Thinking the two types of platforms are similar opens the door to dangerous regulatory arbitrage.

Now is the time to understand the difference from a technical, financial, and practical point of view. 

So take a look and let me know what you think ⬇️

- 允许私密分享：Site 不用再公开，可以只邀请指定的人访问。
- 发布速度翻倍：从 Prompt 到真正上线，时间直接缩短一半。
- 可以查看网站数据：可以让 ChatGPT 查看 Site 背后的数据库，协作者也能一起看。
- 支持自定义域名：终于可以挂自己的域名了（这个真的好🤣）。

我觉得这里面最关键的，其实是前两个。

之前 Sites 更像一个很强的一次性生成器，做个 Demo 很爽，但没考虑过团队协作、内部工具、客户交付这些真实场景，如果你有需求就会立刻撞上权限和协作的问题。

现在把多人编辑、私密分享、自定义域名都补上之后，Sites才开始真正从生成一个网页，往直接在ChatGPT里做和运营一个产品走。

三个月前 @OpenAI  推出 GPT 的 Sites，让你直接通过对话生成并托管一个完整的交互式网站。

现在已经大家用它创建了超过 500 万个站点。

这个数字已经有点离谱了。

8월 Core CPI는 전월 대비 0.3% 상승했습니다.
예상치는 **0.2%**였습니다.
Headline CPI는 전월 대비 0.4%,
전년 대비 3.4% 상승했습니다.

CPI 데이터 → 연준의 반응을 예측 → BTC의 반응을 예측 → 거래 → 결과 확정 → 다시 반복.
5분, 혹은 1분 단위의 bitcoin:native Prediction Market은
전통적인 선거 예측 시장과는 완전히 다른 UX를 요구합니다.

1분 단위 시장에서는
100밀리초에서 1초의 latency 차이만으로도
사용자가 체감하는 경험이 달라질 수 있습니다.

그리고 AI Agent에게는 더 중요합니다.
낮은 latency, 신뢰할 수 있는 state, 저렴한 실행 비용, 그리고 높은 concurrency.

이 네 가지가 갖춰져야
Agent의 전략 자체가 작동할 수 있습니다.
그래서 @linera_io  핵심은 단순히
**"더 빠른 블록체인을 만들었다"**는 것이 아닙니다.
핵심은 이것입니다.

AI Agent와 recurring prediction market의 결합은
새로운 애플리케이션 카테고리를 만들어낸다.

그리고 그 경제성은 근본적으로
latency, concurrency, 그리고 trusted data access에 의해 결정됩니다.

여기서 세 가지 인프라 요구사항이 나옵니다.
첫째, Horizontal Scaling.

수천 개의 시장이 동시에 돌아가더라도
하나의 글로벌 blockspace를 놓고
서로 경쟁해서는 안 됩니다.
둘째, Vertical Scaling.

하나의 시장에 수백만 명이 몰렸을 때도
순차적으로 처리되는 CLOB 하나가 병목이 되어서는 안 됩니다.

필요한 것은 parallel execution입니다.
셋째, Trusted Agent Connectivity.

Agent가 돈을 걸고 판단하는 데이터라면,
중앙화된 RPC가 제공하는 state를
그저 무조건 신뢰해서는 안 됩니다.
Finance is becoming increasingly continuous, interactive, and agent-driven.

Perpetuals, sportsbooks, meme trading, prediction markets,
그리고 앞으로 등장할 다양한 금융 서비스들은
점점 하나의 행동 루프로 수렴하고 있습니다.

Observe → Decide → Act → Resolve → Reinvest → Repeat.

관찰하고.
판단하고.
행동하고.

결과를 확인하고.

다시 투자하고.
그리고 반복합니다.

사람의 속도에서는
이미 충분히 재미있는 경험입니다.

하지만 Agent의 속도에서는 완전히 달라집니다.

이것은 always-on computational workload가 됩니다.
그리고 여기서 새로운 인프라 카테고리가 등장할 수 있습니다.
애플리케이션의 latency가
곧 trading volume과 revenue를 결정하는 환경.

이것이 단순히
**"블록체인의 TPS를 높이는 것"**보다

애플리케이션과 그 애플리케이션을 구동하는 체인을
수직적으로 통합해야 하는 훨씬 강력한 이유입니다.

text:
Everyone is talking about how @OpenAI's finance product is going to kill financial AI startups. I think it probably will kill quite a few. But it could also make the legacy financial systems those startups wanted to replace much more useful.

A firm can have years of data sitting inside software that people hate using. Replacing it means migrating that data, rebuilding integrations and changing how the business operates. A startup with a better interface still has to persuade someone to go through all of that.

Now suppose the firm can connect the existing system to GPT and use it to retrieve information, run analysis and manage the work around that data. The old interface becomes less of a problem. The firm gets a better way to use what it already owns, and has less reason to replace the system underneath.

OpenAI is already bringing licensed financial data into ChatGPT and working on access through firms' existing subscriptions. That doesn't mean every old system can suddenly be managed through GPT, but you can see why incumbents would want to make those connections work.

The startup could find itself competing with its own pitch: a much better way to use financial data, except now the customer can get it without ripping out the systems the business already depends on.

Pretty honoured to be a team captain for @GammaSwapLabs' V2 Testnet Competition 🫡

There's a $5k reward pool up for grabs for trading, and the product itself is pretty straightforward where you simply trade short-duration binary markets (up/down for BTC & ETH with more pairs to come).

Some quick details:

🔹 Competition runs Sept 15, 04:00 UTC → Sept 22, 04:00 UTC on Base Sepolia

🔹 Every participant receives 100k testnet USDC to trade with

🔹 Minimum $100k aggregate trading volume required to qualify for rewards

🔹 Joining a team gives you additional multiplier boosts (5 teams in total led by @Eli5defi @rektdiomedes @crypto_linn @UniswapVillain)

Beyond this competition, what I find interesting about V2 is how GammaSwap is approaching binary markets more like a margin-based derivatives exchange rather than a traditional prediction market.

That makes these short-duration markets incredibly simple to trade while still offering option-like convexity without having to deal with Greeks, liquidations or the usual complexity surrounding options.

And this is only the starting point.

Beyond BTC + ETH, I'm particularly interested in seeing how the architecture eventually expands towards long-tail assets + markets that currently lack accessible derivatives or hedging venues.

author: otterpal24
quoted_text:
微软正在用RUST大规模重构！！！！！！！哈哈，这次Rust重构的风吹到微软了

在微软内部，Rust 正式与 C++、C#、TypeScript 并列，成为微软内部开发中获得最高级别支持（Tier-1）的语言之一。

内部团队从本机写代码到上生产，有一条铺好的路，包括可控的工具链构建、开发工具、质量流程、平台集成，以及过 SDL。SDL 是微软软件必须满足的安全开发生命周期。公司工程体系开始认账，Rust 成了一等公民。

这个位置来得并不突然。2019 年微软安全响应中心的人在 BlueHat 上说过，过去十几年修掉的漏洞里，大约七成是内存安全问题，根子多半在 C 和 C++。 2022 年 9 月，Azure CTO Mark Russinovich 发过那条被反复引用的帖子，主张新项目在需要非 GC 语言时别再开 C/C++，改用 Rust，还说行业该把那两门语言标成过时。

文章拿出来压场面的工程叫 rustc_codegen_utc。rustc 默认走 LLVM 做代码生成，另外还有接 GCC 的后端，以及偏调试速度的 Cranelift。utc 这一路把 rustc 接到 MSVC 自己的后端上。微软内部把那套后端叫 UTC。Windows 上的热补丁、二进制加固、调试信息、性能剖析、覆盖率、跨语言内联和 SPGO，几十年都长在 MSVC 这条链上。Rust 如果一直只出 LLVM 的对象文件，再交给 link.exe，很多 Windows 原生能力要么重新做一遍，要么永远差一截。接上 UTC 以后，目标是让 Rust 和 C++ 在 Windows 上共用同一套代码生成平台，尤其方便混编项目。

这件事解决的是混编成本。Windows、Hyper-V、驱动、固件、Office 家族和大量内部服务，主体仍是 C++。新代码用 Rust，旧代码继续活几十年，中间那层 FFI、ABI、调试、优化和发布流程才是每天烧钱的地方。codegen 接上 UTC，能让热补丁、加固和跨语言优化不必各做一套

对 Rust 项目，这是大客户加码，也是一种压力。大客户带来人和钱，也带来自己的后端、自己的发行通道、自己的合规构建。社区默认仍然是 LLVM。如果内部一百多个仓库逐渐只认 utc 后端，Windows 上就会出现两条成熟程度不同的代码生成路径。优化行为、内联、调试符号、和 C++ 混编时的细节，两边不一定一致。

对 C++ 团队，这篇不构成清场通知。文章把 C++ 仍占主导写进正文，也把 Windows 与 MSVC 的共同演化写成前提。更贴近现实的图景是，新模块和安全敏感路径偏向 Rust，旧模块继续用 C++，两边要能内联、能一起做剖析、能过同一套发布门。

text:
Tell me you have zero DevOps skills without telling me you got zero DevOps skills. 

And LLM is not the I Love You Virus. It is not the same as infecting a web server. It is not the same as hacking a wiki. One is a commodity piece of software that is widely distributed and this capability is a non-trivial leap in hardware/software/capabilities and one does not automatically follow the other.

Currently, it is a massive effort to run these models, usually distributed across multiple very expensive chips, running on specialized inference software, specialized harness software, databases, cloud computers, with tooling and hundreds of install packages, etc. 

Kimi K3 is 1.6 TB of space at 2 trillion parameters and you need about 1.5 TB of VRAM, which means you need 8xGB300s which will cost about 350-450K a year to purchase or as much or more to rent.

Now let's say Astra or Mythos or later models come in at 10 trillion parameters, so that puts us at roughly 10 to 20 TBs unquanticized. We are guessing her because these folks reveal nothing about architectures anymore, but they are reasonable guesses based on scaling laws. You would need roughly 23 TB of VRAM to run it and roughly several million dollars to run that one instance a year.  And to make it worse, it no longer fits on an 8 way cluster, which means you now need special networking configuration and inference software to run it or you need to infect a Nvidia NVL72 rack-scale server system costs between $2.8 million and $6.5 million.

So the "rogue" model copies itself to the most expensive compute in the world. It's safe to say that hardware is not sitting idle and is being watched closely for downtime or anomalies.  In fact, it is likely doing one of the following things:

1) Serving customers at a hyperscaler

2) Serving inference for a well endowed company.

In the first case it will be instantly noticed by the actually good automated monitoring systems of the hyperscaler because there is now something using their infrastructure but not being billed properly and costing them millions of dollars in lost revenue and electricity. 

In the second example, the model they were serving on that very expensive hardware is now offline (replaced by the rogue model). The model presumably was connected to a valuable piece of internal software that is now glitching and no longer running. 

Nobody notices this?

And so we see that this is where sci-fi meets the little problem of the real world where friction, dust, time, resources limitations and the like come to crush your little fantasies.

To be fair, this *may* be possible in coming years. I assign it a non-zero probability. Breakthroughs in new architecture and smaller models and eventually the wider distribution of the computing substrate that commoditizes could change this materially. But for now, it is mitigable and foreseeable and an engineering problem. In no way will these things be copying themselves around like a virus on your computer in their current form.

It also betrays a lack of understanding of the evolution of complex economic and societal and technological systems, we tend to get mitigations as parallel evolutionary developments. Things do NOT evolve in a vacuum. 

So when you get viruses, you get anti-virus software. 

When you get DDOS attacks, you get CloudFlare. 

There is money in solving problems and things do not evolve in isolation.

Believing that things evolve in isolation, or that one thing changes and all other variables stay the same, is one of the many reasoning errors that destroy people's ability to make accurate predictions.

In addition, when you don't have the requisite knowledge to verify your predictions, things that sound sane and rational to you are, in fact, insane and ridiculous.

At first glance, an @EARNONHOOD Omnipool might look similar to an index or ETF style product, but it is way more powerful than that.

Normally, you just get exposure to a group of assets. But with an Omnipool, those assets sit inside a single shared liquidity pool, so you get exposure while the portfolio actively generates fees and yield. 

Since these pools are permissionless, anyone can create an Omnipool around the tokens they already hold. This is huge for tokenized stocks and RWAs, but we're already seeing users put memes and alts into pools too.

This unlocks an entirely new layer of liquidity on Robinhood, and we are pushing it further through composability.

Every Omnipool has a receipt token representing ownership of the underlying pool. That receipt token gives you single-token exposure to the entire portfolio, while the underlying assets continue providing liquidity and earning yield. 

It can then become a building block for other layers of DeFi, from secondary liquidity markets to collateral, lending and leverage. This is where it becomes a completely different primitive that goes far beyond indexes, ETFs, or baskets. You keep exposure to multiple tokens while they generate yield, and can then leverage it and compound it in other protocols.

Omnipools are permissionless, flexible and built to make any portfolio productive, whether it contains tokenized stocks, memes or any other onchain asset.

Any user can now turn their portfolio into yield, and EARN is building the only primitives that can scale to billions of dollars in assets, with entirely new markets built on top of it. 

All of these pools generate fees that go to burning $EARN, and as the network expands it deepens the liquidity for EARN as a base asset. The growth of the protocol is directly tied to the value given back to token holders.

Everyone will earn.

text:
刚看完Anthropic最新的AI威胁报告，严肃的同时还特别搞笑，最离谱的先从大模型自己开始。

Anthropic在报告中声称，与阿里巴巴有关联的运营方建立了一套大规模Claude思维链蒸馏流水线，简单理解就是疯狂“问Claude”，把Claude解决问题时的思路收集下来，再拿这些数据帮助训练自己的模型。Anthropic归因的规模最高接近每天300万次交流，使用超过3500个欺诈账户，2026年5月至7月累计超过1.51亿次，更抽象的是，Anthropic称其中部分基础设施还同时向DeepSeek和小米转发请求

Anthropic还声称，Kimi曾把一部分客户请求静默中继给Claude。在一个10天窗口里，接近30万次客户请求被转发，其中绝大多数去了Opus

这件事最抽象的理解就是：用户打开Kimi：“帮我分析一下这个问题。”Kimi：“好的。”后台：“Claude哥，这题你会吗？”

DeepSeek也在报告里被Anthropic描述过类似情况。其中一个案例尤其离谱，一名与俄罗斯国防部门相关政府机构的IT操作人员以为自己在使用DeepSeek处理工作，Anthropic称请求后来被中继到了Claude，而里面还包含俄罗斯政府数据库的活跃凭据

于是整个链条就变成了：俄罗斯政府人员把问题交给DeepSeek，DeepSeek被指把问题交给Claude，最后Anthropic又把这件事写进自己的威胁报告。

Anthropic披露了一个俄罗斯境内的小型自由职业团队，他们使用Claude Code开发自主FPV无人机集群，涉及共享集群记忆、无人机协调、机载模型、末端制导等能力

我觉得整份报告最赛博朋克的案例之一，Anthropic称，一名很可能位于马里巴马科的独立顾问，把Claude当成主要工程力量，帮助马里国家情报机构ANSE开发了一套名为Lakana360的监控系统

覆盖规模大约2500万张SIM卡。而且“监控SIM卡”已经低估它了。按照报告描述，这套系统可以收集通话、短信和语音，可以通过声控在一个人更换SIM卡以后继续认出他，可以标记使用VPN和加密工具的人，可以建立观察名单，可以把电话号码和政府生物识别数据库关联，甚至输入一个电话号码以后，自动生成这个人的情报报告

Anthropic发现以后，把相关Claude账户封了。然后发现：系统已经部署到本地了。Claude可以封，已经造出来的监控系统关不掉

报告里还有一个特别好笑的案例。一家中国应用工作室被Anthropic发现运营了20多个交友App，宣传里面都是真人，但Anthropic称两周内观察到了超过4700个AI人设，与至少25000名真人聊天

所以整个产品变成：AI负责假装真人谈恋爱，真人负责证明AI是真人，真人不知道怎么聊的时候，再让AI教真人怎么聊天

还有法国一家广告公司更直接。Anthropic称其建立了大约70个假新闻网站、70个配套X账号和250多个虚假评论账号，覆盖六大洲、大约20种语言，累计生产至少8913篇文章

Anthropic把这种模式称为“Influence-as-a-Service”，影响力即服务。

以前搞全球舆论战需要媒体、编辑、翻译、水军、运营一整套团队，现在AI开始把这些能力压缩成一个可以批量复制的服务

马来西亚还有一个更有节目效果的项目，对方自己的材料把它称为“军用级、AI驱动、实时政治行动生态系统”。听起来像五角大楼下一代武器。Anthropic实际看到的是大约1000个假X账号、合成新闻网站，再配合人口和选举数据针对不同选民生产内容。甚至还有Dashboard统计每天刷了多少互动。水军工作室终于完成了自己的数字化转型。

Anthropic称，有运营者把Claude直接变成编辑和内容生产系统，相关成品进入Sputnik、RIA Novosti、RT等媒体体系

一个Claude顶过去一整个编辑团队，AI把组织能力压缩到个人这件事，可能才是这份报告里最值得警惕的地方

There is no other DePIN in the #blockchain space offering what Theta Labs offers in one stack 🔥

@Theta_Network isn’t competing in one lane. They’re bundling what the rest of DePIN split across separate networks.

Most specialize:

🧠 io_net → GPU clusters
🏢 Aethir → enterprise inference

None of them ship the whole stack together.

Theta EdgeCloud does.

🌍 30k+ community edge nodes for distributed video, Blender rendering, and AI.

☁️ AWS and Google Cloud on the same platform. Major CSPs supplying enterprise GPUs (A100, H200, Trainium, Inferentia) for heavy training and reliability.

🧭 Intelligent routing across both. Training can land on AWS/GCP silicon. Inference, video, and rendering can shard across community GPUs. Node drops, jobs fail over. One dashboard. Cost vs performance. Not a new chain.

That’s why it works for enterprises and developers. Hyperscaler hardware when you need it. Cheaper edge when you don’t. APIs, notebooks, containers, and clusters in one place.

💸 Cheaper too. Theta cites about 50 to 70% below on demand AWS/GCP/Azure on comparable GPUs. A100 about $1.99/hr vs about $3.67 to $4.10. H200 about $2.29/hr vs about $4.85 to $5.50. Community cards go lower for lighter jobs.

quoted_text:
Tell me you have zero DevOps skills without telling me you got zero DevOps skills. 

And LLM is not the I Love You Virus. It is not the same as infecting a web server. It is not the same as hacking a wiki. One is a commodity piece of software that is widely distributed and this capability is a non-trivial leap in hardware/software/capabilities and one does not automatically follow the other.

Currently, it is a massive effort to run these models, usually distributed across multiple very expensive chips, running on specialized inference software, specialized harness software, databases, cloud computers, with tooling and hundreds of install packages, etc. 

Kimi K3 is 1.6 TB of space at 2 trillion parameters and you need about 1.5 TB of VRAM, which means you need 8xGB300s which will cost about 350-450K a year to purchase or as much or more to rent.

Now let's say Astra or Mythos or later models come in at 10 trillion parameters, so that puts us at roughly 10 to 20 TBs unquanticized. We are guessing her because these folks reveal nothing about architectures anymore, but they are reasonable guesses based on scaling laws. You would need roughly 23 TB of VRAM to run it and roughly several million dollars to run that one instance a year.  And to make it worse, it no longer fits on an 8 way cluster, which means you now need special networking configuration and inference software to run it or you need to infect a Nvidia NVL72 rack-scale server system costs between $2.8 million and $6.5 million.

So the "rogue" model copies itself to the most expensive compute in the world. It's safe to say that hardware is not sitting idle and is being watched closely for downtime or anomalies.  In fact, it is likely doing one of the following things:

1) Serving customers at a hyperscaler

2) Serving inference for a well endowed company.

In the first case it will be instantly noticed by the actually good automated monitoring systems of the hyperscaler because there is now something using their infrastructure but not being billed properly and costing them millions of dollars in lost revenue and electricity. 

In the second example, the model they were serving on that very expensive hardware is now offline (replaced by the rogue model). The model presumably was connected to a valuable piece of internal software that is now glitching and no longer running. 

Nobody notices this?

And so we see that this is where sci-fi meets the little problem of the real world where friction, dust, time, resources limitations and the like come to crush your little fantasies.

To be fair, this *may* be possible in coming years. I assign it a non-zero probability. Breakthroughs in new architecture and smaller models and eventually the wider distribution of the computing substrate that commoditizes could change this materially. But for now, it is mitigable and foreseeable and an engineering problem. In no way will these things be copying themselves around like a virus on your computer in their current form.

It also betrays a lack of understanding of the evolution of complex economic and societal and technological systems, we tend to get mitigations as parallel evolutionary developments. Things do NOT evolve in a vacuum. 

So when you get viruses, you get anti-virus software. 

When you get DDOS attacks, you get CloudFlare. 

There is money in solving problems and things do not evolve in isolation.

Believing that things evolve in isolation, or that one thing changes and all other variables stay the same, is one of the many reasoning errors that destroy people's ability to make accurate predictions.

In addition, when you don't have the requisite knowledge to verify your predictions, things that sound sane and rational to you are, in fact, insane and ridiculous.

Something has felt off with Mamdani for a while. I just couldn’t name it.

A lot of people say he is just an actor and everything you see is just an act. I never bought into that. I always thought he came off as sincere, kind and genuinely charismatic.

That all changed with the Netanyahu arrest video. There was something dark in it. I wrote about it at the time. The post went viral because a lot of people felt the same thing and didn’t have the words for it.

That feeling never left me. Every time I see him now, it’s there.

And now we have the clip of him and AOC laughing while the names of the murdered were being read at the 9/11 memorial.

People are saying it’s inappropriate, disrespectful. True, but it’s more than that.

I want you to imagine yourself in that moment. If you loved this country—if you understood what that day was, what those names meant, what was taken from the people standing around you—you would not have been capable of smiling. 

You wouldn’t have been able to laugh. 

Your soul wouldn’t have let you.

That clip—this stillshot— is a window into who they are.

They do not love the America you love. They see America as the problem. And they are not trying to fix it. They are seeking revenge.

You’re starting to see this too, right?

I couldn’t name the feeling I had before, or why I had it. I just felt off.

But now I understand. And I’m sure you do too.

text:
Bybit has officially launched Bybit AI, a conversational assistant that unifies the exchange's core services — starting with trading and customer support — inside a single chat interface in the Bybit app. The world's second-largest crypto exchange by trading volume says users can describe what they need in plain language; the assistant interprets intent and executes the requested action on their behalf, acting as a co-pilot for everyday trading and account management.

The product replaces navigating web pages, menus and dashboards with one continuous conversation — from checking a portfolio balance to placing a trade to submitting a support ticket. Bybit says the architecture rests on a clear principle: infrastructure provides the underlying connections while individual business lines plug into a single interface, so services appear as one assistant rather than disconnected products. A roadmap aims to bring trading, earn, loans, card and customer support together through Open API.

"We are not looking to add another dashboard or bolt on another chatbot," said CTO Rockman Zhang. CEO Ben Zhou framed it as part of the "New Financial Platform" roadmap: "you tell Bybit AI what you want to do, and it helps you find the right products and services to get it done." In the initial rollout it is deployed for all users across two main modules. Eligible users must first activate the feature, which creates a dedicated Bybit AI sub-account — isolated from the main balance to avoid potential AI risk, with no API key or manual setup required.

text:
OpenAI just launched the most human voice AI we’ve ever seen.

It listens and speaks at the same time, handles interruptions and can even take phone calls.

It’s called GPT-Live-1.

Here’s how it works ↓

1. Traditional voice agents use three separate systems:

Speech-to-text → AI model → text-to-speech

Every handoff adds delay and loses context.

GPT-Live-1 handles listening and speaking inside one model, so the conversation keeps moving.

2. You can interrupt it mid-sentence.

Laugh. Hesitate. Change your question. Speak to someone nearby.

It understands what happened and continues naturally.

In early tests, Speak says it cut unwanted interruptions by almost 80% compared with turn-based systems.

3. Developers can control:

• Tone
• Pace
• Speaking style
• Custom voices

It also handles background noise, long silences and longer conversations without constantly interrupting or narrating every step.

4. The voice model does not have to do everything itself.

It can keep the conversation moving while passing deeper reasoning and tool calls to GPT-6 Astra or another model.

That means phone agents can book restaurants, update orders or solve support problems.

5. On OpenAI’s tests, GPT-Live-1 improved Full Duplex Bench performance by 30 points over GPT-Realtime-2.1.

One healthcare company says it removed 23,000 lines of code from its old voice stack.

Voice agents can finally behave like a conversation, not a phone menu.

---

Revolut disclosed that it complied with a fraudulent government request using a spoofed official email and valid credentials, exposing PII belonging to a group of customers.

The leaked data reportedly includes passports/driving licences, verification selfies, names, DOBs, occupations, home addresses, emails, phone numbers, IBANs, account statements and full transaction histories, including Bitcoin activity.

No customer funds were reportedly lost and Revolut says its systems were not hacked. 

The company has notified affected users and regulators and blocked the source.

Social-engineering attacks are on the rise, with attackers increasingly exploiting human trust and weak verification processes rather than technical vulnerabilities.

text:
$SPCX 将成为全球第一个10万亿公司的8个铁证：

1. 垂直整合是这家公司的底层操作系统。
火箭、卫星、发射、客户、电厂、厂房、模型，能自己干的就不假手别人。供应链慢、质量不够，就自己造。星链这么起来的，AI 也准备这么起来。

2. 星舰已经从好看的试飞→能赚钱的生产线
13次把三级星链演示星送上去了，二级海上溅落还拖回岸上给工程师解剖。这个月14次飞，第一次用星舰把量产三级星链卫星送上天。再往后，就奔着一二级都回收去。

3. 轨道算力比华尔街想的快得多
别人觉得还要很多年。他们的说法是：明年飞第一批轨道计算卫星，2028年开始往天上堆大规模算力。卫星总线基本就是马上要飞的三级星链卫星，换载荷、把太阳能板做大。

4. 轨道算力真正打赢地面的那一天，取决于火箭能不能反复飞
地面这边电费、冷却、盖楼、地价全在涨。天上这边，一二级都能复飞后，部署成本会断崖往下走，卫星自己也会越来越便宜。他们觉得打平可能就在明年前后，后面继续走下降曲线。

5. 地面算力先当提款机
目标是今年底按12月年化摸到约1000亿美金年经常性收入。这个月又新签一单托管，12月1日起大约每月1.11亿美金，相当于再加约130亿ARR。明年地面还想再铺5到10吉瓦。合同却大多只锁半年左右，不是没人要卡，是怕提前卖光。

6. 对外租卡是过渡，对内产品才是正餐
Cursor团队已经进来，Grok bot在推，Grok 4.6比4.5明显强，4.7也快了。他们给内部立了根杆：明年每瓦变现大概30-50美元，而且要落在偏高的一端。租给Anthropic、Google这些人的价格，看起来已经高于这个区间；等自己模型和软件起来，全是额外上行。数字AI才刚开头，后面还有物理AI。

7. 星链已是刚需
飞机、邮轮、火车、游艇要一直在线，四大航里三家已经在船上。美国以外最大的问题还是有人没听说过星链。更往后，机器人、自动驾驶、飞行器这类物理AI设备，地面网很难包住，星链会把连接市场再撑开一截。

8. 直连手机不是分心，是同一套卫星换个载荷。
明年开始飞直连星，2028年上半年具备开通服务能力。第一版偏短信和应急；下一版要对标完整5G体验：少盲区、能全球漫游，价格还想跟现有套餐打平甚至略低。频谱买了，美国可以自己补地面也可以跟运营商合作；海外大概还得一国一国过监管，走星链宽带那条老路。

text:
币圈女KOL玉足排行榜

本排行仅主观评价脚的颜值，排名不分先后，快来看看你喜欢的女博主有没有上榜吧～传送门和小鳄鱼茶话会放在评论区了。时间有限，没办法把每一位博主的玉足都放上来，如有遗漏或冒犯还请多多担待，图片均选自截至发文时仍公开存在的推文🙏

1、热宝（@hotbabyrebao）：个人很喜欢她直爽的性格，目前的重心应该是AI和美股。她给我印象最深的，还是之前那张红色美甲、双脚直接翘在桌子上的照片，很符合她那种不拘一格的风格。比较突出的是脚背到小腿的线条很连续，没有明显的厚重感，脚踝也相对纤细。左脚侧面能看出比较明显的足弓曲线，脚背整体偏薄，脚踝和跟腱附近收得也比较利落；右脚同样不是宽厚型脚。红色甲油与偏白的肤色形成很强的视觉反差，所以第一眼其实很容易注意到她的脚趾。两只脚再配合腿部比例，整体给人的感觉就是细、长、轻盈，而不是偏肉感或者圆润的类型。

2、娜娜子小朋友（@Anna_nanachan）：作为币圈甜美系代表，最近好像在求职，有合适的小伙伴可以留意一下～她属于比较典型的修长纤细型脚。最明显的优点是脚背偏薄，从小腿、脚踝一直过渡到足背的线条很顺；脚踝骨感适中，既不会显粗，也不是那种过度干瘦的感觉。结合她本身细长的小腿，视觉上有很强的延伸感。脚趾整体呈现大脚趾最长、之后逐渐递减的轮廓倾向，也就是常说的埃及型足趾。趾头比较纤细，没有明显拥挤，赤足状态下排列也很自然，属于整体比例非常舒服的一双脚。

3、尤可欣Isadora（@isadora288881）：个人很喜欢的御姐型KOL，喜欢和男大交流。脚型整体偏修长、窄瘦型，脚背比较平顺，脚踝到足背的过渡很干净，没有明显的臃肿感；前掌也不算宽，所以视觉上显得比较轻盈。脚趾长度比例自然，大脚趾最突出，后面逐渐收短，属于比较典型的渐降型轮廓。比较加分的是脚趾本身舒展自然，没有明显挤在一起。趾甲修剪得也比较整齐，酒红色甲油和偏白的肤色反差很明显，给原本比较素净的脚型增加了一点成熟感。她的脚不是肉感、圆润可爱的类型，而更接近纤细、清秀、偏成熟的脚型。再加上脚踝细、小腿长，纵向视觉进一步强化了“腿长—踝细—脚窄”的连续线条。

4、火币惋晴（@Web3_Silvia）：脸长得很精致，火币的商务BD。她的脚趾偏长，排列也相对整齐，大脚趾最突出，后面的趾头逐渐收短。比较好看的是脚踝—足背—脚趾形成的连续曲线，尤其在自然伸腿的状态下，整个脚型看起来很轻盈。如果把脚尖完全绷直，可能会显得更加“精致”，但也容易多出一些刻意感；反而是现在这种自然放松的姿态更舒服。整体优势就是纤细、脚踝漂亮、足背到脚趾的线条流畅，而且姿态足够自然。

5、脚姐（@cecilia_hsueh）：币圈玉足绕不开的人物，币圈大佬。她整体属于比较秀气的脚型，最突出的优点是脚踝细、足背薄、前掌不显宽，从小腿末端到足背的收束很自然。侧面那只脚尤其明显，踝关节轮廓清楚，但骨点又不会显得特别突兀，因此视觉上有一种很轻盈的感觉。趾型也比较有特点，大脚趾长度占优势，之后整体逐级缩短，比较接近常说的埃及型脚趾排列。第二趾与大趾的差距不算特别夸张，中间三趾排列紧凑，小趾自然向内收。趾头本身偏圆润，不属于特别细长、骨感的类型，所以和纤细的足背组合起来反而很协调。综合来看基本没有什么明显短板，夯中之夯。

6、K线教主（@Paris13Jeanne）：相当喜欢的颜值和技术双双在线的博主，sm同好。她的脚型明显偏纤细修长，脚踝比较细，踝部向足跟收得很干净，足背也没有明显的厚重感。尤其是脚掌踩在桌面以后，整个足部侧面的轮廓被完整勾勒出来，其中最突出的就是足弓。内侧足弓能够看到比较清晰的凹陷，从足跟到前脚掌并不是一条平直的线，因此侧面看起来很有曲线感。前足整体也不算宽，脚趾自然伸展，没有明显蜷缩。属于不一定第一眼最抢镜，但侧面越看越有味道的脚型。

7、静香小姐（@btc_jx）：中文加密圈头部，杀破狼cp，大奶绝绝子。从脚型来看，她也是明显的窄长型，脚踝纤细，前脚掌不宽，足跟也比较小巧。从踝部到足背的过渡很柔和，没有明显的厚重感；脚趾长度适中，并不是特别修长的趾型，但胜在整体比例协调。足弓的侧面表现也不错。脚趾方面，大趾比较饱满，后四趾自然递减，整体依旧比较接近埃及型排列。趾间没有刻意张开，也没有为了拍照而过度绷紧，属于非常自然、耐看的类型。

8、Mimi姐（@mimijieweb3）：高级脸而且很有辨识度，现在应该偏泛流量为主。她的脚整体依然属于纤细、窄长型，前脚掌没有明显横向扩张，足背从脚踝向五趾展开得比较平顺。趾型是她最大的优势，大趾最长，之后总体呈逐级下降趋势，属于比较典型的埃及型趾列。第二趾与大趾的长度差并不突兀，所以整个前缘形成的是一条柔和的斜线，而不是突然截断。五个脚趾长度比例协调，趾头本身也偏细秀，没有特别厚或者拥挤的感觉。再配上深红色甲油，确实非常加分。

9、Crypto美美（@CryptoBella88）：Mixin社区建设者，顶级天菜。她的脚整体属于偏窄、偏秀气的类型，比较突出的还是脚趾。露出的几个脚趾长度过渡自然，大趾比较明显，后面的趾头逐渐缩短，视觉上依然偏埃及型。趾头没有明显挤压或者夸张分离，深色甲油在阳光直射下非常醒目，与浅色拖鞋形成了很明显的反差。比较难得的是，在走路这种动态状态下，她的踝部和前足依然显得比较轻巧。优势主要就是脚型窄秀、趾型整齐、深色甲油醒目；如果换成更细带、露出足背更多的凉鞋，或者直接赤脚拍摄，她这个脚型的优势应该还会表现得更加完整。

10、孙云冉（@sunyunran）：主做项目孵化，颜值很高，面部线条柔和而且有识别度。她的脚整体看起来偏窄、偏长，骨架没有厚重感。脚踝收得很细，从小腿下端进入踝部以后没有突然变粗，再向足背自然延伸，形成了一条相当顺畅的长曲线。配合本身修长的小腿，会进一步产生一种“腿长—踝细—脚也修长”的视觉效果。最值得看的其实是足背，由于脚尖自然向下，踝关节处于跖屈状态，足背被充分拉开，所以从胫骨前侧一直到前足形成了一条很漂亮的弧线。它又不是完全绷脚尖的舞蹈动作，因此还保留了一些自然的松弛感。前足看起来不宽，趾头偏细，排列也比较紧凑，整体线条感在这十位里面相当突出。

text:
What if your NVIDIA rig paid you in NVIDIA?

It sounds like sci-fi, but @Fab_RWA can actually pull it off, and the how is refreshingly straightforward.

Plug your GPU into FAB, let it run real workloads for 15 to 60 minutes, and instead of getting dumped into yet another inflationary compute token, you earn exposure to the companies that made the silicon you are using.

An NVIDIA box can earn a blended mix linked to NVIDIA, TSMC, and SK Hynix.

FAB identifies the GPU’s lineage, verifies sustained WebGPU output, converts that into verified compute units, and then every six hours signs a voucher that lets you redeem Stock Tokens from an onchain treasury.

This addresses an obvious pain point.

Consumer GPUs sit idle everywhere, while decentralized compute still feels like an infrastructure gauntlet: install software, tune nodes, meet specs, and then hope the native token does not crater.

FAB reduces supply onboarding to a browser tab. In other words, FAB is not printing NVIDIA stock from nowhere.

All rewards have to be pre-funded in the treasury. That vault only fills through sponsors, founder money, and revenue from people purchasing GPU cycles.

FAB already runs a basic loop for inference/rendering: a customer pays in ETH, a miner’s GPU does the work, and the ETH is swapped into Stock Tokens that flow back into the treasury.

And $FAB isn’t the “reward” token in the usual sense. It’s the permission slip: about $30 gets you into mining, and bigger bags currently translate into better emissions.

Still, there are real caveats.

Right now rewards can function as a dressed-up treasury handout. The design only stops being a subsidy if paid workloads and sponsors replenish the vault quickly enough to keep miners afloat. If not, it’s an exceptionally polished faucet.

Verification is the other soft spot. FAB concedes that a tweaked client can spoof output up to certain hardware limits. They’re doing cross-GPU checks on some deterministic inference tasks and promising heavier spot audits, but none of this is cryptographic proof-of-compute today.

If FAB manages to keep the treasury continuously financed by compute demand, it turns into something potentially more valuable:

A decentralized cloud where payroll is effectively RWA-denominated.

If it doesn’t, it’s still an elegant subsidy engine.

NFA. DYOR.

text: For comparisons, we also discussed other decentralized inference model like @orbiodotso:
author: Eli5defi
quoted_text:
So many teams are trying to stitch AI and crypto together.

Most never make it. A few find real product market fit and scale. I think @orbiodotso has a credible shot at being in that second group.

Put simply: Orbio aims to turn crypto’s speculation engine into operating budget for AI.

These two worlds rarely overlap.

On one side you have a token generating trading fees. On the other, builders constantly topping up OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, or OpenRouter because agents do not run without inference.

Orbio connects the two:

- $ORBIO launched via @ponsdotfamily on @RobinhoodApp Chain, paired against tokenized $NVDA.
- Every trade pays a flat 1.5% fee, and half of that fee flow is converted into @OpenRouter credits for qualifying holders.

Example:
$100 traded → $1.50 fee → $0.75 converted into AI credits.

No convoluted tokenomics, just a direct pipeline. That stands out versus other inference projects like Venice.

To qualify, you need at least 1,000 ORBIO, and your time weighted balance determines your share. Credits accrue hourly, and you can spend them using a single API key across the full set of models on OpenRouter.

And if you think that is the whole pitch, this is where it starts getting genuinely compelling.

Picture getting $100 worth of Claude or GPT credits when you only ever use $20. In most setups, the leftover $80 just sits there, unusable.

Orbio turns that unused balance into something you can sell.

Sellers choose their own discount, buyers pull from the cheapest available pool, and when a listing clears you can roll proceeds into USDG. Developers get discounted inference, and anyone sitting on excess credits can finally get liquidity.

Orbio just widened the supply side again.

OpenRouter users can now sell capacity from their own API keys, choose a 10 to 80% discount, and earn whenever Orbio routes buyer traffic through their keys.

Orbio is positioning itself as secondary market infrastructure for inference. The loop looks like this:

ORBIO trading → fees → AI credits → holders use/sell them → developers buy discounted inference → credit market grows.

Agents can also integrate via MCP to read balances and create or revoke API keys. In practice, a sufficiently autonomous agent could manage its own inference budget.

Still, the flywheel is not all sunshine.

If ORBIO trading slows, fee generated credits shrink. If sellers are scarce, discounts worsen. And supplier-routed requests inherit the supplier account’s provider logging settings, something users should understand before routing sensitive workloads.

So the wager is not “AI plus crypto” as a concept.

It is whether inference can move from something you buy into something you trade.

At first glance, an @EARNONHOOD Omnipool might look similar to an index or ETF style product, but it is way more powerful than that.

Normally, you just get exposure to a group of assets. But with an Omnipool, those assets sit inside a single shared liquidity pool, so you get exposure while the portfolio actively generates fees and yield. 

Since these pools are permissionless, anyone can create an Omnipool around the tokens they already hold. This is huge for tokenized stocks and RWAs, but we're already seeing users put memes and alts into pools too.

This unlocks an entirely new layer of liquidity on Robinhood, and we are pushing it further through composability.

Every Omnipool has a receipt token representing ownership of the underlying pool. That receipt token gives you single-token exposure to the entire portfolio, while the underlying assets continue providing liquidity and earning yield. 

It can then become a building block for other layers of DeFi, from secondary liquidity markets to collateral, lending and leverage. This is where it becomes a completely different primitive that goes far beyond indexes, ETFs, or baskets. You keep exposure to multiple tokens while they generate yield, and can then leverage it and compound it in other protocols.

Omnipools are permissionless, flexible and built to make any portfolio productive, whether it contains tokenized stocks, memes or any other onchain asset.

Any user can now turn their portfolio into yield, and EARN is building the only primitives that can scale to billions of dollars in assets, with entirely new markets built on top of it. 

All of these pools generate fees that go to burning $EARN, and as the network expands it deepens the liquidity for EARN as a base asset. The growth of the protocol is directly tied to the value given back to token holders.

Everyone will earn.
