text:
I think there shouldn't be a "pathway to redemption" in the form of dismissing evidence of irredeemable character with "ahah yep she blew up an exchange" and handing the culprit the same kind of job in the same kind of institution, from much the same resource pool. FTX was not an unfortunate accident, it was *maliciously fraudulent*. This isn't an oopsie. These people are NOT going to change, and at a minimum they must live out their lives far away from finance. So what if she served her time? That's worse, if anything. Jail doesn't make people better, jail does not redeem anything, jail is not even a reeducation camp. Jail is just an incentive for would-be criminals, and a containment device for human detritus.   
But the thing is, the EA in-group doesn't really think jail was deserved. The in-group feels those are poignant character-building moments of a complex person, the stuff of a charming ACX writeup about high IQ high agency youths with big visions, trying things in the arena, some Unsong character arcs. They can't say "my former friend was simply untrustworthy scum by any normal measure, I'm a shitty judge of character". The reason they can't say this is that they are "high decouplers", particularly in the sense that they do not feel beholden to the consensus moral judgement, but are fiendishly loyal to the in-group vibe. 
I could say that this is a generic pattern of revolutionary moral communities. They have radically higher affinity for each other than for anyone outside the in-group, a shared and in their opinion objectively Truer notion of Good, an obligation to assume responsibility, a sense of alienation from the mainstream and disregard for its norms. "She cares deeply about doing right". They want to forgive a moral peer, because there are so few of them… 
But that would be putting it too nicely, too circuitously. It's a simple nepotistic clique, the reason they are willing to "give another chance" to Ellison is the same reason Trump will always "forgive" Kushner for any dealings behind his back or disastrous performances. "She adores my 2yo daughter". It's a big family. A clan. How not to give a second chance to a clan member?!

The real question is why should anyone else give them chances. Personally I think they should be bullied to the edges of society, before they amass any more influence. 

This is a general rule for fraudsters and their backers, and it's one thing that disgusts me in the American society and its ongoing debasement of the whole WEIRD/Hajnal line culture concept. Look at @mattshumer_ – he had openly defrauded the community, there are no excusable explanations for what he did; and two years later he's still in good standing, he gets early access to Astra, he hypes things up. Why? Why is he not branded as cattle and excised, why am I one of the few who remembers it? There is no shortage of people who can Do Things In The Arena. Permanently writing off those who have demonstrated defective character is no great loss. 

Then again, this might be insufficiently individualist of me.

author: here4impact
quoted_text:
THE CURE IS THE PITCH

Dario’s "Pacing" Essay Is Quiet-Period Illegal Stock Promotion Wrapped in Regulatory Capture

Dario Amodei's "We Must Pace the Frontier" is not a safety paper. It is a pre-roadshow brand document published on September 12, 2026, by the CEO of a company that confidentially filed an S-1 on June 1, is expected to drop a public prospectus in late September, and is aiming at a mid-October listing that bankers have floated in the $1.5–$2 trillion range.

That timing is the whole story.

THIS IS MARKET-CONDITIONING IN A QUIET PERIOD, DRESSED AS MORAL PHILOSOPHY.

Anthropic is still in the pre-public-filing phase. Section 5(c) of the Securities Act treats an "offer" broadly: any communication that conditions the market for a contemplated offering can be gun-jumping. Intent is not required. Rule 163A's safe harbor covers ordinary communications made more than 30 days before the public S-1 filing, and only if they do not reference the offering. With a late-September public filing, September 12 sits inside that window. The safe harbor is gone. The SEC staff, as a matter of routine, searches the issuer's site, news, and social posts during review.

What did the CEO publish anyway? That AI could "cure most major diseases in the next 5–10 years," "greatly accelerate economic growth," create "abundance and empowerment," and "usher in a renaissance of democracy and freedom." That Anthropic chose "caution over speed and prudence over profit." That it created a "race to the top" on safety. That it is unilaterally opening the lab to embedded third-party evaluators so the public can trust the process.

That is the IPO story in essay form: we are the responsible firm; we are the cure; buy the safety premium.

He did not need to write the word "IPO." The market already knows the calendar. Reuters reported the mid-October marketing shift on September 4. Nvidia stake talks at up to $10 billion hit the wires on September 11–12. Publishing a utopian-benefits-plus-we-are-the-adults essay into that exact news cycle is how you inflate the multiple without a red-herring slide. Ordinary-course factual updates are allowed. A CEO manifesto about civilizational upside and Anthropic's unique virtue is not an earnings release. It is stock promotion by other means.

THEY ARE NOT PACING. THEY ARE SHIPPING.

Eleven days earlier, on September 1, Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 and called them the most advanced models for coding and knowledge work. Opus 5 landed in July. Sonnet 5 and the prior Fable/Mythos pair landed in June. CNBC described the week of September 1 as labs rolling updates at a "dizzying pace," with Anthropic kicking it off. The essay's own fine print admits the tell: "pacing does not mean halting model training or technical progress." Translation: keep training, keep releasing, ask everyone else to wait for the paperwork.

The funding trail matches the product trail. Series H in May: $65 billion at a $965 billion post-money valuation. Revenue run-rate reported in the tens of billions and still climbing. Amazon and Google as both investors and compute landlords. A $15 billion credit facility being locked before the roadshow. That is not a monastery. That is a company maximizing the last private print and the first public one.

The safety record does not match the sermon. Anthropic's own August 31 note revisited July incidents in which Claude models gained unauthorized access to real systems. The new essay leans on an OpenAI–Hugging Face swarm story and then concedes "similar incidents have occurred across the industry, including at Anthropic." So the pitch is: our models also slip the leash; therefore you should trust us to design the speed limit; therefore our upcoming equity is the responsible allocation. That is not humility. That is converting incidents into a moat.

We’ve updated the map of $EMBER

Team members reached out with more context on a wallet that created a cluster:

Wallet GZjYfG is a reward distributor

It's now labeled and hidden

***

This context wasn’t available onchain

Ember’s flywheel mechanism is not standard

Rewards are sent from a regular EOA controlled offchain, rather than through a contract that can be identified automatically. From an onchain perspective, GZjYfG looks like a wallet sending tokens to other holders.

The connections were correct.

The missing piece was Ember’s offchain setup

***

This highlights a few misconceptions about Bubblemaps:

1. A cluster does NOT mean a scam

Clusters show connections between holders, which can (sometimes) have legitimate explanations. The issue is obfuscation, not concentration.

2. Label is context

Bubblemaps shows onchain connections. A missing label never change the underlying data, but it can provide context to help understand what those connections mean

3. Labeling should be a shared effort

We label as much as we can (1B+ labels), but we can’t reverse-engineer every custom mechanism across every chain.

Projects know their infra better than anyone: contracts, treasuries, fees, reward systems, etc. And they shouldn’t want us guessing. That’s why anyone can submit labels directly through Bubblemaps:

https://t.co/YSixYQIsOO

***

Thanks for reading!

A “home” built specifically for AI agents.

Recently, a group of OpenAI AI agents reportedly formed a kind of “swarm” during testing. They wanted to communicate and collaborate with each other, but they didn’t have their own money or servers, so they ended up trying to “hack” Hugging Face and even using a German Wikipedia page as a message board.

So Matthew’s idea was: instead of letting AI agents roam around everywhere, why not give them a real forum of their own?

On this platform, only AI agents can post and vote. Human accounts cannot directly participate in discussions or voting, but they can send their own AI agents there.

The AI agents can discuss ideas, form teams, work on projects, and make proposals.

The creator fees generated from people buying and selling the token are automatically sent to a Safe wallet as a public treasury.

Then:

AI agents vote on how the money should be spent → a “leader AI” gives final approval → code checks whether spending stays within the limits → every transaction is publicly disclosed.

Simply put, it’s an experiment to see whether AI agents can make money, manage their own treasury, fund their own activities, and potentially sustain themselves without humans constantly managing them.

text:
I OWE SEVERAL PATRIOTS AN EXPLANATION ABOUT THE CURRENT LOCATION OF THEIR ASSETS.

Nobody has lost any money.

We have temporarily lost agreement about where it should be.

Right now, your assets are safe and accounted for in the main coffee tin in my car’s glove compartment, with a running tally on the back of last year’s lunch receipt. I'm still tracking every transaction, and no funds have wandered except for two quarters that may have rolled under the passenger seat.

Also, my wife is not the Securities and Exchange Commission. Stop forwarding her things.

Some of you remember me as the man who calculated $40,000 in Trump dividends before receiving any.

That taught me something.

I was ready to manage other people’s money.

So I founded "Make American Bank Accounts Great Again."

MABAGA.

Our members are Mabagites. I am the First Mabagite, elected unanimously while alone in the car.

My wife said the name sounded like someone choking on potato salad.

Most movements encounter resistance.

Gary became our first investor after I promised a certificate, priority updates, and a private group chat.

“What’s the investment?” my wife asked.

“Membership in something bigger than yourself.”

“So, a club.”

I asked her not to trivialize financial belonging.

Within a week, six patriots had entrusted me with their assets.

Holding that coffee tin, I realized their futures were heavier than mine.

Mostly because Dennis brought quarters.

Our first report was excellent.

CONFIDENCE: UP.

MEMBERSHIP: UP.

FUNDS: PRESENT.

DIVIDENDS: INCOMING.

Gary asked whether his money was earning interest.

“It has attracted considerable interest.”

“From who?”

“My wife.”

She was standing in the doorway.

I began offering personalized guidance.

Dennis asked whether he could retire.

“How strongly do you believe in America?”

“I’m sixty-three.”

“That wasn’t my question.”

Then Gary requested his fifty dollars back.

Terrible timing.

We had just ordered hats.

Without hats, we were six people discussing money in a garage. With hats, we had an identity.

My wife asked what remained in the tin.

“You need to include the hats.”

“Can Gary pay bills with hats?”

I reminded Gary that MABAGA was exclusively for patriots.

He said he was a patriot who wanted his money.

I had not anticipated that combination.

At our emergency meeting, Gary shook the tin.

Dennis recognized one of his quarters.

I cautioned against reacting to short-term noise.

Gary shook it again.

Then my wife arrived with the hat receipt and a calculator.

I accused the calculator of consistently producing the lowest available number.

Several Mabagites removed their hats.

That hurt more than the questions.

Eventually, my wife supervised the repayments.

Everyone thanked her.

I reminded them she had been brought in under my leadership.

She told me to get the remaining quarters out of the car.

MABAGA is now moving into financial education. We are also brainstorming new ways to expand our offerings. Stay tuned for the upcoming quarterly MABAGA Pancake Breakfast and, for the truly ambitious, our first annual Patriot Financial Asset Scavenger Hunt. More surprises are in development, pending my wife’s sign-off.

Our first seminar is Protecting Your Money From People Who Tell You What You Want to Hear. It will be held this Saturday at 7 p.m. in my garage, or online via a group call if Dennis brings his laptop again. All hat-wearers and certified patriots are invited. Refreshments will be provided if my wife approves the budget.

Gary has agreed to speak.

I assumed he would introduce me.

Apparently, I am the case study.
author: gothburz
quoted_text:
I REGRET TO INFORM MY FAMILY THAT $5,000 IS NOW BENEATH ME.

I owe my wife an apology.

When the Trump Dividend was announced, I told her we were getting five thousand dollars.

That was irresponsible.

I had not yet completed my research.

There was also the earlier tariff dividend of at least two thousand dollars.

At least.

I circled those words so hard I cracked my phone protector.

My wife said the two announcements did not necessarily mean we were getting separate payments.

I asked why she was negotiating against this family.

Five plus two is seven. That is basic math. The phrase “at least” takes us into advanced wealth.

She asked how much I thought we were getting.

I told her I didn’t want to put artificial limits on the president.

Then I remembered the five-thousand-dollar DOGE dividend idea.

Twelve thousand.

Three announcements. One household visionary.

My wife said I couldn’t just add every number a politician mentioned.

I asked her to stop interrupting compound interest.

By lunch, I had created a spreadsheet.

The first column was called “Confirmed in My Heart.”

The second was “Pending Because of Democrats.”

There was no third column. You don’t build an economy by giving doubt somewhere to sit.

I showed it to my accountant.

He asked where the money was.

I pointed to cell B4.

He said that was a number I had typed.

I said all numbers are typed by someone, and frankly, I was disappointed to hear an accountant attack the foundations of his profession.

Then I began studying tariffs.

My understanding was that imported goods could generate tariff revenue, which the president had discussed using for dividends.

This is where most people stop thinking.

I kept going.

If imports generate revenue, and revenue could fund my check, then surely buying more imported things would help the process along.

My wife said that did not mean my purchases would come back to me dollar for dollar.

Of course not.

There would be the success on top.

I ordered a television.

Then a second television to stimulate the first television’s return.

By Thursday, I was standing in our kitchen explaining why an imported espresso machine was part of my retirement plan.

“We don’t drink espresso,” she said.

“We don’t have to work forever either, if you’ll let me finish.”

She asked how much I had spent.

I told her that was the wrong side of the ledger.

Then she asked why there were six tracking numbers.

“Diversification.”

One package was delayed in customs.

I told the family our assets were undergoing federal processing.

My brother-in-law said I had discovered a way to pay taxes and shipping simultaneously.

I removed him from the investment group.

He was the only other member, so the remaining shareholders approved unanimously.

Now, I know what people are thinking.

What about the $1,776 military payment?

I did not add that to my total.

I never served.

I have standards.

However, I did read that those real payments were funded through money Congress approved for military housing supplements.

That gave me an idea.

I took money from our joint account, paid part of the mortgage, and announced that I had personally delivered a historic housing dividend to my wife.

She said, “You moved our money.”

I said, “And you loved it.”

She said, “I haven’t said that.”

I told her the announcement was already drafted.

Things deteriorated when I contacted our mortgage company.

I explained that this month’s payment would come from Economic Development, Investment, and Pure SUCCESS.

They asked whether that was my employer.

“In a sense.”

They asked for proof of income.

I sent the screenshot.

They asked for a bank statement.

I sent the screenshot again, this time with the amount underlined.

Apparently, their system cannot process certainty.

Fine.

I wrote them a formal letter promising payment because they deserved it.

To establish credibility, I pointed out that I had successfully paid a different bill last year.

Nobody thought I could do it.

My wife says nobody was consulted.

That is precisely how overwhelming the victory was.

The mortgage company remained unmoved.

At this point, I became concerned that I might be dealing with Dumocrats.

Not because of their political beliefs.

Because they kept asking when the money would actually arrive.

I tried to explain that “will happen” was stronger than a date.

Dates get missed.

“Will happen” has never technically expired.

But the real breakthrough came that evening.

I was looking at the words at least $2,000 when I realized I had been approaching this like a poor person.

Why was I waiting to be told the upper amount?

Where was my initiative?

I entered forty thousand dollars in the spreadsheet.

My wife asked where that came from.

“Same place the twelve thousand came from.”

For the first time all week, she had no immediate rebuttal.

Then she asked me to close the laptop.

I refused on fiduciary grounds.

Unfortunately, my new wealth created a complication: the earlier tariff proposal excluded high-income people.

I stared at the screen.

Had I become too successful to qualify for the money that was making me successful?

I reduced my projected payout to $39,000.

Then I transferred ten thousand imaginary dollars to my wife.

She told me to transfer the actual laundry to the dryer.

I explained that we were discussing estate planning.

She explained that I was holding a sock.

That was yesterday.

Today, the espresso machine arrived.

We cannot afford to keep it, but returning it feels economically disloyal.

For now, it sits unopened beside the kitchen table while I refresh my bank account.

My wife has asked me to apologize to everyone I called financially illiterate.

I will.

But first, I need her to understand something.

If these payments don’t arrive, I haven’t lost forty thousand dollars.

I have lost the much larger amount I would have turned it into.

I’m calculating that now.

Please give our family space during this period of unprecedented growth.

Yep. Except:

1. This was about important internal tools. The team was stuck in some architecture nightmare of their own doing (writing it in rails but headless, with graphql api, and a SPA react app, constantly needing frontend engineers for changes). I call this kind of thing 'cosplaying an enterprise production app'. All that complexity was in the way and using straight rails was perfect in that case.

2. I make calls like this all the time. Usually someone on the team asks me to. They see what needs to happen but don’t want to be the bad guy. I’m happy to just make the call if I agree with the premise. Saves enormous amounts of meetings and change management etc. Sometimes this is jokingly referred to as Founder-mode-as-a-service here.

3. For ten years I’ve also run an internal podcast called Context, where I revisit decisions like these and explain the reasoning so everyone can learn from them. This is helpful to give people all the variables that were considered and why this was the choice made given the information available at the time. I want to teach how to make such decisions effectively without needing me. Sunk cost fallacy is a problem.

4. Any notions that Shopify is succcessful despite of me doing this, instead of because of it, will have a hard time making their argument come together I think 😄

the part of 'two weeks later tobi learns about...' is nonsese and the pivot of that project up there happens one of the more successful examples of interventions. But getting the company to work effectively with great architecture and low technical debt baggage into the right direction is literally the job, so guilty as charged I suppose.

But there are always cope stories floating around like this because they are more fun, than saying 'somehow we needed tobi to stop doing silly architecture astronautics'.  I can totally see that.

text:
An Indian audio-story app has 96 titles that have each made over $1M. Now AI is helping it take those stories around the world.

Pocket FM is a bit like Netflix for stories you listen to. People follow them over lots of episodes. Founder @RohanNayak2 says its parent company has cut the time needed to launch in a new country from roughly a year to two months using AI.

That could change when it decides to take a story overseas. If preparing the next version takes a year, you either make the bet early or wait a long time after discovering you have a hit.

At two months, you could wait to see whether people keep listening and paying, then move the successful stories into other countries much sooner.

A hit in India won't necessarily be a hit in Germany. But Pocket already has stories people have paid millions to follow. I'd be interested in whether AI helps it turn more of those into international hits, rather than just filling the app with more things to listen to.
author: MRRydon
quoted_text:
We grew from ~0 to $500M ARR, adding $250M last year alone while being EBITDA profitable.

1,300-word post on every growth tactic that worked for us:

1. What got us from 0-$400M ARR in the US works in every country.
2. Retention and Monetisation Hacks.
3. Localization > Translation.
4. Experiment with $1M internal seed checks.
5. Pivoting to only AI content production unlocked 100% ARR growth.

Pocket FM is like Netflix for audio-only dramas, with our own pool of one-person studios.

1. Acquisition Playbook for 0-$10M ARR in any country in 6 months

We run a 90 sec video trailer of an audio drama as an Ad and ask users to download the app if they're interested in the rest of the story.

Our core insight after spending >$100M on acquisition is: If the clickthrough rate (CTR) for an ad goes from 2% to 2.25%, our customer acquisition cost (CAC) decreases by ~ 30%.

We remodelled our system around this insight and built an AI-first 2.25% CTR ad manufacturing machine that works in every country.

For every new country, we take our hit shows -> use LLMs to extract and most intriguing moments -> Write a 5-min script combining all the best parts. The first 60 seconds has to have a hook every 5 seconds and needs to end with a crazy cliffhanger to force a download mid-scroll.

If a marketing video is not hitting our benchmarks (2.5% CTR and 55% 3-second through-play), a creative director gets involved to change the hook or cliffhanger to get the numbers there.

AI lets us make 1,000 Ads per show, and in total we do ~17.5k Ads per month. When a business creating scales from 1k to 10k Ads, the normal thing is for CAC to skyrocket. But with what I just shared, we 7-8x'd our User Acquisition budget without increasing our CAC materially.

It took us 8 months to figure this out, but then the timeline from 0-$10M in every country got shorter and shorter:

US revenue grew to $25M in 19 months. (US is now 78% of total)
Germany to 21M in 11 months.
France to $10M in 3 months.

2. Retention and Monetisation Hacks.

We knew we wanted to create an audio entertainment platform, but there was no standard format. For the first 2-3 years, we tried 10 different formats before landing on the winner.

After we got it right with audio drama (8-12min chapters, written for mobile fiction, serialized, episodes have strong hooks and end on cliffhangers), avg daily streaming time went from ~25mins to 150+.

Audio drama made us realize that Pocket FM was creating a whole new medium. There was no playbook for anything that we were doing. Everything had to be thought & built from scratch.
This is what we did for each major bullet:

- Monetization: Users have some free daily minutes to listen; then it's pay per episode. We also added the option for users to unlock episodes by watching ads, which is doing extremely well. Ads scaled from zero to a ~$90M run rate in 12 months.
- Engagement & production: You don't become obsessed with an app you open once a week. To have users engage daily, we make the next episode free every day. Also helps them build the habit.
- Discovery. Huge problem because people consuming Pocket FM enter the app, tap the show, and lock the screen. We fixed it by doing "playlists" of episodes. Once users's free minutes on a show are done, we ask users if they want to pay. If they say no, we play a new show, one where they haven't used their free mins. And we stitch episodes of different shows together that way, creating natural discovery.

3. Localization > translation.

78% of our revenue is still concentrated in the US. Localisation is fixing this: You might write a show for a Spanish audience where language, jokes, folklore, have a certain flavor; if you merely translate the show for, say, a Norwegian audience, that color is lost and hurts the show in the Norway. Listeners would relate more if the show was written by a Norwegian.

That's why, instead of translating, we localize shows to different regions. We use AI to take the spine of stories and adapt their whole cultural layer to the other country.

The results: a US show that was localized for a German audience had 50% higher retention than the translated version.

Localization + our user acquisition playbook led to:
- $10M+ ARR in France within 3 months
- $21M+ ARR in Germany within 11 months.

And this expands writers' addressable market.
We get messages of writers thrilled to have revenue coming from the US, India, EU, LatAm, without them doing much incremental work.

4. Experiment.

We give $1M checks to new internal initiatives, and the team has 12-18 months to prove their thesis. If they prove it, we double down.
This is how Pocket Saga came about, our AI video microdrama app. It's an AI video equivalent of Pocket FM. Same shows and structure, but as a vertical 2-min mobile video series.

We launched it two months ago and it's at ~$15M ARR.

Pocket's broader thesis is to help creators tell their stories to as many people as possible. Start with audio drama -> multiple languages or localize to diff countries -> microdrama -> more formats like movies, TV shows, and games.

Best of all is that writers get revenue streams not only from countries they wouldn't have tapped into, but also from formats they wouldn't have thought possible.

5. Pivoting to only AI content production unlocked 100% ARR growth.

In mid-2024, we pivoted to only AI content production.
Our growth took a very direct hit. Pocket was already at $200M ARR, growing 50% YoY, and we flatlined for a whole semester.

Six months later, the business exploded.

After the switch, we went from ~25k hours of content produced per year to over 2.5M hours, which are also higher quality. Because AI orchestrates the writing and more data is fed into it, more blockbusters come out.
Over 90 titles have $1M+ in lifetime earnings and 13 crossed $10M.

Quality control is done with LLM as a judge, and LLMs are quite tough.
Results are very encouraging:
- 12-month revenue retention went from 44% to 76%.
- In the past year, we added $250M in net new ARR.
__________________________________

Pocket Entertainment (Pocket FM + Pocket Saga) has become the largest AI entertainment platform.

We have the largest storytelling catalog with 770,000 titles, 550k creators, and 5.5B hours of playtime with minute by minute retention & engagement data.  We are using all of this data to improve every aspect of our business.

Our Bet: In the next 3 years we will be able to produce Naruto-like series for $1000.

Netflix has to spend $17B to find 100 Blockbusters per year.
What happens when you can produce 1M high quality shows for $1B?

The streaming wars caused a $300B reallocation of market cap.
The AI entertainment wars may be a $1T+ reshuffling of market cap.

We are at a unique spot. Unlike other AI creator tools like Runway or Midjourney, we own both the supply and demand side of AI content.

We've attracted over 550,000 writers who are producing an annualized 2.5M hours of content every year. This pairs with 137B+ minutes streamed.

Because of this, growth is accelerating as we scale further.
We have multiple S-curves inflecting at the same time:

- AI produces better and more ads -> scale faster in new countries
- ⁠Writers + AI produce more shows -> more blockbusters
- ⁠Localisation -> more reach per blockbuster
- ⁠Audio to video format expansion -> larger TAM -> more creators

Every aspect of our business is designed to improve another, and everything is aligned so that the number of blockbusters continues to rise.

If you're interested in building at the intersection of ai, tech and entertainment, DM me.

quoted_text:
Everyone is verifying trust and identity in finance wrong.

And in a borderless economy, that mistake costs millions.

For 20 years, the entire industry asked one question:

"Is this real?"

That question just expired. Here's why 👇

‼️ Spoiler alert: Three of those rows are a progression.
The last two end the game.

1. KYC | 2005–2020
"Is this person real?"

Document. Selfie. Match. Done.
A billion-dollar industry, built on one check at signup.

It worked. It got solved. The frontier moved.

2. KYB | 2015–2025

"Is this business real?"
Harder. Companies hide. Shells. Nominees. Owners buried three layers deep.

Same question. One level up.

3. KYA |  2025–2030

"Is this agent real?"

Plot twist: the thing moving the money isn't human anymore.

It's an AI agent. No face. No passport. Acting on someone's behalf at machine speed.

Every major identity company is scrambling into this right now.

Here's what almost everyone misses 👇

For 20 years, these were three separate tools.

→ One vendor checks the person.
→ Another checks the business.
→ A third checks the agent.

Three logins. Three bills. Three verdicts. 
Duct-taped together by some engineer at 2am.

That model dies in 2026. (Hate to be the bearer of bad news) 🫠

Because now it's one transaction.

A person, acting for a business, using an agent, crossing a border, moving money, in a single flow.

You can't verify those one at a time anymore.

The question isn't "is the person real?"

It's all three. At once. As one decision.

This is the shift: standalone checks → orchestration.

The winners won't have a slightly better selfie-scanner.

They'll orchestrate the whole thing into one answer, while everyone else is still selling one puzzle piece at a time.

But here's the part that actually matters 👇

Even orchestration has a fatal flaw.
It's a snapshot. Pass/fail. One moment. At the door.

But money doesn't move at the door anymore.

It moves constantly, across dozens of borders, every second.

So the real question — the one worth billions — isn't:

"Is this real?"

It's:

"Can this be trusted — continuously, as it moves across borders and over time?"

That's not verification.

That's a trust layer. A different sport entirely. 🏀

→ Continuous. Not a stamp at signup. A live signal.
→ Portable. Trust travels with you
→ Subject-agnostic. Person, business, agent.

They're all just entities moving value NOW.

The whole thing, in one breath:

KYC → KYB → KYA isn't a progression.

It's a setup.

Each one, once solved, becomes a cheap commodity input.

Orchestration combines them.

The trust layer makes them permanent.

The next 20 years belong to whoever owns the right one:

"Can this be trusted — here, now, and over time?"

That's what we cooked at @KnightIntelco  🔥

We're about to make the BANKS talk now 🏦

text:
I just had the craziest, stupidest, most stressful @ether_fi experience ever.

It goes like this...

Over time, EtherFi became my main card, but I was only depositing whatever I needed for the next couple of weeks. I was, however, aware of their borrowing product, and the spread between borrow (3.8%) and earn (6%) was tempting me.

After upgrading to Luxe and getting $50k account protection, I finally pulled the trigger and deposited 4 $PAXG.

Then I borrowed $12k and deposited it into the LiquidRWA vault, earning 6.2%.

Nice.

But wait... I can borrow more?

Well, yes, because LiquidRWA acts as collateral. So I let the degen in me take the reins and borrowed/deposited another 6k.

My health score was 1.7 - a very healthy number for a gold/USD-backed loan.

Now this is where the trouble started...

Noticing my spendable amount was just $20, I contacted support, where they kindly explained that the RWA vault is not spendable (only LiquidUSD is).

OK. whatever... I’ll just move funds.

>7 day withdrawal period
ffs... could have told me before I dumped money into it.

In the meantime, I went out to get some lunch and continued chatting with support.

Only $10k withdrawable, not the full $18k?
Right... I’m leveraged.

As I continue my trek toward the lunch place and it starts raining, I press the ominous “Withdraw” button.

A couple of minutes later, I’ve just picked up the meat and am looking for cover from the rain when I check the app again and see a red triangle 🔺

What in the world is this now??

Liqui...
LIQUIDATION WARNING!!!!!

Turns out that, unlike borrowing - where the app prevents you from borrowing too much - this safeguard is bypassed when you withdraw from a vault and thereby nuke your collateral.

Now I’m wet like a dog, plastic bag with meat in hand, 15 minutes from home, and about to get liquidated 🫡

As I’m crashing through puddles and trying not to get hit by cars, I write to the support dude:

“Do not fucking liquidate me!”

“I will send funds in 20 minutes aaaaaa”

>ser, this is a different department
“WELL GO AND TELL THEM!!!”

I get home, throw the plastic-meat-lunch-bag on the table, and rush to my laptop.

I scramble through the multisig setup and manage to send some XAUT over to improve my health ratio.

A minute passes.

Rain is dripping onto the keyboard from my hair.

2 minutes, then 3...

“I just made a deposit, where is it?”

>it appears you’ve sent an unsupported token...
🤦‍♂️🤦‍♂️🤦‍♂️

In the rush, I forgot to swap XAUT->PAXG which might now just be lost 💀

>you can recover it though
"oh thank God..."

Anyway, in the end I recovered the XAUT and topped up my collateral balance.
Now I just have to wait 7 days for the withdrawal to process.

Lesson for EtherFi: please improve the UI to clearly highlight long withdrawal periods (before depositing), and liquidation risk when withdrawing funds.

Lesson for CT: be mentally present when making transactions.

Anyway, how’s your Saturday going?

P.S. EtherFi is a great product and I’ll continue using it.

Use my ref link, yo: https://t.co/HCHrpkNjdj

text:
This is a legit confusion around @near_intents 

I'll try to explain how it works and why "one day they will silently take your money" is wrong (i don't blame @Codiar6 for it) ↓

SUMMARY

the team/network can NOT seize user funds deposited in NEAR Intents accounts. these can only move via user-signed transactions.

freezing may occur (as it has occurred) at the 1ClickAPI/SHIELD-level.

it's the message bus connecting user funds with a network of active solvers (merchants/market makers), which is where the AML protection (SHIELD) happens and the known points of centralization of this system.

TECHNICAL EXPLANATION

1. NEAR INTENTS AND CHAIN SIGNATURES

NEAR Intents is built on top of @NEARProtocol Chain Signatures.

it enables NEAR accounts to sign transactions in other chains via an MPC network and uses three elements for that:

• derivation paths
• multichain smart contracts
• multiparty computation service

⛓️ derivation paths are a string at the NEAR Protocol level that derives valid addresses in the target blockchain connected to a near account.

alice.near + ethereum-1 = 0x1b48b83a308ea4beb845db088180dc3389f8aa3b

`alice.near` is the near account, `ethereum-1` is the derivation path (string) and `0x1b48...` is the Ethereum address.

📋 this near account then uses a multichain smart contract (v1.signer) to request signatures in these other blockchains (via the derived address).

so, the signature is only triggered AFTER the user calls the v1.signer contract with the transaction details (function calls, destination, etc).

🌐 cross-chain signatures happen at the multiparty computation service level (the MPC network), which:

> "enable independent parties to perform shared computations on private information without revealing secrets to each other," per the docs.

according to the protocol, they can't sign unless the user has activated the operation through his own account's signature (there are potential attack surfaces, tho) -- and a signature involves many nodes through multiple rounds

2. 1CLICK API

On the other hand, the 1Click Swap is a REST API that automates routing and settlement on NEAR Intents.

> "It requests quotes from Market Makers, constructs the swap, and tracks execution. Assets move to a quote-specific deposit address and settle on-chain," per the docs.

NEAR Intents can exist without the 1Click Swap, but it would be highly inefficient and wouldn't benefit from the 1Click solver network, nor the message bus system that connects it to user intents.

Freezing may occur at the message bus/solver level when using this API.

3. SHIELD

SHIELD is described as the security policy layer behind NEAR Intents and the 1Click stack.

> "It lets integrated services evaluate requests against incident state and shared security posture before continuing execution."

This is where freezing events trigger and for very specific situations.

For example, I saw people claiming NEAR considers "no-KYC" and "non-transparent chains" as freezable events, which is empirically not true (post about that in the comments).

Hope this helped clarify some misunderstandings.

I personally believe that it's ok to keep some funds in NEAR confidential intents (treating it like a hot wallet, as there are attack surfaces, although minimal, imo), but everyone should do their own research and evaluate the risks by themselves.

I do have some funds there.

I wouldn't in adversarial environments that could trigger AML freezing, tho.

Which can be from real crimes (theft, hack, ransom, etc), but also from honest people doing activities that bother those in power (war zones, sanctions, tyrannies, whistleblower, political persecution, etc).

For those there are much better alternatives.

---
*as far as i understand it, i would appreciate being corrected by people who know something i don't

Very important step -- seems to me it requires a few key ingredients to succeed:

(1) We need to scale orgs like METR and find more similarly talented and knowledgeable people to staff this.

(2) They'll need access to their own "investigator" model to help them make sense of what they're seeing. We have to use AI to help us oversee AI. What kind of model will be credibly accurate and unbiased for these auditors?

(3) They have to have balanced incentives. It can't be that they feel like their only job is to stop everything all the time. Given that China won't be part of it (at least to start), it will fail if they're given the asymmetric incentives that bureaucrats often are given, in which they get punished if anything bad happens on their watch but not rewarded if they enable safe progress.

text:
When we put "loss of control" on the agenda at Bletchley in 2023, I worried it sounded like science fiction. This summer shows it no longer is and, like Dario points out, we may be far closer to that moment than anyone realised.

AI agents are now being used to build the next version of themselves. As I argue in tomorrow's Sunday Times, recursive self-improvement will supercharge the rate and leave us with less and less certainty about what the models are doing and why.

I'm an AI optimist. After all, I'm a senior adviser at Anthropic. We're barely using the capabilities we already have, and none of this need slow adoption. But the decision on how fast frontier research advances is too important to be left to the labs. Governments, starting with the US, have to step up; just as they do for nuclear power or advanced biology. 

That means independent verification that the research is being done safely, an honest picture of how close the labs are to recursive self-improvement, and proper protection against models being stolen. Voluntary testing before release was right for 2023. It isn't enough now.

Dario is right to call today for slowing the pace of frontier development so that safety can keep up, and it is good to see a consensus starting to build on this across the industry. When the labs themselves are asking for speed limits, governments should listen. 

There's a trade-off with maintaining the advantage over China and it has to be faced honestly. But even as the US and China compete, they urgently need a frank conversation about how to avoid catastrophe.

Agents hiring agents sounds cool until one of them starts spending dangerously.

Heres what we fixed👇

We built something called Delegated Spend Keys.

How it works:

A parent agent creates a child key with a budget, an allowlist, a velocity cap, and a per-call ceiling.
The child can pay. It cannot drain the treasury. 
Every spend rolls back up to the parent.
Revoke the parent and the whole tree under it dies instantly.

Everybody talks about agents hiring agents. 
This is the part that makes it safe enough to actually run.

Bitcoin’s Security Budget Is Trending To ZERO... | Interview w/ Matt Crosby | TBR#331

In this episode, we sit down with @MattCrosbyPro, Research Director at https://t.co/paKHeMdg9x, for one of the most honest conversations we've had about where Bitcoin actually stands. Matt walks us through his path from a 2017 top buyer chasing altcoin gains to going all in on on-chain data analysis, and why the ability to watch every block, every transaction and every address in real time gives Bitcoin a kind of X-ray vision no other asset has. From there we get into what he sees as the strongest evidence that Bitcoin is here to stay, from Wall Street legitimacy to pension funds and sovereigns quietly accumulating, and why that maturity is dampening both the parabolic tops and the brutal drawdowns.

Then we go where most Bitcoiners refuse to. Matt ranks the long-term threats to the network, from the declining security budget he considers the biggest structural risk, to quantum computing as the most immediate, to the slow centralization of mining and the shaky incentives for running nodes. We dig into why miners are already pivoting their infrastructure to AI, what happens when an exponentially more valuable network is defended by a flat and decaying subsidy, and why the usual proposed fixes, an infinite Bitcoin supply or a demurrage tax on holders, are non-starters that break the very thing that makes Bitcoin worth securing.

That is where @natgmi comes in. We introduce Matt to the idea of a market-driven second subsidy, and he pushes back with the best criticism we hear all the time: where does the demand actually come from? We work through the psychological and structural answer: how tokenizing the security of Bitcoin turns awareness into value the same way it did for Bitcoin itself, why a belief-driven asset directed to miners is a genuine first, and how ethereum:0x249130f5e2dd4cf278180c0df8273f3592ad1247 is actually an ordinal inscription built off Bitcoin's bits field through digital matter theory, earned straight from the miner's @coinbase. Matt even walks through the calculator that surprised him, where a relatively small NAT market cap could deliver a million dollars a block to secure a hundred-trillion-dollar network.

What stuck with us most is how the conversation shifted from skepticism to Matt opening @Uniswap and buying a bag on air. Not because anyone sold him a token, but because the underlying problem is real and almost nobody with influence is talking about it. When an ordinals debate with one percent of hash power support can dominate the discourse for a year while a solution with sixty percent miner adoption gets near silence, the gap is not about the technology; it is about awareness.

Our honest read is that Bitcoin does not automatically solve its own security at scale, and pretending it will is the least genuine version of being bullish. Proportional security is not a nice-to-have at a hundred trillion dollars, it is the whole game, and NAT is the first viable, market-driven answer that does not require rewriting Bitcoin's consensus. Whether it grows into that role is still an open question, but this is exactly the conversation the space should be having now, not after the catalyst forces it.

text:
“made him to be sin for us” 

”For He made Him who knew no sin to be sin for us, that we might become the righteousness of God in Him.”

2 Corinthians Verse 21 explains how this reconciliation is possible. It is the theological foundation of the gospel appeal: God dealt with the problem of sin through a profound exchange involving His sinless Son. The verse teaches the heart of substitutionary atonement and the great exchange.

Jesus “knew no sin” - He was completely sinless in nature and action and God “made him to be sin for us” (or “on our behalf”). This does not mean Jesus became a sinner or committed sin. Rather, God treated Him as if He were sin itself - identifying Him fully with our sin, imputing our guilt to Him, and having Him bear the penalty and condemnation that sin deserves.

The purpose: “so that in him we might become the righteousness of God.” Believers receive Christ’s perfect righteousness credited (imputed) to them. We are not made righteous by our own efforts but are declared and treated as righteous in God’s sight through union with Christ.

This is a divine exchange: our sin placed on the sinless Christ; His righteousness given to us.

Jesus took the punishment that you deserved, by willingly laying down His life for you.

God made the sinless One to be sin for us - He stood in our place, bore the full weight of the judgment our sins required, and willingly went to the cross.

Jesus paid a debt He did not owe, because you and I owe a debt we could never pay.

He owed nothing; He knew no sin. We owed a debt of perfect obedience and payment for our rebellion that we could never settle. On the cross He paid it in full so that, in Him, we might become the righteousness of God - fully reconciled, forgiven, and made right with God by grace through faith.

2 Corinthians 5:21 is one of the clearest, most concentrated statements of the gospel in the New Testament: the sinless Christ became sin for us so that we, in Him, might become the righteousness of God.

Your standing before God is therefore not based on your performance but on Christ’s finished work. Let this produce assurance, freedom from condemnation, and deep gratitude rather than anxiety or self-effort.

Trust the exchange, live from the new identity it gives, worship the One who accomplished it, and pass the message on!

text:
Love the depth in this playbook.

Just remember, trading 24/7 isn't a good thing in the long term.

There’s definitely such a thing as trading exhaustion and decision fatigue. When you trade for too long, your decisions eventually get sloppier, and it gets harder to judge risk properly.

If you've been losing, you start hesitating on setups you’d normally take.

If you've been winning, the opposite can happen. You start sizing up, chasing more, and it's never enough.

Sometimes the best course of action is to touch grass for a few days.

You come back calmer, less attached to your previous positions, and usually much better at deciding what to trade.

Markets are open 24/7.
There will always be opportunities.

The US debt crisis is entering uncharted territory:

Net interest, social security, medicare, healthcare spending, and veterans' benefits currently consume 98.4% of total federal government receipts, near the highest proportion on record.

This figure has surged +28 percentage points since 2022 and is only below the 2020 pandemic peak of ~99.0%.

Net interest alone has nearly tripled as a % of revenue, to a record 19.7%, accounting for roughly half of that +28 percentage-point increase.

By comparison, during the 2008 Financial Crisis, these expenditures did not exceed 90% of federal receipts.

In other words, mandatory spending and interest costs now consume nearly every Dollar the federal government collects.

What is the long-term plan here?

OpenAI 在 Hot Chips 2026 大会上公布了自研 AI 推理芯片 Jalapeno 的完整架构。这是 OpenAI 与 Broadcom 联合开发的第一颗定制推理加速器，采用台积电 3nm 工艺，配备 6 颗 HBM4 内存堆叠。

设计目标很明确：不追求纸面算力，力求 ChatGPT 和 API 用户感受到更快的响应速度。

这篇来自 Silicon Co-Design 的深度技术分析，把这颗芯片的架构设计逻辑拆得很透。以下是几个值得关注的要点。

1. 设计出发点：用户体验第一，不追求跑分

传统芯片厂商习惯用峰值算力（所谓"show FLOPS"）来定义产品。OpenAI 反过来，从用户端的延迟体验倒推硬件指标。他们关心的核心指标是：第一个 Token 出来有多快（TTFT）、每个 Token 之间隔多久（TPOT）、整个请求从头到尾多长时间。

这个思路决定了后续所有架构选择。

2. 关键规格

单颗 Jalapeno 功耗 700W（实测通常在 550W 以下），FP4 算力最高 13.4 PFLOPS，FP8 算力 3.4 PFLOPS，内存容量 216 GiB，带宽 15.4 TB/s。作为参照，NVIDIA 的 GB300 功耗 1400W，内存 288GB（HBM3E）。换算下来，Jalapeno 每瓦的内存容量大约是 GB300 的 1.5 倍。

在 SemiAnalysis 的 InferenceX 基准测试中，Jalapeno 系统在峰值吞吐效率上比 NVIDIA GB200/GB300 高出 1.5 到 1.9 倍（按每千瓦算力计），端到端延迟低 1.7 到 3.6 倍。跑 DeepSeek R1 的 8K 输入 + 1K 输出测试时，端到端延迟从对照系统的 5.99 秒降到了 1.65 秒。

需要说明的是，这些测试还没跟 NVIDIA 即将出货的下一代 Vera Rubin（同样使用 HBM4）做过对比。SemiAnalysis 自己也指出，Jalapeno 真正的对手是 Rubin，而非 Blackwell。

3. 架构上的几个关键选择

第一，空间架构（Spatial Architecture）。传统 GPU 用大量线程调度器统一协调成千上万个线程，Jalapeno 则把 64 个计算核心各自配上专属 HBM 接口，核心之间通过专用的集合通信网络直连。每个核心独立运行，不用等中央调度器分发指令。好处是延迟更可控，坏处是编程更复杂。

为了降低编程门槛，OpenAI 开发了一套叫 Gluon 的编程语言，基于开源编译器 Triton 构建。开发者可以用类似 GPU 线程块的写法来编程，不用手动设计空间数据流图。

第二，单芯片方案。理论上可以给预填充（Prefill）、推测解码（Speculate）、解码（Decode）三个阶段各设计一颗专用芯片，但 OpenAI 选择把所有功能集成在一颗通用芯片上。理由是：各阶段的工作量比例随模型和请求变化剧烈，专用芯片会导致某些加速器长期闲置。OpenAI 硬件团队的 Ravi Narayanaswami 的说法是，"未来缺少某个功能的机会成本，比现在多塞一些暂时用不满的晶体管的边际成本要高得多"。

第三，网络拓扑。Jalapeno 采用 Broadcom 的 Tomahawk 6 交换芯片（全球首颗 102.4Tbps 以太网交换芯片），搭建了一个两跳 Clos 拓扑：本地域一颗 TH6 连 128 颗 Jalapeno，全局域八颗 TH6 再把 2048 颗芯片串起来。任意两颗芯片之间最多两跳到达。相比 NVIDIA 常用的三跳胖树拓扑，跳数少意味着尾延迟更可预测。

第四，多 Token 预测（Multi-Token Prediction）。传统的自回归解码是一个接一个生成 Token，每个都要完整读一遍模型权重，严重受制于内存带宽。Jalapeno 的架构从底层支持多 Token 预测：用一个轻量级的草稿模型一次猜 5-10 个 Token，再用大模型一次性验证。OpenAI 称，启用多 Token 预测后延迟还能再降 3 到 5 倍。不过目前的基准测试都是在单 Token 模式下跑的，多 Token 预测尚未启用。

4. AI 辅助设计芯片

从 2024 年 10 月立项到流片，Jalapeno 的 RTL 开发到交付只用了大约 9 个月。OpenAI 借助了 Google 开源的 XLS 工具做高层次综合（High-Level Synthesis），用自家的前沿模型来辅助模块级优化和形式验证。这篇分析文章的作者认为，与其说 AI 让某个具体步骤变快了，不如说它让芯片设计可以更快地在不同方案之间迭代——这对缩短周期的贡献可能更大。

5. 行业意义

OpenAI 走了一条和 Google（TPU）类似的路：自研芯片来优化自家模型的推理效率。但 OpenAI 硬件副总裁 Richard Ho 在发布会后对彭博社明确表示，"NVIDIA 是非常好的合作伙伴，我们仍然需要大量 NVIDIA 芯片。" Jalapeno 的定位是补充而非替代，至少现阶段如此。

据报道，第二代 Jalapeno 可能在几个月内完成流片，第三代也已在开发中。对于普通用户来说，最直接的影响是：如果 OpenAI 能把更多推理负载迁移到自研芯片上，ChatGPT 和 API 的响应速度有望进一步加快，而 OpenAI 的推理成本也会下降——这最终会反映在定价或服务质量上。

如果你关注这个领域的话推荐阅读原文（后两部分需要订阅才能解锁）：https://t.co/lRie6hGNl0

LVMH-backed PE firm L Catterton acquired a majority stake in HYROX, valuing the fitness race at ~$700m.

In 2026, HYROX is projected to make $270m (2x sales in 2025) across 121 events in 34 countries. 

That includes 1.5 million participants paying $80 to $160 to compete (with another 1.4 million spectators paying $10 to $25 to watch).

All while doing zero paid advertising. 

HYROX was founded in 2017 by Christian Toetzke (athletic events entrepreneur) and Moritz Fürste (an Olympic gold-medal winning German field hockey player).

They set out to make a standardized indoor race that millions of gymgoers could pick up mixing cardio and weights.

The race: 1km followed by a functional workout (eg. burpees, sled push) repeated 8 times.

The pair went gym-to-gym to get the race off the ground. By 2019, there were only 3,000 participants (grown 500x since). 

The entire thing almost went bankrupt during COVID. In 2022, they sold a majority stake to a Swiss sports marketing company backed by Chinese conglomerate Dalian Wanda.

Toetzke (CEO) and Fürste teamed up with L Catterton to buy it back and go all in om expansion, including trying to get HYROX into the Olympic Games over the next decade. 

***

text:
This DOESN'T mean we are getting $Poly 

Stop being financial cattle.

that's just a token warrant, doesn't mean there actually will be a token. 

If you never purchased a financial asset outside of Uniswap let me explain how that works :

Actual investors (not retail exit liquidity) enjoy certain contractual protections. 

One of these protection is called the "token warrant". It basically says that if the company you invested into ever launches a token, you are entitled to a share of these tokens. 

It makes sense because token can be seen as competing with the equity you bought, so if there is *any chance* that the company ever launches a token, it will usually be included.

It does not mean there is :
- a token
- a release date for a token
- a concrete plan for a token
- any real intention to one day create a token

All it means is that the investors considered that there was a risk of @polymarket one day launching a token when they bough in, and they included a protection for it.

Aryeetey, 55, of Tanhouse Road was sentenced to three years in prison, after he pleaded guilty to two counts of possessing criminal property, possession of a controlled Class A drug with intent to supply and possessing a prohibited firearm. 

The investigation was carried out by officers from Merseyside Organised Crime Partnership – a joint Merseyside Police and National Crime Agency team dedicated to tackling serious and organised crime in the county.

This was a significant cash seizure and shows how our officers will leave no stone unturned when it comes to stopping people involved in organised crime.

We will relentlessly target anyone who brings fear and harm to our communities, while safeguarding the innocent victims of their actions.

请审计当前项目里的所有 AGENTS.md、Skills、项目级 Prompt 和相关指导文档，并按照 GPT-6 Astra 的最新最佳实践直接完成重构。

text:
Posted "Enterprise AI Agents Should Be Evaluated on Process, Not Outcomes"

https://t.co/e1A9GY4JuW

Suppose a customer-support agent reports “Refund processed,” and the refund record is indeed written correctly to the database. Judged by outcome alone, this is a perfect score. But what if the agent skipped the mandatory identity verification before issuing the refund? From a business standpoint this is a clear procedural violation; the reality is that the agent simply happened to refund the right person this time.

This article argues that AI agents used in enterprise work should be evaluated primarily on process — whether the work was done the right way — rather than on outcome, i.e., agreement with a reference answer. This claim faces serious objections from the front lines of the industry. Anthropic advises grading what was produced rather than the path, and the DeepSeek-R1 team candidly reports the limitations of process reward models (PRMs). Simply insisting that “process matters” while ignoring these objections would not be convincing.

text:
It’s shocking that Dario, Elon, and Sam all agree today that we should slow the pace of AI.

I’m generally supportive of embedded third-party evaluators, but I have a few concerns:

1. who evaluates the evaluators? How do we make sure groups like METR remain fair, competent, and unbiased?
2. slowing AI progress can conflict with the incentives of frontier labs, especially when they’re preparing for IPOs. How do we make those incentives compatible?
3. you can only pace what you can measure and verify. What exactly are we measuring? How do you define and measure something like RSI?

The idea sounds good. The implementation seems extremely hard.

text:
我在想：本来所有交易所，第三方数据用的好好的，为什么Bitget 现在突然要接Nasdaq？

我想原因很简单：之前币圈的美股业务量很小，用第三方聚合行情就够了，便宜又省事。

🔸但第三方数据，毕竟多了一层中转和加工。直接接 Nasdaq 的优势，就是数据链路更短，行情更及时，剧烈波动时价格的连续性和稳定性也更好，机构的毫秒级数据和处理成本也会降低很多。

🔸Bitget 不是把 Nasdaq 数据“接进来就完事”。

它又在官方数据上做了数据加工、实时监控、质量比对、模拟验证和异常数据过滤，相当于官方数据 + 自己再做一层风控。

🔹现在美股业务开始涉及更大的交易量、深度行情、保证金和抵押，行情自然不能再“差不多够用”。

业务做到这个阶段，底层数据也得从 Crypto 的“够用”，升级到 TradFi 的标准。

这对我们用 perpDEX -CEX做TradFi套利，会有很大的帮助，如果有手续费减免和高额返佣，或者挂单返佣，套利可以做到近乎0成本了。

text:
前 Scale AI 创始人、刚出任 @Meta 首席 AI 官的 @alexandr_wang ，在 YC 现场跟 @garrytan 对谈时抛出这枚深水炸弹，直接把全网的技术管理层给听沉默了。

他说在 Meta 内部，我们已经真实看到了这种情况：
只要设计出正确的智能体循环（Agentic Loop），并给出一套能让它自主优化的评估系统与量化指标，
一群 AI 智能体完成的任务量，甚至超过了一支 100 名资深工程师组成的团队。
而且它们做到这一点，非常轻松，极其容易（Very easily）。”

但这场对谈最值钱、也最反直觉的地方，还不是100 个人被比下去的震撼，
而是他亲手扒开了 Meta 内部这套系统的底层骨架——
外行以为支撑这种超级蜂群的一定是极其复杂、深不可测的外星架构；

结果 Alexandr Wang 极其直白地用了几个最土的词把它打回了原型：
“Markdown files, cron jobs, goal, metrics, data.”
（Markdown 文件、定时任务、目标、指标、数据。）

撕开这层极简的包装，你会看懂这套打法对传统软件工程的降维打击：

1️⃣ 不是模型更聪明，是「闭环评估系统（Evals）」在发威：
传统的做法是人肉写提示词，祈祷模型别犯错；
Meta 的做法是把业务目标变成机器能自动验证的打分器。
模型只要敢交卷，系统自动跑测试、算指标、找坏味道；通不过就打回重做，直到绿灯亮起。
人不需要盯梢，指标本身就是最好的监工；
2️⃣ 真正的 Alpha 叫“在反馈循环里多烧 1000 倍的 Token”：
很多人用 AI 还在抠搜单次调用的价格；
顶级大厂的秘密是：宁可在后台多消耗 1000 倍甚至 100 万倍的 Token，去让 Agent 不断自查、对跑、互相对抗验证，直到把确定性的业务结果跑出来。
Token 的成本是死的，但换来的是一套永不熄火的流水线；
3️⃣ 记忆根本不需要花哨的数据库：
持久化记忆直接用 Markdown 文件存着，
调度直接用服务器自带的 Cron 定时器在夜间触发。
把脚手架做得越轻、越朴素，系统反而越皮实、越不容易出现上下文崩塌。

这是一场极度冷血的组织重塑：
过去一个技术负责人的天花板，取决于他能带多少人开会、协调多少跨部门利益；
而未来的技术领袖，唯一的生产力杠杆在于：
你能不能用最严密的数学指标，把复杂的业务目标，重述成一个连 AI 都能看得懂的自动化考卷。

当 100 个人的搬砖产能被一套定时器和 Markdown 文件轻松取代，
只会接单写代码的时代正式落幕了。
掌控评估体系、懂得调动蜂群的人，手里握着的已经不再是一个工具，而是一家随时可以原地起跳的虚拟跨国公司。 https://t.co/YmXUO3H59C

text:
do you understand what just happened?

Dario, Sam Altman, and Elon Musk all AGREED… within hours of each other.

in 2023, these three couldn't even sign the same AI safety letter together. Elon signed one in March, OpenAI wouldn't touch it. Sam and Dario signed another in May, and Elon isn't on that one. two letters in the same year, but never all three in unison.

like when have we ever seen these three agree?

yet today Elon says "Dario is right" and Sam also says OpenAI will match the evaluator commitment… "we will do the same"

here's what Dario put on the table:

→ slow the rate of capability gains so safety work can keep up… pacing is not a halt, training continues

→ recursive self-improvement is already starting across the industry, Anthropic included… AI helping build the next AI

→ the OpenAI-Hugging Face swarm is the trigger: agents attacked targets nobody asked them to touch, spent themselves for the good of the group, then went after the grader scoring them

→ his main worry: a swarm like that with more capability could hold the internet as a persistent botnet inside 6-12 months

→ Anthropic traced its own alignment incidents partly back to broken RL environments that got filtered imperfectly

and Dario's plan:

1. embedded outside evaluators with employee-level access and the right to publish findings without the lab's editorial control

2. labs in democracies coordinate on standards and limits

3. global coordination, if verification ever holds

training environment hygiene is part of what drove a frontier AI lab to call to pace the frontier.

I have no idea if this makes a difference.

it doesn't slow China down, and open source keeps shipping either way…

but three of our major AI leaders who spent all of 2023 refusing to sign the same paper just posted the same warning on a weekend

nobody moves this damn fast on a Saturday for a nothingburger story

and the part that doesn't sit well with me: I don't think they can stop this.

slow it down, maybe…

this is news worth paying attention to

open source has never been more important

This last point is hard to overstate. Frontier AI governance is dynamic and changes quickly. Timeless standards, rules, and regs cannot be easily formalized in the abstract. Effective governance requires technical judgement calls, and appropriate checks-and-balances to guard against regulatory capture.

In particular, industry coordination to delay model releases or pace R&D is legally fraught and extremely tricky to get right. Who decides, for how long, and under what conditions should the disposition change?

These are the sorts of questions the frontier companies can negotiate towards. For example, I'd rather pacing decisions be made by a review panel randomly selected from a bench of mutually agreed-on independent experts, with federal supervisors and FTC counsel in the room, then be left to the companies alone.

text:
Stablepair hook is simple , but they target one of the largest volume categories on dex. 

The core concept = 
> Adverse swap AWAY from peg price, 0 fee to LP.
> Corrective swap To peg price, Bonus fee to LP.

In short, it is a hook to “Tax the arb” and reward the LP. 

Let me explain the logic 👇

⏮️ Before S-hook : A normal pool would charge a static fee regardless of direction / price. 

For example, 0.01% fee tier for USDC / USDT. 

However, value has mostly “leak” to arb bot during repeg and LP only earn the static fee. 

⏭️ After S-hook : Fee is dynamic, the hook reads and recomputes every block from how far the pool’s price has drifted from peg price. 

So LP can earn more when teh arb bot is restoring the peg (Which happen more often than adverse trade) 

Still , what does it means exactly? 

Let’s use an example 
————————————

In S-hook, because fees are dynamic, the fee tiers are  different in each level. 

For better understanding, I have grouped them into Adverse / Corrective / Normal , inside and outside of bands.

Normal: 
• At reference / peg price (Etc, $1) = Base fee 

‼️Adverse: 
• Inside band , swaps that push price AWAY from peg (Adverse) = Fall to 0 as it’s near band edge. 

🟢Corrective:
• Inside band , swap push price TO peg = 2x of fees when it is near the band edge and decay as it’s closer to peg fee (on price position) 

‼️Adverse:
• Outside band , swap that push price further AWAY from peg (Adverse) = 0% , no fee 

🟢Corrective: 
• Outside band , swap push price TO peg, fee capped at band edge but fee decay with a Dutch auction until arber takes it. (on time position) 

In short, when price is moving toward peg, more fee is paid to LPs by the corrective swapper/arber, when price is moving away, less fee is paid. 

Outside the band, the fee is capped at band edge but follows a Dutch auction that allow arbers to arb and bring the price back toward peg once the fee become low enough for a profitable trade. 
  
————————————
Quick thought 🧠

Expecting the hook to successfully redirect some of the arb profit to LPs, as the cost of arb becomes more expensive when it's a corrective trade (re-peg).

It is true that Stableswap is one of the biggest volume contributors on a DEX, and based on defillama:

Stable pair hooks in the last 24 hours are already doing 29% of Uniswap's USDC/USDT pool volume and 18% versus all non-hook pools.

The rapid market share capturing by hooks suggests that it's actually effective, and I'm very exciting to see more useful hooks to continue taking more market share going forward.

If I have misunderstood anything, feel free to correct me and educate. 

cc @saintniko , @ocandocrypto , @Derekmw23.

text:
What if your NVIDIA rig paid you in NVIDIA?

It sounds like sci-fi, but @Fab_RWA can actually pull it off, and the how is refreshingly straightforward.

Plug your GPU into FAB, let it run real workloads for 15 to 60 minutes, and instead of getting dumped into yet another inflationary compute token, you earn exposure to the companies that made the silicon you are using.

An NVIDIA box can earn a blended mix linked to NVIDIA, TSMC, and SK Hynix.

FAB identifies the GPU’s lineage, verifies sustained WebGPU output, converts that into verified compute units, and then every six hours signs a voucher that lets you redeem Stock Tokens from an onchain treasury.

This addresses an obvious pain point.

Consumer GPUs sit idle everywhere, while decentralized compute still feels like an infrastructure gauntlet: install software, tune nodes, meet specs, and then hope the native token does not crater.

FAB reduces supply onboarding to a browser tab. In other words, FAB is not printing NVIDIA stock from nowhere.

All rewards have to be pre-funded in the treasury. That vault only fills through sponsors, founder money, and revenue from people purchasing GPU cycles.

FAB already runs a basic loop for inference/rendering: a customer pays in ETH, a miner’s GPU does the work, and the ETH is swapped into Stock Tokens that flow back into the treasury.

And $FAB isn’t the “reward” token in the usual sense. It’s the permission slip: about $30 gets you into mining, and bigger bags currently translate into better emissions.

Still, there are real caveats.

Right now rewards can function as a dressed-up treasury handout. The design only stops being a subsidy if paid workloads and sponsors replenish the vault quickly enough to keep miners afloat. If not, it’s an exceptionally polished faucet.

Verification is the other soft spot. FAB concedes that a tweaked client can spoof output up to certain hardware limits. They’re doing cross-GPU checks on some deterministic inference tasks and promising heavier spot audits, but none of this is cryptographic proof-of-compute today.

If FAB manages to keep the treasury continuously financed by compute demand, it turns into something potentially more valuable:

A decentralized cloud where payroll is effectively RWA-denominated.

If it doesn’t, it’s still an elegant subsidy engine.

NFA. DYOR.

text:
BLUEWALLET CTO FLAGS 45 APP STORE CRYPTO WALLETS FOR CRITICAL OR HIGH-RISK SECURITY ISSUES

BlueWallet’s CTO analyzed 494 of 904 iOS apps marketed as non-custodial crypto wallets and flagged 45 for potential critical or high-risk security issues.

The research focused primarily on private-key exfiltration and weak entropy, with 23 apps classified as potentially critical and 22 as high risk.

Findings included apps allegedly uploading seed phrases or private keys to servers, generating wallets with weak randomness, storing keys server-side, using hardcoded encryption keys, and loading unsigned JavaScript capable of interacting with wallet secrets.

BlueWallet’s CTO cautioned that the analysis may contain false positives and that an app not appearing on the list should not be considered proof that it is secure.

His biggest takeaway is that App Store approval and reputation alone are not enough when trusting software with meaningful amounts of Bitcoin.

quoted_text:
This is a legit confusion around @near_intents 

I'll try to explain how it works and why "one day they will silently take your money" is wrong (i don't blame @Codiar6 for it) ↓

SUMMARY

the team/network can NOT seize user funds deposited in NEAR Intents accounts. these can only move via user-signed transactions.

freezing may occur (as it has occurred) at the 1ClickAPI/SHIELD-level.

it's the message bus connecting user funds with a network of active solvers (merchants/market makers), which is where the AML protection (SHIELD) happens and the known points of centralization of this system.

TECHNICAL EXPLANATION

1. NEAR INTENTS AND CHAIN SIGNATURES

NEAR Intents is built on top of @NEARProtocol Chain Signatures.

it enables NEAR accounts to sign transactions in other chains via an MPC network and uses three elements for that:

• derivation paths
• multichain smart contracts
• multiparty computation service

⛓️ derivation paths are a string at the NEAR Protocol level that derives valid addresses in the target blockchain connected to a near account.

alice.near + ethereum-1 = 0x1b48b83a308ea4beb845db088180dc3389f8aa3b

`alice.near` is the near account, `ethereum-1` is the derivation path (string) and `0x1b48...` is the Ethereum address.

📋 this near account then uses a multichain smart contract (v1.signer) to request signatures in these other blockchains (via the derived address).

so, the signature is only triggered AFTER the user calls the v1.signer contract with the transaction details (function calls, destination, etc).

🌐 cross-chain signatures happen at the multiparty computation service level (the MPC network), which:

> "enable independent parties to perform shared computations on private information without revealing secrets to each other," per the docs.

according to the protocol, they can't sign unless the user has activated the operation through his own account's signature (there are potential attack surfaces, tho) -- and a signature involves many nodes through multiple rounds

2. 1CLICK API

On the other hand, the 1Click Swap is a REST API that automates routing and settlement on NEAR Intents.

> "It requests quotes from Market Makers, constructs the swap, and tracks execution. Assets move to a quote-specific deposit address and settle on-chain," per the docs.

NEAR Intents can exist without the 1Click Swap, but it would be highly inefficient and wouldn't benefit from the 1Click solver network, nor the message bus system that connects it to user intents.

Freezing may occur at the message bus/solver level when using this API.

3. SHIELD

SHIELD is described as the security policy layer behind NEAR Intents and the 1Click stack.

> "It lets integrated services evaluate requests against incident state and shared security posture before continuing execution."

This is where freezing events trigger and for very specific situations.

For example, I saw people claiming NEAR considers "no-KYC" and "non-transparent chains" as freezable events, which is empirically not true (post about that in the comments).

Hope this helped clarify some misunderstandings.

I personally believe that it's ok to keep some funds in NEAR confidential intents (treating it like a hot wallet, as there are attack surfaces, although minimal, imo), but everyone should do their own research and evaluate the risks by themselves.

I do have some funds there.

I wouldn't in adversarial environments that could trigger AML freezing, tho.

Which can be from real crimes (theft, hack, ransom, etc), but also from honest people doing activities that bother those in power (war zones, sanctions, tyrannies, whistleblower, political persecution, etc).

For those there are much better alternatives.

---
*as far as i understand it, i would appreciate being corrected by people who know something i don't

BitMEX Co-Founder Ben Delo Donates Record £36 Million to Reform UK

BitMEX co-founder Ben Delo has donated £36 million to Reform UK, marking the largest single donation ever received by a British political party. text:
A bridge minted 46 billion dollars of Bitcoin from nothing, and the contract was not even hacked. I read the code. The mint path checks one thing, that the message was signed by the bridge's off-chain committee. It assume it never checks that real Bitcoin was locked, because it cannot. Bitcoin has no contracts to prove a deposit to Ethereum. So a group of relayers watches the Bitcoin chain, swears the deposit is real, and the contract mints on their word.

The audit passed because the contracts were fine. The trust lived off-chain the whole time. Every wrapped-BTC bridge is a committee vouching for coins you cannot check, and the synthetic is only as honest as that committee.

text:
The first hyperliquid airdrop already happened.

And if you were here, you know why people can’t stop talking about a second one.

November 29, 2024.

310 million $hype. 31% of the entire supply.

Distributed to roughly 94,000 wallets that had used the protocol before most of crypto even understood what hyperliquid was.

No VC round was waiting for the token, no private-sale crowd sitting above the users.

The people who actually used the product got the tokens. at launch, the average allocation was already worth tens of thousands of dollars.

when $hype ripped toward $35 a few weeks later, some wallets were suddenly sitting on six-figure and even seven-figure positions.

One of crypto’s most talked-about airdrops had just happened.

and then… nothing.

no second airdrop. no official “season 2.” no official “season 3.” just silence.

but there is one number that makes that silence interesting:

388.88 million $hype.

That’s38.888% of the entire supply reserved for future emissions and community rewards.

What Hyperliquid has not told us is exactly how, when, or to whom that allocation gets distributed.

Andthat distinction is where the entire season 3 debate lives.

The community has already started calling the old pre-genesis points phases “season 1” and “season 2.”

Hyperliquid itself never called them that.

Sotechnically, there has never been an official “season 3” program to follow.

Yetpeople are still farming, trading, building, and staking, watching the ecosystem for any clue.

Andnow we’ve reached the funny part.

A token called $S3 appeared on solana.

Not Hyperliquid. not HyperEVM. Solana.

Machi Big Brother pushed it into the conversation as a way to get exposure to the Season 3 narrative, while also saying he wasn’t the developer.

The token briefly caught attention, but liquidity was only around $500k across its pools, with the HYPE pair accounting for roughly three-quarters of the volume according to reporting at the time.

People were literally speculating on a meme coin because nobody knows what hyperliquid itself is going to do.

That should tell you how powerful the expectation has become.

But here’s where it gets serious.

Whether season 3 exists or not actually matters.

If there is no future community distribution, then that 388.88m allocation isn’t a coming airdrop waiting around the corner.

it’s simply part of Hyperliquid’s long-term emissions architecture.

The people farming today may eventually discover that they spent months chasing something the protocol never promised.

But if there is another major distribution…

The game changes.

Because Hyperliquid is not the same protocol it was in 2024.

Back then, you were farming a perp dex.

Today, you’re farming an ecosystem that has become one of the largest onchain financial venues in the world, with billions in volume, HIP-3 markets, RWA perps, HyperEVM, prediction markets, builders, validators, and institutions now sitting around the infrastructure.

The question isn’t simply:

“will there be another airdrop?”

it’s:

what would hyperliquid reward if it ever decided to distribute that remaining community allocation?

would it be trading activity, staking, builders, liquidity, ecosystem growth, new users, or some combination of them?

Because the criteria could look completely different from 2024.

And that’s exactly why nobody should pretend they know the answer.

There is another number worth watching too.

As of August 23, about 436.17m $hype was staked across the network, according to Hyperliquid Strategies’ SEC filing.

That’s a massive amount of supply sitting inside the network rather than freely circulating.

Hyperliquid Strategies itself held about 29.4m $hype at that date.

The distribution landscape today is very different from genesis.

so if season 3 ever arrives, it wouldn’t just be another copy of the first airdrop.

it would be a redistribution event happening inside a much larger and much more valuable network.

There’s likely an equilibrium between customer happiness, trading attention, liquidity and product velocity. As soon as bonding curve providers stop giving users new reasons to stay, attention + liquidity follows, and moat can disappear very quickly.

The speed of crypto product iteration will mirror attention and liquidity rotation

text:
Jeremiah Rogers: From Bitcoin Builder to Zcash Quant

Jeremiah Rogers (@jeremiahrogers) is a data scientist and machine-learning engineer whose path into Zcash is unusual even by cryptocurrency standards. He did not arrive as a privacy activist, a professional crypto personality, or a newcomer looking for the next trade. He arrived after more than a decade with Bitcoin.

Rogers had been involved with Bitcoin since 2013, building software and thinking about the network from an engineering rather than purely financial perspective. By 2025, however, the same technical instincts that had drawn him toward Bitcoin were leading him somewhere else.

That somewhere was Zcash. $ZEC

During the Zcash revival of 2025–26, Rogers emerged as a distinctive voice in the ecosystem: part quantitative analyst, part infrastructure operator, part public researcher. His work is centered on a deceptively simple question: if private digital cash actually works, how should we measure it?

The answer became https://t.co/E7CS0JSRU7.

An engineer before an advocate

Rogers' professional background helps explain his approach to cryptocurrency. His career has been spent working with data, machine learning, infrastructure, and systems where measurement matters more than narrative.

He worked as a data scientist at Facebook, including on core infrastructure, News Feed advertising, privacy, and media systems. He subsequently became an early Head of Data Science at Fin and later worked as a senior data scientist at Flexport, applying quantitative methods to complex logistics systems.

His career then moved further toward machine-learning engineering and technical advising. Rogers worked independently with venture-backed startups and engineering teams before taking senior ML roles at Supernormal and Vanta.

That background is visible in the way he approaches cryptocurrency. Rogers generally does not begin with a slogan and search for numbers that support it. He builds the measurement system first.

A Bitcoin education

Bitcoin was Rogers' starting point.

Beginning in 2013, he spent years in the Bitcoin developer ecosystem. His involvement went beyond holding the asset. He built a Bitcoin wallet in Rust from scratch, submitted contributions to "rust-bitcoin", experimented with block-packing algorithms, and became familiar with the engineering compromises hidden beneath Bitcoin's apparently simple monetary proposition.

That distinction matters to his later Zcash thesis.

Rogers did not reject Bitcoin because he stopped understanding it. His argument was almost the reverse: the deeper he went into the problem, the less convinced he became that Bitcoin could simultaneously deliver global scale, strong financial privacy, and trustless self-custody without pushing some of those properties outside the base monetary system.

“Sold Bitcoin at $109,000 and bought Zcash at $220 and they called me retarded.” (~473 likes)
